player_safe.name: The Clover Co-op
player_safe.public_face: A cheerful Hush village mutual: shared ale, shared tools, shared stories, and a four-leaf clover painted where neighbors gather.
player_safe.short_description: Warm lamps, clover doors, shared bowls, and dry jokes make the Clover Co-op feel like Hush's stubborn heartbeat.
player_safe.long_description: The Clover Co-op is not impressive in a capital-city way. It is impressive in the way a table can hold ten people, then somehow hold twelve. Its doors are painted with uneven clovers, its benches remember every argument, and help arrives wrapped in a joke before anyone admits it is help.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The clover on the door is hand-painted and a little lopsided. Inside, lamps burn low and golden, a pot keeps itself warm, and three conversations pause just long enough to measure whether you are guests, trouble, or both.

player_safe.short: The social heart of Hush; shoes get polished and filled with trinkets.
player_safe.one_line: The social heart of Hush; shoes get polished and filled with trinkets.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Clover Co-op smells like tea, polished shoes, damp wool, and food made by people who count generosity carefully.
player_safe.long_body:
The Clover Co-op is alive like a kitchen during a storm: warm, crowded, useful, nosy, and full of small systems players can engage with.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Taproom: Mismatched tables, card games, and low voices make the main room social terrain. Counter shelves: Jars, tools, notes, and tabs show what the community trades. Back kitchen: Steam, knives, bread, and practical staff movement keep the place from freezing into exposition. Notice board: Handwritten local notices reveal village priorities.

Plants and materials: drying herbs, moss-honey combs, edible mushroom strings. Animals and background life: a tiny hearth-lizard stealing heat, market beetles under crates, moss hens near the back door. The air carries soup steam, card taps, jar clinks, floorboard gossip squeaks. Morning supplies, afternoon gossip, evening food, and late-night worry all pass through this room.

What people can get here: food, moss-honey, rumors, minor supplies, community introductions.
player_safe.known_for: Shoes come off at the door, and by the time you leave someone has tucked a little gift into them, a coin, a sweet, a folded note. Mismatched tables hold card games and lowered voices. Jars and tabs and handwritten notices crowd the shelves. Steam rolls out of the back kitchen where bread and knives keep a steady rhythm, and the floor squeaks in the exact spots everyone has learned to step around.
player_safe.culture_food: Soup is always going, thick with moss-greens and whatever the farms could spare. Moss-honey comes by the comb. Tea arrives without being ordered, in a cup that does not match its saucer. The bread is cut thick and handed over while it is still too hot to hold properly.
player_safe.travel_texture: You smell it before the door opens, soup and damp wool and polished leather. Inside the noise closes around you, cards and jars and gossip, and a chair gets nudged out with someone's foot before anyone bothers to say hello.

player_safe.name: Firstmoss Launch Festival
player_safe.short: Celebration of moss-ripened crops and spring abundance.
player_safe.one_line: Celebration of moss-ripened crops and spring abundance.
player_safe.read_aloud: Firstmoss is not a party break; it is Hush showing what the ward protects.
player_safe.long_body:
The banners are crooked, the stage wobbles, and the singing is terrible and beloved. The joy is real and just effortful enough to notice, the way a town laughs loudest on the day it most needs to.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Tiny stage: A wobbly platform holds speeches, music, and public nerves. Food line: Festival food tells players what the village grows and values. Moss lantern lane: Fresh green lanterns mark a beautiful path. Game corner: Children and adults compete in low-stakes games with very serious local rules.

Plants and materials: firstmoss lanterns, braided reed streamers, festival herbs, freshly cut moss crowns. Animals and background life: Festival Moths orbit green lanterns, Ratcoons hunt crumbs under benches, moss hens chase everything they can reach. The air carries laughter covering worry, green lantern glow, food steam, wet grass under dancing feet. The festival grows from setup to speeches to food to music; tension can enter at any stage without stopping the celebration.

What people can get here: festival food, small local crafts, public introductions, rumors softened by celebration.
player_safe.known_for: Everyone is wearing moss. Crowns of it, fresh-cut and still dripping, on heads of every age. A wobbly stage holds whoever was brave or bullied into singing, and the crowd loves them anyway. Children play a game with rules older than the ward and argue the calls with total seriousness. The banners are handmade and crooked, and so are the smiles.
player_safe.culture_food: The food line is the festival. Moss-honey cakes come off the pan still spitting fat. River fish blackens on reed fires. Someone keeps topping up a green cordial they swear is medicinal, and winks when they say it. You eat standing, with your fingers, and a stranger hands you bread shaped like a lantern before you learn their name.
player_safe.travel_texture: You smell it long before you see it, woodsmoke and frying honey and crushed grass under dancing feet. As you come in, the worry on the grown faces tucks itself behind a smile. Green lantern light catches everyone, and for one night even outsiders look like they belong.

player_safe.name: Hush Farms
player_safe.short: Glowing blue moss grows over fruits and vegetables.
player_safe.one_line: Glowing blue moss grows over fruits and vegetables.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Hush farms glow low under canopy-shadow, blue moss catching on tools, boots, and the undersides of leaves.
player_safe.long_body:
Hush Farms feels like real agricultural infrastructure: water levels, raised beds, moss rows, tools, storage, repair labor, and tiny creatures making honest work harder.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Raised moss rows: Green rows glow softly under low light. Water gate bank: Small gates control which fields drink. Tool sheds: Practical sheds show what people repair every day. Reed edge: The boundary between farm and wild wetland is alive.

Plants and materials: Sunless-Farm Moss, firstmoss, glowmoss, edible reeds, canal herbs, fungus ropes on shaded posts. Animals and background life: Ratcoons test every storage lid, Festival Moths gather when lanterns come out, silver minnows clean irrigation channels. The air carries water-level clicks, mud suction, lantern reflection, crop glow dimming when water is wrong. Water feeds moss, moss feeds people and insects, insects feed frogs and birds, and every gate adjustment changes the whole farm.

What people can get here: fresh food, farm tools, water-route directions.
player_safe.known_for: Blue moss glows low across the rows, catching on boot-soles and the undersides of leaves until the whole field hums faint and green. Raised beds run between channels of black water. Little gates click as someone decides which field drinks tonight. The tools lean exactly where hands will want them in the morning.
player_safe.culture_food: Everything here is half-grown under moss, pale roots and glowing greens pulled up dripping. Workers eat in the field, bread and cold fish and a flask of something green, standing between the rows. The first vegetable pressed into your hand is still cool from the water and tastes faintly of minerals and rain.
player_safe.travel_texture: The light drops and turns blue as you come under the canopy, and the ground goes soft and wet underfoot. Frogs cut off mid-click as you pass. Every few steps a gate clicks somewhere and a channel quietly changes its mind about where the water goes.

player_safe.name: The Hanging Office
player_safe.short: A treehouse-office counterweighted by a rune-marked boulder and full of forms, runes, plants, and magic.
player_safe.one_line: A treehouse-office counterweighted by a rune-marked boulder and full of forms, runes, plants, and magic.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Hanging Office creaks above the ground like a joke told by someone exhausted from surviving it.
player_safe.long_body:
The Hanging Office feels sacred and domestic, not just exposition: ropes creak, carved faces watch, tea cools, papers are pinned with thorns, and height makes every truth feel more delicate.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Root ladder approach: The climb makes trust physical. Porch platform: A suspended porch gives a view over forest layers. Cabin table: The central table holds work, tea, notes, and the package. Carved-face wall: Old protective faces mark the tree itself.

Plants and materials: bark faces, hanging moss, branch orchids, tea herbs in small pots. Animals and background life: moths in porch light, small branch birds nesting under eaves, quiet insects inside bark grooves. The air carries rope creak, height wind, warm cabin light, carved faces seeming to change expression. The home is maintained by small rituals: sweeping, rope checks, tea, ward listening, and watching the tree's mood.

What people can get here: Custodian answers if trust is present, high vantage, ward context.
player_safe.known_for: The whole office hangs off one great branch, balanced against a boulder carved with runes that someone clearly argues with daily. You climb a root ladder to reach it, and it answers every step with a creak. Papers are pinned to the walls with thorns. Carved faces in the old bark seem to follow the conversation. A teacup goes cold on the table because the work never quite stops.
player_safe.culture_food: Tea is the whole economy up here, brewed from porch herbs in chipped pots and pressed on every visitor whether they asked or not. There is honey if you have earned it. The biscuits are stale in a way the host will cheerfully deny. You drink it high above the forest floor and try not to look down.
player_safe.travel_texture: The climb makes trust physical, hand over hand up roots worn smooth by other nervous visitors. The platform sways just enough to remind you it is hanging. Wind comes up through the boards, the ropes complain, and the carved faces watch you decide whether to trust the floor.

keystone_profile.what: A master wardstone: a massive lion-faced stone sealed as corporate cargo and sent from Emeris toward Hush to renew failing protection there.
keystone_profile.wardstone: A wardstone is a carved stone node that projects protection, suppresses monster manifestation and wild-magic bleed, records crossings, and, in the GM-only layer, skims soul-signal when tied to Soulspire Solutions' network.
keystone_profile.source_gate: It was dispatched through Emeris's custody route. Emeris Capital Gate is a route threshold, not an empty socket.
keystone_profile.capital_city: Emeris is the local territory capital and one-shot start city. Athervast is the faraway grand capital and is not the Keystone's current table problem.
keystone_profile.custody: Emeris Crown Holdings holds the concession and custody paperwork; the crew receives the job together; Marlowe or a chosen replacement PC carries the package custody function; optional Sabine can handle S00-01 briefing questions; the Whitefire Custodian repairs it; the deeper ward stack profits from it.
keystone_profile.built_by: The current hardware is maintained through Mithril & Mortar fabrication and legacy Lumbax/Kazrak ward-craft, with independent keepers like the Whitefire Custodian preserving older methods.
keystone_profile.protects: It protects against monster manifestation, wild-magic bleed, frontier truth-bleed, and cascading ward failures.
keystone_profile.protects_against: Monster manifestation, wild-magic bleed, frontier truth-bleed, and cascading ward failures.
keystone_profile.ward_network: The Keystone participates in the Goldspire Ward Network under the Public-Private Ward Compact, linking wardstones, relay spires, billing rights, soul-signal power, and breach response.
keystone_profile.profit: Kazrak creates/monetizes danger; Mithril & Mortar builds/maintains ward infrastructure; Soulspire Solutions powers/skims it; The Grail guards/responds; Goldwater finances/insures; Emeris Crown Holdings holds the concession; RuneSpark Entertainment spins the story; Hexmart sells cheap consumer protection.
keystone_profile.value: Its practical value is community safety at Hush and the Open Vale lines. Its market value is obscene because outer protection can be turned into revenue, response contracts, and soul-signal leverage.
keystone_profile.damage: Cracks can destabilize a ward, vent old fear, summon audit pressure, or let the stone answer questions in a voice no one admits hearing.
keystone_profile.magic_nearby: Minor magic makes it hum, reflect false stars, or taste of copper. Strong spellcasting near it should call for a DC 15-20 check or tick the ward countdown.
keystone_profile.communities_notice: Community-rooted PCs notice who gets protected first, who is asked to wait, and which local names vanish under corporate labels.

player_safe.name: Open Vale™ Ritual Site
player_safe.short: An ancient circular clearing of standing stones and ward-light, with a freshly painted company marker staked at its edge.
player_safe.one_line: An ancient circular clearing of standing stones and ward-light, with a freshly painted company marker staked at its edge.
player_safe.read_aloud: Open Vale is older than its branded marker: a circular clearing where stone, moss, and ward-light remember protection before paperwork.
player_safe.long_body:
A beautiful clearing with real ground to use, stone for cover, open lanes for sightlines, ward-lines underfoot, and a center worth standing in front of. Pressure can come from every direction at once.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Ritual center: The protected middle holds the Custodian's work. Standing stone ring: Old stones create cover, lanes, and sacred weight. Flowered approach lanes: Open grass paths show where threats can arrive. Ward-line spokes: Glowing lines connect center to surrounding stones.

Plants and materials: Sunfire Lily, flowered ward grasses, low healing herbs, moss at stone bases, wind-bent seed heads. Animals and background life: Ward-Moths trace the ward lines, Mist-Things gather at the edge of low fog, field crickets go silent near ward pulses. The air carries ward light, pressure changes, petal movement against the wind, countdown rhythm. The clearing breathes with the ritual: light gathers, pressure rises, life pulls back, then returns if the ward stabilizes.
player_safe.known_for: A perfectly circular clearing older than the painted Open Vale marker staked at its edge. Standing stones ring a center where moss and ward-light still gather. Flowered grass paths run in from every direction. Lines of light spoke out from the middle to the stones, and the company sign looks very small and very recent against all of it.
player_safe.culture_food: No market, no stalls, just the clearing and whatever people bring. Offerings of bread and flowers rest at the bases of the stones. Whoever keeps the ritual shares a little honeyed water, blessed mostly by intention.
player_safe.travel_texture: You smell crushed grass and cold stone before you understand where you are standing. The air pulls taut as the ward-light gathers. Petals drift against the wind, the field crickets cut out, and a slow countdown rhythm settles into your chest whether you want it there or not.

block2.personality: A predator made of policy, hunting where debt, ward-failure, and fear overlap. The original person wanted release from a debt that taught them to collect others, and that single unpaid wanting is the only crack in the ledger.
voice: Please state the value of what you refuse to lose.
Unfiled grief accrues.
Protection without invoice is an irregularity.
block2.secrets: The wraith was once a debtor before it became an instrument.
block2.fears: Freely given protection and memories that refuse a price.

likes_dislikes.likes: Filed grief, named liabilities, and hesitation.

block2.day_to_day: Drifts where debt, ward failure, and fear overlap, listening for memories loose enough to seize.

block2.animal_companion: No animal; loose pages and blue flame orbit like carrion birds.

player_safe.name: Relay Spire
player_safe.short: A slim, windswept relay tower with a beacon at the top that has lately begun to burn thin.
player_safe.one_line: A slim, windswept relay tower with a beacon at the top that has lately begun to burn thin.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Relay Spire is distant enough to be a future problem and bright enough that nobody can pretend it is unrelated.
player_safe.long_body:
The Relay Spire is the Relay distilled into a vertical problem: too much wind, too many stairs, not enough certainty.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Base room: Coils of rope, spare flags, and boots make the tower human. Outer stairs: Windy stairs make movement dramatic. Beacon top: The top holds light, danger, and horizon.

Plants and materials: ridge lichen, wind grass, tiny flowers pressed into cracks. Animals and background life: courier birds, cliff insects, small nesting things in the eaves. The air carries wind shear, beacon hum, rope clatter, horizon haze. The tower measures time by beacon checks and bird arrivals.

What people can get here: relay access, high vantage.
player_safe.known_for: A slim tower that exists to be high and bright. The base room is all coiled rope, spare flags, and worn-out boots. The outer stair winds up into hard wind. At the top a beacon burns, and lately it burns a little thin, the kind of detail nobody mentions and everybody has noticed.
player_safe.culture_food: Whoever keeps the beacon lives on what they can haul up, hard rations, a thermos of something hot, courier-bird eggs when the nests are generous. They share a cup at the top and watch the horizon over the rim of it.
player_safe.travel_texture: The wind shears harder with every turn of the stair. The beacon hums in your back teeth. Rope clatters against stone, and the horizon hazes off in every direction until the world feels very large and the tower feels very thin.

visual_assets.style_anchor: Bright comedic frontier high-fantasy concept art for a Daggerheart-adjacent tabletop RPG. Medieval/Renaissance fantasy technology only: hand tools, wagons, ropes, parchment notices, ward-stones, carved wood, brass, cloth, stone, moss, lanterns, and magic. player_safe.long_description: Emeris Crown™ is respectability for hire: cream-and-gold coaches, a crowned-lion seal pressed in honest-looking wax, a contract so polite it apologizes while shifting the liability onto you. player_safe.name: Goldspire Territories
player_safe.short: A vast bright frontier-fantasy territory of walled cities, giant forests, wet villages, relay towers, old roads, and cheerful safety promises that never quite cover the cracks.
player_safe.one_line: A vast bright frontier-fantasy territory of walled cities, giant forests, wet villages, relay towers, old roads, and cheerful safety promises that never quite cover the cracks.
player_safe.read_aloud: Goldspire is not one city. It is a huge territory of paved capitals, painted forest roads, mossy villages, quarry towns, river markets, ridge relays, and old magic under newer paperwork.
player_safe.long_body:
Goldspire Territories stretches so wide that no single horizon can explain it. One road may run through honey-stone city gates and festival stalls; another sinks into forest soil beneath trees as wide as houses; another follows canals past moss farms, wet porches, and lanterns reflected in black water. The place is bright, loud, green, gold, and overconfident.

Its cities sell safety as if safety were weather. Its villages know better. Couriers, guides, clerks, farmers, relay keepers, potion workers, and market cooks all keep the region moving while larger powers turn danger into schedules, fees, and stamped reassurances. The territory should feel like a living world, not a backdrop: food smells different by road, animals react before officials do, and every local custom knows something the paperwork forgot.
player_safe.known_for: Gigantic forests, courier roads, territory capitals, branded protection, moss villages, bright markets, relay towers, and older magic that refuses to become a product.
player_safe.culture_food: Road food changes by region: fried gate dough in Emeris, moss-honey bread in Hush, hot quarry stews, bright market skewers, strong forest tonics, and suspiciously cheerful packaged remedies from city manufactories.
player_safe.travel_texture: Travel in Goldspire is a sequence of thresholds: city gate to forest road, forest road to wet village, village path to sacred meadow, ridge trail to relay tower. Each threshold changes the smell, the sound, and who feels in charge.

visible_details: Corporate waymarkers sit on old trail bones.
The road looks maintained until roots, moss, and animal silence contradict it.
subtle_details: Some signs are fresh paint over older local marks.
The forest quiets in waves, as if attention is moving ahead of the party.

sensory_stack.detail: Sap under varnish, rain caught in bark furrows, wet canvas, and the metallic tang of route fixtures.
Tree bark feels ridged like old stone; the road mud clings with fine pale grit.

block2.read_aloud: Goldspire is not one city. It is a huge territory of paved capitals, painted forest roads, mossy villages, quarry towns, river markets, ridge relays, and old magic under newer paperwork.
block2.long_body:
Goldspire Territories stretches so wide that no single horizon can explain it. One road may run through honey-stone city gates and festival stalls; another sinks into forest soil beneath trees as wide as houses; another follows canals past moss farms, wet porches, and lanterns reflected in black water. The place is bright, loud, green, gold, and overconfident.

Its cities sell safety as if safety were weather. Its villages know better. Couriers, guides, clerks, farmers, relay keepers, potion workers, and market cooks all keep the region moving while larger powers turn danger into schedules, fees, and stamped reassurances. The territory should feel like a living world, not a backdrop: food smells different by road, animals react before officials do, and every local custom knows something the paperwork forgot.
block2.known_for: Gigantic forests, courier roads, territory capitals, branded protection, moss villages, bright markets, relay towers, and older magic that refuses to become a product.
block2.culture_food: Road food changes by region: fried gate dough in Emeris, moss-honey bread in Hush, hot quarry stews, bright market skewers, strong forest tonics, and suspiciously cheerful packaged remedies from city manufactories.
block2.travel_texture: Travel in Goldspire is a sequence of thresholds: city gate to forest road, forest road to wet village, village path to sacred meadow, ridge trail to relay tower. Each threshold changes the smell, the sound, and who feels in charge.

player_safe.name: Kazrak Industries
player_safe.public_face: Adventure, certification, glory, and dungeon work pitched like a chance to become legendary.
player_safe.short_description: Kazrak Industries™ sells adventure itself: certifications, hero ratings, and the chance to die famous.
player_safe.long_description: Kazrak™ recruiting tents are pure hype: banners of grinning certified heroes, a barker bellowing about Glory Tier™ benefits, a try-before-you-die Sample Dungeon™ rated 'Tier 0, mostly survivable!' You can buy a Legend License™, a Hazard Heritage™ commemorative coin, and an upgrade to Premium Casualty Coverage™ that pays your next of kin in Kazrak store credit. The recruiter shakes your hand with both of his and calls you 'future legend' so many times it starts to sound like a verdict. The fine print rates your life by Content Value™: the more dangerously you die, the more your story is worth, to them.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: A Kazrak poster shows a smiling hero standing on a pile of treasure no worker could lift alone. The paint is flaking at the edges, but the grin remains perfect.

player_safe.short_description: Kazrak Industries™ sells adventure itself: certifications, hero ratings, and the chance to die famous.
player_safe.long_description: Kazrak™ recruiting tents are pure hype: banners of grinning certified heroes, a barker bellowing about Glory Tier™ benefits, a try-before-you-die Sample Dungeon™ rated 'Tier 0, mostly survivable!' You can buy a Legend License™, a Hazard Heritage™ commemorative coin, and an upgrade to Premium Casualty Coverage™ that pays your next of kin in Kazrak store credit. The fine print rates your life by Content Value™: the more dangerously you die, the more your story is worth, to them.

player_safe.name: Hexmart
player_safe.public_face: Cheap charms, potions, and Pocket Wards for every frontier harm.
player_safe.slogan: Hexmart™: a charm for every harm!
player_safe.short_description: Hexmart™ is a discount-magic supercenter where every fear has a matching trinket and nothing is built to outlast the receipt.
player_safe.long_description: The Hexmart™ stall hits you like a fairground: baskets of blue charms, singing price tags that harmonize when you lift one, a wall of Pocket Ward™ Minis stamped 'Now 12% More Warded!' The greeter presses a free Sample Charm™ into your palm before you have said a word. Shelves are sorted by feeling, not function: a SCARED aisle, a LONELY aisle, a JUST-IN-CASE aisle that is somehow the biggest. The packaging promises 'protection, or your memory of protection back.' Read the foil sticker and the warranty expires the moment you need it, which is, of course, the moment you bought it for.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The Hexmart display is a riot of painted tags, glittering string, tiny bottled glows, and charms sorted by fear: wolves, rain, debt, curses, unfortunate relatives. One basket is marked 'road-safe-ish.'

player_safe.name: Mithril & Mortar
player_safe.public_face: Master builders and ward-smiths selling durable infrastructure and respectable craft.
player_safe.slogan: Mithril & Mortar™: we built the world you owe for.
player_safe.short_description: Mithril & Mortar™ builds the road, the bridge, the ward, and the thing that makes the bridge need replacing.
player_safe.long_description: The M&M™ showroom is a cathedral of competence: sample walls, gleaming ward-bricks, a model village that lights up to show 'protected zones,' and an aproned clerk who quotes load-bearing runes from memory. Buy a DuraWard™ foundation stone, a Lifetime* Mortar tub (*lifetime of the mortar, not yours), or finance a whole bridge through the Build Now, Owe Forever™ plan. The catalog is genuinely beautiful. player_safe.table_read_aloud: The old mark is half-worn but still proud: hammer, trowel, and a wardline cut so clean the stone seems to remember the blow.

block1.name: Mithril & Mortar

block2.internal_tensions: True believers and tired workers keep the public promise alive while managers monetize the gap between promise and harm.
block2.current_moves: Auditing old wardwork while modern divisions quietly profit from what is allowed to crack.
block2.history_hook: Institutional beliefs: The Beautiful Collapse; Debt as Foundation Material; The Trap Division Merger.

rivals: Other brands in staged public competition
block3.who_they_prey_on: Villages that need a wall, a bridge, or a ward and will sign a generational debt to get one that lasts exactly as long as the payments.

player_safe.name: Soulspire Solutions
player_safe.public_face: Comforting soul insurance and afterlife services sold as peace of mind.
player_safe.slogan: Soulspire™: rest easy, we'll handle the rest.
player_safe.short_description: Soulspire Solutions™ sells peace of mind now and, once the debt outlives you, repossesses the soul that had it.
player_safe.long_description: Everything about Soulspire™ is soothing on purpose: lavender light, a hushed lobby, a counselor in soft grey who calls death a 'transition event' and your grief a 'coverage gap.' Brochures for the Eternal Comfort Plan™ show smiling families and a tasteful urn; the waiting-room hymn loops a wellness ballad about rest. Sign the Afterlife Assurance™ and you will feel genuinely better, which is the point, because page forty-seven of the same friendly packet is where a person legally stops being one and becomes, in their cheerful internal term, a 'continuing contributor.' The undead on the night roads are not monsters. They are accounts in good standing.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: A Soulspire pamphlet folds open like a condolence card. The ink is blue-black, the border is tasteful, and the little painted candle at the top has been rendered with more care than most people get in the ledger.

Brochures for the Eternal Comfort Plan™ show smiling families and a tasteful urn; the waiting-room hymn loops a wellness ballad about rest. Sign the Afterlife Assurance™ and you will feel genuinely better, which is the point, because page forty-seven of the same friendly packet is where a person legally stops being one and becomes, in their cheerful internal term, a 'continuing contributor.' The undead on the night roads are not monsters. They are accounts in good standing.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: A Soulspire pamphlet folds open like a condolence card. The ink is blue-black, the border is tasteful, and the little painted candle at the top has been rendered with more care than most people get in the ledger.

player_safe.short_description: RuneSpark Entertainment™ decides which version of what happened is the one everyone remembers.
player_safe.long_description: RuneSpark™ is everywhere and feels like fun: a town crier in spangled livery, a sponsored ballad you cannot stop humming, drifting sky-illusions advertising the next heroic serial. Buy a souvenir broadsheet, a collectible Hero Trading Charm™, a front-row witch-light ticket to a 'true story' that is at least forty percent true. Their stagecoach studio will interview you about the road attack and air a brighter version by morning, where the dead are 'unfortunate,' the danger is 'thrilling,' and the sponsor's ward is the hero. They do not lie, exactly. They edit. And the edit is the history.

player_safe.short: An ancient forest logistics preserve where colossal trees, hybrid fauna, underroot communities, route tolls, and corporate liability language all compete to define what safety means.
player_safe.one_line: An ancient forest logistics preserve where colossal trees, hybrid fauna, underroot communities, route tolls, and corporate liability language all compete to define what safety means.
player_safe.read_aloud: Sablewood is an ancient forest forced to wear a logistics badge: colossal trunks, liability signs, toll language, and living routes that do not care about forms.
player_safe.long_body:
Sablewood is a national-forest-scale wilderness wearing a branded vest it did not ask for. The trees are huge enough to drive wagons through hollow roots; the road is an agreement, not a conquest.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Managed carriage road: A wet road threads between trunks the size of small houses. Root underpasses: Hollow roots create side tunnels, animal shade, and places a cart cannot follow. Waymarker clearings: Cheerful route markers and supply posts look tiny against the forest. Canopy shadow lanes: The light changes suddenly under massive branches. Wild seep hollows: Water gathers in mossy dips full of tracks, eggs, insects, and old leaves.

Plants and materials: car-wide sable trunks with roots that rise like stair rails and force roads to negotiate around them, ledgerleaf vines whose flat leaves curl shut when touched, as if refusing unofficial inspection, blue-green moss mats that remember footsteps for a few minutes before springing back, larkmoth orchids that bloom only where insects have been loud for several days. Animals and background life: Cat-Squirrels leap limb to limb and knock dew from leaves, Giraffe-Deer step over the road as if wagons are very short problems, Lemur-Toads gossip-click from rain hollows and go silent when large predators pass, Fox-Bats sleep under route signs and steal shiny route tokens at dusk. The air carries root creaks like distant doors, warm rain pockets, lantern-light attracts lark-moths, ward markers sometimes hum out of tune. Rain feeds moss, moss feeds insects, insects feed hybrid birds and bats, and larger predators read the road by who goes quiet first.

What people can get here: route caches, waymarker supply hooks, field toll posts.
player_safe.known_for: The trees go up until the sky closes over, and the light that reaches the road is green and always moving. A vest-badge nailed to a trunk reads Sablewood Logistics Preserve, and a hundred yards on the same kind of trunk has swallowed an older sign whole. Route-stones stand painted and numbered in cheerful colors. Every warning on them turns out, eventually, to be true.
player_safe.culture_food: Trade here moves in waxed parcels and field rations, hard bread, smoked strips, larkmoth honey scraped out of orchid hollows. A toll-post sells the same dried fruit it confiscated that morning. Lemur-toads watch you eat and go silent the instant something large shifts in the dark.
player_safe.travel_texture: The road runs sunk into dark earth worn soft by a century of cart-wheels, so the forest rises on both sides like walls. Warm rain pockets drift through with no cloud in sight. A thousand leaves rustle at once and then stop, and you catch yourself counting the silence.

player_safe.name: Old Sable
player_safe.short: The living old forest beneath the brand.
player_safe.one_line: The living old forest beneath the brand.
player_safe.read_aloud: Old Sable is the forest underneath the brand, too old to argue and too alive to be reduced to route language.
player_safe.long_body:
Old Sable is Sablewood without the managerial mask: slower, darker, wetter, and old enough that a humanoid road feels like a recent suggestion.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Cathedral trunks: The trunks rise like towers, each with roots big enough to hide a table. Animal courts: Clearings are shaped by repeated animal use rather than tools. Old road bones: Stone, plank, and sign fragments show where older routes failed. Green hush pockets: Sound drops away under thick leaves.

Plants and materials: car-wide sable trunks with roots that rise like stair rails and force roads to negotiate around them, ledgerleaf vines whose flat leaves curl shut when touched, as if refusing unofficial inspection, blue-green moss mats that remember footsteps for a few minutes before springing back, larkmoth orchids that bloom only where insects have been loud for several days. Animals and background life: Cat-Squirrels leap limb to limb and knock dew from leaves, Giraffe-Deer step over the road as if wagons are very short problems, Lemur-Toads gossip-click from rain hollows and go silent when large predators pass, Fox-Bats sleep under route signs and steal shiny route tokens at dusk. The air carries leaf-shadow flicker, root groan, sudden warm mist, old ward stones swallowed by bark. Old Sable digests everything: signs, roads, bones, secrets, and dropped tools all become part of the forest floor.
player_safe.known_for: No badges out here, no paint. The trunks rise like the pillars of a drowned cathedral, each root big enough to hide a table under. Clearings are shaped by animals walking the same lines for centuries. Now and then a stone or a plank or a corporate sign pokes up through the moss, half-eaten by the floor.
player_safe.culture_food: There is nothing to buy and no one selling. What you eat you carried in or foraged, and the locals who know which mushrooms are kind will share if they like you. The water tastes of cold stone and old leaves.
player_safe.travel_texture: Sound drops away under the thick leaves until you can hear your own pulse. Warm mist comes and goes with no weather to explain it. The light flickers green as the canopy shifts, and old ward-stones sit swallowed in bark, still humming faintly to no one at all.

player_safe.name: Sablewood Route Gate
player_safe.short: The road crossing where nature, signage, and corporate language first collide.
player_safe.one_line: The road crossing where nature, signage, and corporate language first collide.
player_safe.read_aloud: The route gate is where polished assurance meets wet bark, old stone, and a forest that has not signed anything.
player_safe.long_body:
The route gate is bureaucracy wedged between trees: a tiny official station trying to impose straight lines on a forest that only understands curves.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Queue lane: Wagons line up between rope posts and roots. Stamp shed: A cramped shed holds ledgers, lanterns, and a desk built around a branch. Bypass deer path: A narrow animal trail skirts the official lane. Inspection stump: A huge cut stump has become the inspection counter.

Plants and materials: roots buckle the queue stones, moss softens every official post, vines steal loose paper overnight. Animals and background life: fox-bats nest above the stamp shed, small root mice chew wax seals, lark-moths orbit lanterns during delays. The air carries stamp echo, rope creak, wet paper smell, ward-marker buzz. The gate opens, jams, stamps, argues, and gets quietly undermined by roots every day.

What people can get here: route stamps, minor repairs, cheap food stall, questionable ward-token seller.
player_safe.known_for: A tiny official station tries to draw straight lines across a forest that only does curves. Roots have buckled the queue-stones into a slow stone wave. Vines steal loose paper off the desk overnight. The inspection counter is a cut stump the size of a wagon, and the stamp comes down with a sound the whole clearing has learned to dread.
player_safe.culture_food: A cheap stall fries dough in forest fat while you wait, and a man with a confident smile sells ward-tokens of deeply uncertain power. The coffee is bitter and free if you look official enough to be worth the favor.
player_safe.travel_texture: You join the queue between rope posts and roots, wagons creaking ahead of you. Stamp-echo, rope-creak, the wet-paper smell of a hundred soggy forms. A narrow deer-path slips off to the side, unstamped and untaxed, and everyone pretends very hard not to see it.

player_safe.name: Old Sable Canopy Road
player_safe.short: The living road beneath the branded logistics layer, remembered by locals as a place instead of a service corridor.
player_safe.one_line: The living road beneath the branded logistics layer, remembered by locals as a place instead of a service corridor.
player_safe.read_aloud: The canopy road feels like travel through the forest's memory: dim green light, root-shadow bends, and old markers half-swallowed by moss.
player_safe.long_body:
The canopy road feels like walking through a ship rigged into living trees: planks, ropes, pulley baskets, sudden views, and drops that make every joke a little sharper.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Branch platform: Wide wooden landings wrap around living trunks. Rope bridge run: Suspended bridges sway between massive branches. Cargo pulley lane: Crates and baskets pass overhead or underfoot. Canopy nest edge: Wildlife has claimed parts of the structure.

Plants and materials: air moss, branch orchids, rope-gripping vines, bark shelves with tiny rain pools. Animals and background life: fox-bats hang under platforms, lark-moths cluster around pulley lanterns, canopy squirrels hoard route tags. The air carries wind sway, rope groan, green drop-light, distant road noise below. The canopy moves with wind and weight; safe paths are maintained by constant small repairs.

What people can get here: canopy repairs, rope ferries, packed trail food.
player_safe.known_for: The road here leaves the ground entirely. Plank landings wrap the great trunks, rope bridges sway between branches, and crates ride overhead on squealing pulleys. Wildlife has moved into the structure, so half the handholds are also somebody's nest. The whole thing shifts with the wind and with your weight.
player_safe.culture_food: Trail food gets hauled up in baskets packed tight to survive the swing, dried fruit, hard cheese, flatbread gone slightly stale. You eat it sitting on a platform with your boots hanging out over a long green drop.
player_safe.travel_texture: Every step is a small negotiation with the rope and the wind. The bridges groan and give under you. Green light drops through gaps in the leaves, and far below you can still hear the managed road going about its day without you.

player_safe.name: Hush Safe Irrigation Path
player_safe.short: A narrow working path through mosslit water channels that rewards trust built in Hush.
player_safe.one_line: A narrow working path through mosslit water channels that rewards trust built in Hush.
player_safe.read_aloud: The safe irrigation path is narrow, useful, and trusted: mosslit water, low bridges, and farm markers that only make sense if someone explained them.
player_safe.long_body:
The path is safe only because somebody walks it every morning and fixes whatever the water loosened overnight. It is narrow, slick, and known by heart to people who have never once drawn it on a map.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Raised plank run: A narrow path keeps boots above black water. Water-gate switchback: Several small gates divide channels. Reed blind: Tall reeds hide both wildlife and watchers.

Plants and materials: slick moss on planks, tall reeds, water herbs, tiny white canal flowers. Animals and background life: Ratcoons move under the planks, Festival Moths cluster by lantern bends, small fish flash in gate shadows. The air carries board creak, water gulp, gnat hum, distant co-op noise. The path is checked daily; missed maintenance turns safety into hazard.

What people can get here: safe route guidance, water-control knowledge.
player_safe.known_for: A single plank run threads above black water, slick with moss and just wide enough for one. Small gates split the channels off toward the farms. Tall reeds close over your shoulders, hiding whatever is watching from the next bend. Someone has notched the posts with marks that only make sense if a local explains them.
player_safe.culture_food: There is no food out here, only the path and the work. A passing farmer might share a heel of bread and a warning about which plank gives. The water smells green and mineral, and the only sweetness is the moss-honey someone always seems to have tucked in a pocket.
player_safe.travel_texture: Your boots find the planks by feel while the moss does its best to slide you off. Frogs gulp and go quiet under the boards. The reeds muffle the world down to water-sound and the far-off noise of the co-op, and you understand this path is only safe because someone walks it every single day.

player_safe.name: Open Vale Ward Lines
player_safe.short: Lines of stone, moss, and old light that show the ward is infrastructure, memory, and place at once.
player_safe.one_line: Lines of stone, moss, and old light that show the ward is infrastructure, memory, and place at once.
player_safe.read_aloud: The ward lines are not decoration; they are infrastructure made visible as grooves, mosslight, dust, and old promises.
player_safe.long_body:
The ward lines are magic behaving like public infrastructure: beautiful, temperamental, practical, and old enough that maintenance feels like ritual.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Bright junction: Several lines meet and pulse under the ground. Dim gap: A weak stretch makes the whole system feel vulnerable. Stone service marker: Old stones mark where people once tended the line.

Plants and materials: Sunfire Lily, grass grows brighter along stable lines, flowers bend away from unstable gaps, moss thickens around service stones. Animals and background life: Ward-Moths cluster at warm junctions, Mist-Things avoid stable lines and drift near flickering gaps. The air carries line hum, static hair, glowing dew, pressure behind the eyes. Healthy lines invite life; unstable lines create quiet strips animals avoid.
player_safe.known_for: Grooves run through the grass filled with old mosslight, pulsing faintly underfoot like buried veins. Where the lines are strong the grass grows greener. Where they gap, the flowers lean away and a quiet strip opens that the insects refuse to cross. Worn service stones mark where people once knelt to tend it.
player_safe.culture_food: Nobody eats here on purpose. This is a place you tend, not a place you feast. If anything, someone leaves a small offering at a service stone, a heel of bread, a smear of honey, for luck or for habit.
player_safe.travel_texture: The hair on your arms lifts as you cross a strong line. Dew glows where the light pools under the grass. A pressure sits behind your eyes near the bright junctions, and a held-breath wrongness in the gaps that makes you walk a little faster without deciding to.

player_safe.name: The Grail
player_safe.public_face: Holy-road protection with knightly livery, righteous language, and contracts that sound like sacraments.
player_safe.short_description: The Grail™ sells salvation-shaped security: holy escorts, blessed wards, and protection from threats it has no interest in ending.
player_safe.long_description: The Grail™ arrives like a sermon: knights in spotless white-and-gold, a contract written like a sacrament, a choir-sweet recruiter who calls the toll a tithe and the fee a sacrifice. Buy a Blessing of Safe Passage™, a consecrated Ward of the Worthy™, an indulgence-style Pre-Forgiveness Plan™ for whatever the escort has to do to 'protect' you. They are genuinely brave and genuinely armed, and they will defend you beautifully against dangers that, conveniently, never quite get solved, because a solved threat is a closed account. To be judged worthy by The Grail is to be judged able to pay.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: A Grail sigil gleams from a white-and-gold shoulder plate. The escort's hand rests near the sword, but the voice stays gentle enough for a chapel. Somehow that makes the sword louder.

player_safe.short_description: The Grail™ sells salvation-shaped security: holy escorts, blessed wards, and protection from threats it has no interest in ending.
player_safe.long_description: The Grail™ arrives like a sermon: knights in spotless white-and-gold, a contract written like a sacrament, a choir-sweet recruiter who calls the toll a tithe and the fee a sacrifice. Buy a Blessing of Safe Passage™, a consecrated Ward of the Worthy™, an indulgence-style Pre-Forgiveness Plan™ for whatever the escort has to do to 'protect' you. They are genuinely brave and genuinely armed, and they will defend you beautifully against dangers that, conveniently, never quite get solved, because a solved threat is a closed account. To be judged worthy by The Grail is to be judged able to pay.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: A Grail sigil gleams from a white-and-gold shoulder plate. The escort's hand rests near the sword, but the voice stays gentle enough for a chapel. Somehow that makes the sword louder.

sensory_palette: White-and-gold livery, grail-and-sword heraldry, incense, illuminated contracts, stained-glass color, and a haloed knight mascot with an open palm.

the unseen professional behind Tamsin's wound remains an implication, not a confirmed NPC

Goldwater can turn protection into debt.
Bramble Union becomes useful as a public enemy when roads need a villain.

player_safe.name: Goldwater Financial Institution
player_safe.public_face: A trusted bank with portable vaults, gold-black seals, and road-safety financing.
player_safe.short_description: Goldwater Financial™ keeps your valuables safe and your debt safer, because the debt is the valuable.
player_safe.long_description: Goldwater™ branches gleam with trust: portable vaults on polished carts, gold-black seals, a teller who calls you 'a valued risk' like it is a compliment. Open a Roadworthy Account™, add a Ward-Continuity Rider™, finance your own safety with a Fear-Forward Loan™ ('low payments, high peace of mind'). The clerk is warm and the math is warmer: every product quietly assumes something terrible will happen to you, and prices the assumption in. Miss three payments and your friendly account is escalated, in a sealed grey envelope, to a partner that handles 'continuing contributors.' The bank never threatens. It simply compounds.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The Goldwater seal is heavy enough to feel expensive from across the room. An agent smooths a ledger page with two fingers and says the word 'safe' like it has a price already attached.

player_safe.name: Zephra Exchange
player_safe.public_face: A market and toll-house brand that promises orderly crossing, registered cargo, and trade access.
player_safe.slogan: Zephra™: the price of everything, the value of you.
player_safe.short_description: Zephra Exchange™ runs the market, the toll, and the stamp that decides whether your movement counts as legal.
player_safe.long_description: The Zephra™ tollhouse is bureaucratic theater: brass scales, a queue rope, a clerk stamping Movement Legitimacy™ certificates under a banner reading FREE TRADE in expensive gold leaf. Register your cargo, buy a Crossing Credit™, upgrade to a Priority Passage™ pass that lets you skip the line you are also paying to maintain. Prices float by the hour on a big chalk board nobody can quite read. They did not build the river or the road. They built the gate, the fee, and the cheerful word for the fee, which is 'civilization,' and they will sell you a pamphlet explaining why the toll is freedom.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The Zephra stamp lands with a delicate click. The clerk does not raise their voice. They do not need to. The road, apparently, has standards.

player_safe.name: Goldspire Logistics
player_safe.public_face: A forgettable freight-coordination concern with plain grey seals and paperwork nobody remembers seeing twice.
player_safe.short_description: A dull freight mark, a grey seal, and a name too boring to remember keep Goldspire Logistics nearly invisible.
player_safe.long_description: Goldspire Logistics does not look powerful. That is the trick of it. A grey seal appears on crate corners, approval slips, and route papers, always in the same modest ink, always small enough to miss if you are looking for a villain with a banner.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The mark is almost nothing: grey ink, a square crate, a practical little stamp in the corner. It has the confidence of something that does not need to advertise.

block1.name: Goldspire Logistics
block1.public_face: A forgettable freight-coordination concern with plain grey seals and paperwork nobody remembers seeing twice.
block1.what_they_really_do: GM-only: coordinates the staged competition, manages scarcity, and turns danger and protection into the same product line.
block1.place_in_story: Never on stage. It is the unseen pressure behind contracts, routes, prices, and impossible paperwork.
block1.disposition_to_pcs: Does not know the PCs exist yet, which is part of the horror.
block1.the_lever: No lever in this one-shot. The party can only begin to glimpse a pattern.

block2.standing: Total and invisible, like a stage manager for a play the audience thinks is real.
block2.what_they_control: Brands, prices, road dangers, protection products, custody paperwork, and the illusion of choice.
block2.how_they_operate: Shells, subsidiaries, coordinated competition, dull names, and slogans that make every other brand seem separate.
block2.internal_tensions: The owned brands jockey for favor; that friction is a future crack, not a one-shot reveal.
block2.current_moves: Rebalancing which roads are dangerous this season to keep protection demand healthy.
block2.history_hook: The moment competing concerns quietly merged behind a bland name and discovered coordinated scarcity outperformed real competition.

block3.who_they_prey_on: Everyone, framed as serving everyone.

block4.aesthetic: Grey seals, plain crates, forgettable ink, and the only brand that does not need to shout.
voice: It never speaks directly. It speaks through everyone else's slogans.
block4.logo_hook: A plain freight-crate sigil that hides every other mark in miniature.
block4.theme_song_hook: Silence, or polite office music nobody admits hearing. Seed only.

block5.relevance_to_players: The answer to who really benefits, but not a fact handed to the table in this one-shot.
block5.relevance_to_world: The hidden operating system of the Goldspire Territories.
block5.secrets: GM-only: the manufactured-peril thesis lives here. Never say the conclusion for the players.
block5.hidden_ties: GM-only deepest layer: every corporate faction routes upward into this bland center.

progressive_disclosure.content: Invisible. Players only feel that something is off.
A recurring dull name appears on too many documents.
Future-campaign seam: the Board itself. Not reachable as confirmed truth in this one-shot.

earn_it_hooks: Let a sharp party collect the shape: repeated seals, impossible approval chains, and missing signers.
Never confirm the conclusion in the GM's mouth; let players name the pattern themselves later.

player_safe.short_description: A dull freight mark, a grey seal, and a name too boring to remember keep Goldspire Logistics nearly invisible.
player_safe.long_description: Goldspire Logistics does not look powerful. That is the trick of it. A grey seal appears on crate corners, approval slips, and route papers, always in the same modest ink, always small enough to miss if you are looking for a villain with a banner.
player_safe.table_read_aloud: The mark is almost nothing: grey ink, a square crate, a practical little stamp in the corner. It has the confidence of something that does not need to advertise.

sensory_palette: plain grey ink, old crate dust, dry ledgers, unmarked doors, identical stamps, and the smell of paper nobody wants to explain
a name that turns up too often precisely because nobody remembers it
silence where a slogan should be
operating_places: unmarked freight paperwork across the Goldspire Territories
background offices in Emeris and Athervast, visible only as repeated seals and paperwork echoes
the corners of contracts, crate ledgers, and route approvals rather than a public storefront
npc_roster: No public face in the one-shot. Let every visible person belong to a different brand.
Any future director or clerk should be a Kyle confirmation, not an invented reveal.
interconnections: Emeris, Goldwater, Soulspire, Kazrak, Hexmart, The Grail, Zephra, Mithril & Mortar, Artemis, and RuneSpark all create useful pressure around the same territory.
The Midnight Cabal and Umbrand Consortium remain uncertain shadows, not confirmed arms of the company.
reveal_cues: Surface: the hidden layer stays invisible unless players notice repeated paperwork.
Hint: let the same dull mark recur on unrelated documents.
Earned: the players get enough pattern to name the conclusion in their own words.
table_scripts: If players notice the mark: "It is not ornate. It is the kind of stamp you forget unless it appears somewhere it should not."
If they chase the pattern early: "You have enough to feel the shape of something organized, not enough to name the hand."

player_safe.name: Emeris Capital Gate
player_safe.short: A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond.
player_safe.one_line: A great arch of pale carved stone three wagons wide, with toll-counters clacking beneath it and the green dark of Sablewood waiting beyond.
player_safe.read_aloud: A great arch of pale carved stone rises three wagons wide, its keystone leafed in gold and its faces worn smooth by a century of carved caravans setting out. Beneath it runs a permanent little fair: toll-counters clacking, a crier calling the morning rates, a stall hawking painted gate-charms, and the smell of fried dough and hot sealing-wax.
player_safe.long_body:
The Emeris Capital Gate is the city showing off the threshold of the wild. Pale carved stone rises three wagons wide, its keystone leafed in gold, its surfaces worn smooth by a century of carved caravans setting out. Carts queue in the cool of the arch's shadow, and past it the paved road runs straight into the green dark of Sablewood.

Beneath the arch lives a permanent little fair. Toll-counters clack. A crier calls the morning rates. A stall sells painted gate-charms to travelers who already bought three other kinds of courage. The air smells of fried dough, hot sealing-wax, horse-goat harness, and forest rain waiting just beyond the wall.

There is no ward missing here and nothing broken in the public face of the gate. The drama is simpler and more useful: this is where city confidence becomes road risk.
player_safe.known_for: The western threshold of Emeris, route tolls, courier departures, gate charms, caravan queues, and the first straight look into Sablewood.
player_safe.culture_food: Travelers buy fried dough, hot spiced cider, route tokens, painted gate charms, and advice from people who may or may not have survived the road themselves.
player_safe.travel_texture: Passing under the gate cools the air for one breath. Then the city noise falls behind and the forest sound comes forward.

player_safe.name: Emeris
player_safe.short: A walled city of honey-colored stone on the very lip of the great forest, where the last paved road in the world meets the first wild tree.
player_safe.one_line: A walled city of honey-colored stone on the very lip of the great forest, where the last paved road in the world meets the first wild tree.
player_safe.read_aloud: Emeris is a prosperous walled city built where the paved world ends and Sablewood begins. Honey-colored houses climb gentle streets toward a great western gate, banners hang from crowded windows, and the air smells of fresh bread, ink, oiled leather, and the green breath of the forest.
player_safe.long_body:
Emeris is the capital of its own territory and proud of it, a tight, prosperous walled city built where the paved world ends and Sablewood begins. Its houses are honey-colored stone with steep painted shingles, crowded shoulder to shoulder up gentle streets that all seem to bend, eventually, toward the great gate in the western wall. Banners hang from every other window, half of them advertising something.

The markets are loud and good-natured. This is a courier town as much as a capital, so the talk is all of routes and weather and who got back from the forest and who did not. Caravans are loaded in the squares at dawn, and licensed guides hawk their route knowledge like fruit. The smell is fresh bread, ink, oiled leather, and the green breath of the forest leaking over the wall.

The people are frontier-prosperous: friendly, busy, a little boastful, with the particular confidence of folk who have never once doubted that their city is safe. They will tell you Emeris is the finest city in the territory, and within the territory they are not wrong.
player_safe.known_for: The last paved, walled comfort before Sablewood, courier and caravan trade, its great Capital Gate, painted shingles, route gossip, and festivals.
player_safe.culture_food: Emeris treats routes as gossip and safe returns as public celebration. Street food is fried festival dough, skewered river fish, and hot spiced cider sold at the gate to travelers heading into the trees.
player_safe.travel_texture: Leaving Emeris feels like walking out of bread, bells, and stone into green shadow. The road stays paved just long enough to make the first mud feel like a decision.

player_safe.name: Athervast
player_safe.short: A city like a coiled crown, where gold-capped towers rise from the center and the rings spiral outward, lower and louder, until the gleam becomes rumor.
player_safe.one_line: A city like a coiled crown, where gold-capped towers rise from the center and the rings spiral outward, lower and louder, until the gleam becomes rumor.
player_safe.read_aloud: Athervast does not have a skyline so much as a spiral. At its heart stand grand pale towers capped in gold, so tall that clouds catch on them, and from that crown the whole city winds outward in vast circular tiers like the inside of a shell.
player_safe.long_body:
Athervast does not have a skyline so much as a spiral. At its heart stand the grand towers, pale stone capped in gold, so tall that the clouds catch on them, and from that crown the whole city winds outward in vast circular tiers like the inside of a shell, ring within ring within ring. It is the kind of place that makes you think of Atlantis, if Atlantis had been bought and rebranded.

Up in the highest rings the streets are quite literally gold, swept clean every hour, quiet but for the splash of fountains and the soft chime of a thousand floating witch-lights. This is where the elites live and rule. They are carried, not walked. The air up here smells of citrus, cold stone, and money.

Drop a tier or two and the city gets brighter and far louder. The entertainment district never sleeps: enormous magical illusions bloom across the open sky, silent dragons and dancing giants and grinning corporate mascots a hundred feet tall, drifting between towers like colored smoke. Crowds pour out of illusion-theatres and luck-halls, criers sell tickets to wonders that may or may not be real, and the streets taste of spun sugar, spilled wine, and perfume.

Further out, the rings turn to work. Here are the great manufactories: long glass-roofed halls where laborers stir steaming vats of Hexmart healing draughts and bottle them by the thousand, the air gone sharp with mint and copper and something faintly medicinal. The streets here are honest stone, not gold. The people move fast and tired. They make everything the gold rings drink.
player_safe.known_for: Gold streets in the high rings, sky-illusions in the entertainment tiers, potion manufactories in the workrings, and the public claim that it is the safest and grandest city on Terra.
player_safe.culture_food: Status is altitude. Up top: candied citrus and iced wine. In the bright rings: sugar twists, skewers, cheap dazzling cocktails. In the workrings: hard bread and bitter green tonic the factory crews drink to keep their hands steady.
player_safe.travel_texture: Athervast is not on the one-shot route. If it appears, it should feel distant, huge, aspirational, and insulated from the road's mud.

player_safe.name: The Goldspire Relay
player_safe.short: A twisting stone signal-spire of mirrors, flags, and courier-birds, its beacon flickering thinner than it should.
player_safe.one_line: A twisting stone signal-spire of mirrors, flags, and courier-birds, its beacon flickering thinner than it should.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Goldspire Relay twists upward like maintenance became monument, its weak fire making future failure visible.
player_safe.long_body:
Wind, beacon-light, signal-workers, ridge paths, anxious maintenance, and a view wide enough to imply the rest of the story. The world feels like it is answering back from up here.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Signal yard: Mirrors, flags, and courier birds make communication visible. Beacon chamber: The light source flickers with meaning. Ridge overlook: The view connects every prior place at once. Maintenance stair: Narrow steps and tool niches make the spire feel worked, not decorative.

Plants and materials: wind-bent ridge grass, lichen on signal stones, small herbs in stair cracks. Animals and background life: courier birds, ridge insects, tiny cliff goats that ignore danger. The air carries beacon pulse, high wind, signal chime, far storm light. Messages arrive, are questioned, encoded, relayed, delayed, and sometimes quietly corrected.

What people can get here: message relay, ridge lodging, maintenance supplies.
player_safe.known_for: A stone spire that twists upward as if maintenance kept turning into monument. The signal yard flashes with mirrors, flags, and courier-birds. The beacon chamber flickers with meaning. From the ridge overlook you can see every place you have been at once, and the narrow maintenance stair makes plain this is a worked tower, not a decorative one.
player_safe.culture_food: Signal crews eat in shifts at the yard, one hand always free for a flag, bread and hard cheese and a tea brewed strong enough to survive the wind. The courier-birds get the scraps and the affection both.
player_safe.travel_texture: The beacon pulses, high wind tugs at your cloak, signal-chimes ring out of time with each other. Far storm-light flickers along the horizon. Messages arrive, get questioned, encoded, relayed, and sometimes quietly corrected, and you feel the whole web of the world tugging on this one thin point.

outcomes.hard_failure: A flat read of Hidden hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.

outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.

player_safe.name: Underroot
player_safe.short: A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface.
player_safe.one_line: A concealed web of tunnels and homes carved among roots where off-ledger communities survive below the dangerous surface.
player_safe.read_aloud: Underroot is not a dungeon; it is a concealed neighborhood of root rooms, low lanterns, and people who survive below the route economy.
player_safe.long_body:
Underroot is the forest's underside: damp passages, glowing fungus, root doors, old animal routes, and the sense that the ground has a memory.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Root tunnel: Twisting roots make walls, ceiling, and handholds. Glowfungus chamber: Soft light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Flood pocket: A low chamber holds dark water and hidden movement.

Plants and materials: glowfungus shelves, pale root hairs, water moss, small blind flowers. Animals and background life: Centi-Beetles carve low tunnels, Spidermanders press ash-damp feet into soft walls, Hellbender legends make every tremor feel observed, Fox-Bats sleep in warm cracks. The air carries drips echoing too far, earth-warm air, root doors creaking as they grow, fungus light dimming near noise. Roots pull water down, fungus turns rot into light, insects feed on fungus, and larger animals use the tunnels during storms.
player_safe.known_for: This is not a dungeon, it is somewhere people live, down where the official map stops. Roots make the walls and the ceiling and the handholds. Soft fungus-light turns water drops and old stones into landmarks. Low doorways open on rooms warmed by the earth itself, and the air tastes of damp and lamp-smoke.
player_safe.culture_food: Food comes up from below and out of the dark, pale fungus, blind fish, roots boiled soft, a thin sweet beer brewed in a hollow. It is shared carefully, because everything down here was hard to get, and a guest who wastes it is not a guest for long.
player_safe.travel_texture: You duck and the world goes close and warm. Drips echo too far in the dark. Root-doors creak as they keep growing, and the fungus-light dims when you raise your voice, as if the place itself is asking you to keep it down.

player_safe.name: The Titan's Steps
player_safe.short: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
player_safe.one_line: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Titan's Steps climb through height, rope, sweat, and hazard pay until travel itself feels like a negotiated risk.
player_safe.long_body:
Each stair is a plaza. Each crack is a path. Every climb is a small expedition, and the people who run it have learned to laugh at the size of the place so it does not crush them.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lower grass step: Grass and flowers turn a single stair into a meadow. Crack path: A split in the stone is wide enough to walk through. Overlook lip: The edge gives a dizzying view across the territory.

Plants and materials: wind grass, step flowers, crack-root shrubs, lichen maps. Animals and background life: ridge goats, stone swifts, crack crickets, little lizards basking on warm stone. The air carries wind rise, warm stone, huge shadows, distant echo. Rain fills cracks, flowers bloom in steps, goats graze the platforms, and old carved channels guide water down.

What people can get here: wind shelter, rare herbs, high vantage.
player_safe.known_for: Each stair is the size of a town square, so a single step takes half a morning to climb. Grass and flowers have turned the lower treads into hanging meadows. A crack in the stone becomes a road you walk down the middle of. From the lip, the whole territory unrolls so far below that birds pass beneath your boots.
player_safe.culture_food: Climbers eat light and often, hard biscuit, dried meat, a sharp tea brewed at altitude to keep the hands steady. Hazard pay buys better rations near the top, and people guard a warm flask like a secret worth keeping.
player_safe.travel_texture: The wind rises with you and the air thins until your chest works for every breath. Warm stone underfoot, huge cold shadows overhead. An echo you started comes back to you changed, and you feel, in a dizzy funny way, very small and very alive.

block2.culture_food: Climbers eat light and often, hard biscuit, dried meat, a sharp tea brewed at altitude to keep the hands steady. Hazard pay buys better rations near the top, and people guard a warm flask like a secret worth keeping.

player_safe.one_line: A Sablewood trade point where route knowledge, watches, and liability-backed bargains change hands above or beside the old wood.
player_safe.read_aloud: Duskwatch Exchange is where route knowledge changes hands quietly, because the forest charges more for ignorance.
player_safe.long_body:
Duskwatch Exchange is a trade post at the hour when everyone wants business done before dark: lantern counters, route boards, package yards, food smoke, and tired guards.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lantern counters: Merchants trade goods under warm low light. Watch platform: A raised lookout watches road, sky, and crowd. Package yard: Crates, straps, seals, and arguments make terrain.

Plants and materials: dusty hedge rows, lantern herbs, tough road weeds. Animals and background life: pack beetles, courier birds, dusk moths, tired road ponies. The air carries lantern smoke, bell calls, seal wax smell, twilight chill. Business peaks at dusk, then the exchange becomes watchful, quiet, and protective.

What people can get here: trade goods, package handling, road news, cheap hot food.
player_safe.known_for: Everyone wants their business done before dark, so the whole place moves at a hurried, friendly clip until the light goes. Lantern counters glow under low awnings. A raised platform keeps watch on road and sky at once. The yard fills with crates, straps, wax seals, and the particular arguments of tired people with somewhere to be.
player_safe.culture_food: Hot food comes off a smoking griddle fast and cheap, skewers, fried roots, a strong dark stew ladled to anyone with a coin and a hurry. The cider is warm, and the portions get bigger as the light gets lower.
player_safe.travel_texture: Lantern smoke and seal-wax in the cooling air, bells calling the last trades. As dusk drops the bargaining quiets and the place turns watchful, doors easing shut, lanterns pulled in, the whole exchange listening to the dark beyond the wood.

player_safe.name: The Catcher's Cradles
player_safe.short: A cradle system associated with the Titan's Steps, letting Sablewood's logistics guild make vertical risk look routine.
player_safe.one_line: A cradle system associated with the Titan's Steps, letting Sablewood's logistics guild make vertical risk look routine.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Catcher's Cradles make vertical danger look routine: suspended nets, rescue platforms, and the quiet pride of people who catch mistakes for a living.
player_safe.long_body:
The Catcher's Cradles are practical and absurd: huge nets, hanging baskets, pulley towers, safety flags, caught debris, and workers who judge people by how they handle rope.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Lower net field: Big nets sag under old catches. Pulley posts: Ropes and baskets create vertical movement. Repair platform: Workers patch nets and gossip overhead.

Plants and materials: rope vines, wind moss on poles, snagged seed pods. Animals and background life: nesting swifts, net spiders, beetles eating old rope fibers. The air carries rope twang, net sway, pulley squeal, sudden drops stopped by fabric. The cradles catch falling cargo, branches, animals, and pride; workers sort what can be saved.

What people can get here: rope work, salvage, fall-safe crossing.
player_safe.known_for: Huge nets sag between the trees, heavy with a century of caught things, branches, crates, the occasional boot. Pulley towers haul baskets up and down. Safety flags snap overhead. The workers size up a newcomer entirely by how they handle a rope, and they are usually right.
player_safe.culture_food: The crews eat on the repair platforms, passing a shared pot hand to hand so no one has to climb down for it. Plain food, beans and bread and strong tea, eaten with the easy gallows-humor of people who catch other people's mistakes for a living.
player_safe.travel_texture: Ropes twang and nets sway as you cross. Something drops nearby and is caught with a soft enormous whump you feel in your teeth. The workers move like the height is nothing, and watch to see whether you can do the same.

player_safe.name: The Lucent River
player_safe.short: A luminous river whose blue night glow lets travelers keep time and whose waters are sold, mythologized, healed by, and hunted in.
player_safe.one_line: A luminous river whose blue night glow lets travelers keep time and whose waters are sold, mythologized, healed by, and hunted in.
player_safe.read_aloud: The Lucent River carries blue light through Sablewood like a road that refuses to become a road.
player_safe.long_body:
The Lucent River is beautiful navigation: glowing current, rope ferries, shrine stones, shallow crossings, and water bright enough to make secrets feel visible.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Rope ferry: A small ferry crosses the bright current. Shrine bank: Tiny offerings sit where the river bends. Glow shallows: The riverbed shines through clear water.

Plants and materials: river reeds, glow algae, bank herbs, water lilies with pale undersides. Animals and background life: Craymeleon-pulled boats work the current, Eeligator ripples cut the glowing shallows, glass fish flash under the rope ferry. The air carries blue light from below, rope creak, current whisper, wet stone coolness. Algae bloom with moon and ward pulses; fish follow light, birds follow fish, and ferry workers follow all of it.

What people can get here: ferry crossing, river food, local shrine customs.
player_safe.known_for: The water carries its own blue light, bright enough at night to read by, so the river looks like a road that refused to become one. A small rope ferry hauls across the current. Tiny offerings sit on the bank where the water bends. In the shallows the glowing riverbed shines up through your own reflection.
player_safe.culture_food: Ferry folk grill glass-fish caught straight from the bright water, sweet and faintly luminous, and sell river-cress by the handful. Pilgrims buy little bottles of the glow, which is mostly algae and entirely hope.
player_safe.travel_texture: Blue light rises from below and lights you from the wrong direction, so faces look strange and honest at once. The ferry rope creaks, the current whispers, the wet stones breathe cold, and you catch yourself lowering your voice without meaning to.

player_safe.long_body:
The High Falls are loud, wet, and vertical: rainbow mist, rope overlooks, slick ledges, tents near the spray, and conversation that has to become gesture.

The place breaks into usable table spaces: Mist overlook: The falls drown out small talk. Spray path: A slick path crosses behind or beside falling water. Lower pool: Cold water gathers with floating flowers and debris.

Plants and materials: spray moss, cliff flowers, water ferns, roots gripping wet stone. Animals and background life: Craymeleon shells flash near mooring ropes, Eeligator shadows move below the lower pool, mist swifts hunt through spray. The air carries roar, rainbow mist, slippery stone, sudden cold gusts. Mist feeds moss, moss holds insects, insects feed birds, and falling water erases tracks unless someone knows where spray cannot reach.

What people can get here: clean water, cold storage, hidden conversation space.
player_safe.known_for: The Lucent River throws itself off a cliff into a cave mouth no one has fully mapped, and the roar swallows every word. Blue-white spray hangs in a permanent rainbow. Slick ledges thread behind the falling water. Tents cluster just out of the spray, and the people in them do not raise their voices because they cannot.
player_safe.culture_food: Cold is the whole pantry here. The spray keeps fish and milk and cut fruit fresh on the lower ledges, and travelers trade for the luxury of something genuinely chilled. A kettle has to be carried well back from the water just to be heard to boil.
player_safe.travel_texture: The roar arrives before the falls do and takes your words with it. Spray beads on everything, the stone goes treacherous underfoot, and cold gusts shove up out of the pool. Conversation becomes hands and eyebrows, and the falling water quietly erases your tracks behind you.
