gmBeats.label: Meet the contact
gmBeats.title: Your Contact
gmBeats.gmScript: Use this beat for Sabine only if you want the optional backup NPC job-giver. If Sabine is in play, do not say her name until the players ask or she introduces herself. Push her image to the player display here. Marlowe remains a PC custodian in the crew and receives the job with everyone else.
gmBeats.storyTakeaway: The contact is a real, frayed person, not just a corporate mouthpiece.
gmBeats.mechanicTakeaway: Model the core loop: ask a question, get an answer.
gmBeats.playerTakeaway: The woman has a name once I engage with her.

player.title: Engagement reveals the contact
player.statement: The contact has a name when players ask or she introduces herself.
player.body: If Marlowe is a PC, do not make Marlowe the briefer. Marlowe receives the job with everyone else and can still carry custodian pressure.
player.say: "A tired, well-dressed field agent watches the crew from beside the carriage. She looks ready to talk, but she has not volunteered much yet."
player.ask: If players ask her name: "Sabine. Sabine Quillon. You are the crew Emeris sent? Good. We are losing daylight."
player.deeper: If Marlowe is a PC, do not make Marlowe the briefer. Marlowe receives the job with everyone else and can still carry custodian pressure.

story.title: The contact is nervous but capable
story.statement: The contact's tension gives the company story a human crack.
story.body: Do not reveal manufactured danger here. The useful clue is emotional: competence plus nerves.
story.say: "She is not falling apart. She is competent, tired, and watching the road like it has disappointed her before."
story.ask: If players ask whether she is lying: "On Instinct or Presence 13, she is not simply lying; she is repeating a company-safe version of danger while worrying about the parts she cannot control."
story.deeper: Do not reveal manufactured danger here. The useful clue is emotional: competence plus nerves.

mechanic.title: Social reads follow player approach
mechanic.statement: Reading the contact uses Instinct; pressing or reassuring her uses Presence.
mechanic.body: On Fear, give the truth with pressure: she notices the read, gets guarded, or hurries the handoff.
mechanic.say: "If you watch her tells, roll Instinct. If you press, charm, or reassure her, roll Presence. Difficulty 13 either way."
mechanic.ask: If players ask what success gives: "You learn she is scared of the run, not of you, and that the official danger line sounds practiced."
mechanic.deeper: On Fear, give the truth with pressure: she notices the read, gets guarded, or hurries the handoff.

gmBeats.label: Briefing
gmBeats.title: The Sealed Package
gmBeats.gmScript: The briefing lays out the job in plain terms. If Sabine is in play, she gives this information; otherwise keep the same facts without making Marlowe the hirer. The crate is the package, never the Keystone Asset. If asked, the briefer can name Hush and the Sablewood preserve.
gmBeats.storyTakeaway: The contract terms are now explicit and table-facing.
gmBeats.mechanicTakeaway: Foreshadow that the journey will ask for rolls once risk appears.
gmBeats.playerTakeaway: I know the objective, the pay condition, and the don't-open-it rule.

player.title: The package is inspectable but sealed
player.statement: Players can examine the outside without opening it.
player.body: This cue should produce action: who checks the seal, who watches the contact, who positions near the cargo.
player.say: "The crate is visible in the carriage: banded shut, cold at the hinges, and not marked for public handling."
player.ask: If players ask whether they can inspect it: "Yes, the outside. You can look, touch, weigh, smell, or check the seal without opening it."
player.deeper: This cue should produce action: who checks the seal, who watches the contact, who positions near the cargo.

story.title: The crate feels more important than cargo
story.statement: The package hints at wardcraft, mineral wrongness, and official handling.
story.body: Even a success should preserve the reveal. Say wardcraft, stone-like weight, wrong mineral, protective seal; do not say Keystone Asset.
story.say: "It looks like cargo until you pay attention; then it looks like cargo someone paid magic and paperwork to keep quiet."
story.ask: If players ask what an inspection reveals: "Knowledge 14: the seal is contractual and protective. Marlowe Knowledge 13: old, high-tier wardcraft. Varian Instinct 13: wrong-mineral scent under the wax. Khari Strength or Instinct 13: the weight sits low and dense, like stone hidden in freight."
story.deeper: Even a success should preserve the reveal. Say wardcraft, stone-like weight, wrong mineral, protective seal; do not say Keystone Asset.

mechanic.title: Inspection uses approach-based traits
mechanic.statement: The trait depends on how the PC investigates.
mechanic.body: This is a strong teaching moment for Daggerheart traits: the same object can invite different traits based on method.
mechanic.say: "Tell me how you inspect it. Reading the magic is Knowledge. Noticing scent or pressure is Instinct. Testing weight is Strength or Instinct."
mechanic.ask: If players ask for Difficulty: "Use 14 for a general inspection, 13 for a character-specific lane: Marlowe wardcraft, Varian scent, Khari weight-sense."
mechanic.deeper: This is a strong teaching moment for Daggerheart traits: the same object can invite different traits based on method.

gmBeats.label: Questions
gmBeats.title: What Do You Ask?
gmBeats.gmScript: Let players interrogate the job. If Sabine is present, use her answers: name if asked; Emeris as employer; Hush as the destination; the forest danger as the company line; sealed means sealed. Marlowe's player also gets bonus insight and an extra Arcana check here.
gmBeats.storyTakeaway: Players convert unknowns into knowns by asking.
gmBeats.mechanicTakeaway: Optional Instinct or Presence 13 can read her nerves; optional Knowledge 14 can sense the official route story is too smooth.
gmBeats.playerTakeaway: Curiosity pays, and some answers may feel interestingly incomplete.

player.title: Questions move the scene
player.statement: Players can ask direct practical questions before accepting the road.
player.body: Give the table permission to be concrete. This beat is where players learn that curiosity pays.
player.say: "She is willing to talk while the crew loads up. Ask the practical question your character would not leave without asking."
player.ask: If players ask what to ask: "Who are you? Who hired us? Where are we going? What is the route? What happens if the package is damaged? What danger are you not saying plainly?"
player.deeper: Give the table permission to be concrete. This beat is where players learn that curiosity pays.

story.title: The company line has weak spots
story.statement: Answers provide names and practical facts, plus one useful doubt.
story.body: Names are safe here because the players earned them through the briefing. After naming, immediately translate back into plain meaning: company, village, old forest.
story.say: "Her answers are practical: destination, route, pay, and handoff. The uncomfortable part is how rehearsed the safety language sounds."
story.ask: If players ask for names: "Employer: Emeris Crown Holdings. Destination: Hush, a forest village. Route: the old forest road; company maps call it Sablewood."
story.deeper: Names are safe here because the players earned them through the briefing. After naming, immediately translate back into plain meaning: company, village, old forest.

mechanic.title: Question answers can trigger focused rolls
mechanic.statement: Direct questions get direct answers; hidden pressure gets a roll.
mechanic.body: This cue teaches that rolls should add leverage or texture, not block basic information.
mechanic.say: "If you ask a practical question, she answers. If you want to know what is underneath the answer, that is where a roll can happen."
mechanic.ask: If players ask what roll fits: "Knowledge 14 spots the route story as too clean. Instinct or Presence 13 reads her nerves. On Hope, she volunteers one extra practical detail. On Fear, she answers but gets guarded or pushes the crew to leave."
mechanic.deeper: This cue teaches that rolls should add leverage or texture, not block basic information.

gmBeats.label: Departure
gmBeats.title: You In?
gmBeats.gmScript: Get a clear yes or boarding moment. If Sabine is in play, this is where her backup job-giver role ends. Either way, the whole crew has received the job together and now owns the route.
gmBeats.storyTakeaway: The job is accepted and the journey begins.
gmBeats.mechanicTakeaway: Commitment and fictional positioning are the mechanic: players choose to board, inspect, ask, or create risk before departure.
gmBeats.playerTakeaway: We are committed and on the road now.

player.title: The crew commits
player.statement: Players choose to board, position, or force one last action before departure.
player.body: This should close the briefing without hard-cutting player agency.
player.say: "Before the carriage rolls, tell me your last practical move: board, take reins, sit by the crate, ask one final question, or inspect one thing."
player.ask: If players ask whether they can delay: "Yes, briefly. One last question or action, then the job needs to move before the route window closes."
player.deeper: This should close the briefing without hard-cutting player agency.

story.title: The route now belongs to the crew
story.statement: Once they leave, the contact recedes and the party owns the job.
story.body: This prevents the backup contact from becoming a guide NPC. The Prologue hands control to the PCs.
story.say: "The handoff is signed. The contact steps back. The carriage, the package, and the road are yours now."
story.ask: If players ask whether Sabine comes with them: "No. She handles the handoff. The crew takes the route from here."
story.deeper: This prevents the backup contact from becoming a guide NPC. The Prologue hands control to the PCs.

mechanic.title: Commitment and positioning lock in
mechanic.statement: The departure records who drives, who guards the crate, and who watches the road.
mechanic.body: If a PC creates risk before departure, call the roll that matches the action. Tampering with the seal should create employer pressure rather than reveal the contents.
mechanic.say: "Who has the reins, who sits closest to the package, and who is watching the road as you leave?"
mechanic.ask: If players ask why it matters: "Those answers decide who gets the first sensory clue, who can react first to the road, and which trait fits if trouble appears."
mechanic.deeper: If a PC creates risk before departure, call the roll that matches the action. Tampering with the seal should create employer pressure rather than reveal the contents.

pacing.label: Onboarding + Prologue
pacing.context: pregens, safety, connections, Contract overview, Job briefing, forest threshold

perCharacterLayer.lane: Arcana, ward-sense, and the custodian responsibility around the package.
perCharacterLayer.passive: Her attuned elven senses pick up faint ambient magic from the warded marker as they cross. She feels the boundary click off behind them.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: She can name that the boundary felt built, maintained, and contractual rather than natural.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, as the last marker passes behind you, you feel a faint magical boundary click shut like a latch.

perCharacterLayer.lane: Shadows, deals, underworld instinct, and noticing when a job smells wrong.
perCharacterLayer.passive: The treeline has good shadow cover. He is already mapping where he would hide, or where someone else would.

discover.text: He spots that the official road is suspiciously the only cleared path; everything else has grown over.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: He can call out hiding places before the carriage reaches a blind curve.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, the treeline is full of hiding places. The official road is almost too clean compared with everything grown over around it.

perCharacterLayer.ancestryClass: Highborne Human Warrior, Call of the Brave
perCharacterLayer.lane: Threat-reading, escort habits, social warmth, and de-escalation.
perCharacterLayer.passive: Sightlines. He clocks the road's blind corners before the party reaches them, an old escort habit.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: He can ask who is watching the curve, the rear, and the carriage before the first blockage.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, your old escort habits kick in. The road has blind corners before the carriage reaches them.

perCharacterLayer.lane: Protection, reach, weight-sense, terrain scale, and standing between harm and the crew.
perCharacterLayer.passive: The scale of the trees registers differently to a giant. She reads them as climbable, defensible, useful terrain, not just scenery.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: She can point out where a large body can brace, lift, block, or climb if trouble hits.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, these trees are not just scenery to you. At this size, they are climbable, defensible, and useful.

perCharacterLayer.lane: Heightened smell and hearing, tracking, pathfinding, and home-terrain instinct.
perCharacterLayer.passive: This is their world. Varian reads the forest's mood through scent and sound. The hybrid animals are calm now, which means nothing is hunting yet.

discover.text: They pinpoint which direction the lark-moths and fox-bats avoid, foreshadowing the road blockage ahead.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Wayfinder gives the GM a clean reason to frame the fastest safe line through this stretch.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, the forest is calm for now. You can hear small creatures moving normally, which means nothing is hunting yet.

player.title: The table crosses a threshold
player.statement: Players know the setting has changed and the forest matters.
player.body: This transition should be brief, sensory, and playable. It is not a second lore briefing.
player.say: "The city falls behind. The road narrows. The old forest becomes the room around the carriage."
player.ask: If players ask what to do here: "Tell me who has the reins, where your character is in the carriage, and one thing they notice as the trees close in."
player.deeper: This transition should be brief, sensory, and playable. It is not a second lore briefing.

story.title: The company does not own the old forest
story.statement: The forest feels older and larger than the signs claiming it.
story.body: Use size and sensory language first: trunks wider than a carriage, green filtered light, animal calls dropping quiet, brass signs bolted to older stone.
story.say: "The signs say the route is managed. The trees make that claim feel very small."
story.ask: If players ask what the forest is called: "Locals call it the old forest. The company signs call it Sablewood."
story.deeper: Use size and sensory language first: trunks wider than a carriage, green filtered light, animal calls dropping quiet, brass signs bolted to older stone.

mechanic.title: Threshold framing hands players authorship
mechanic.statement: Ask who drives and let one player add a concrete forest detail.
mechanic.body: This reinforces that players can author sensory details when invited, while Kyle keeps control of hidden causes and the next obstacle.
mechanic.say: "Before the road problem appears, who has the reins, and what is one strange detail your character notices about these trees?"
mechanic.ask: If players ask for a roll: "Most details are free. Use Instinct 10 if someone wants a hint of trouble before the next scene; success points toward where the forest goes quiet."
mechanic.deeper: This reinforces that players can author sensory details when invited, while Kyle keeps control of hidden causes and the next obstacle.

player.title: Players can add one forest detail
player.statement: The table helps make the forest vivid with one concrete observation.
player.body: This is a safe creativity prompt: small, sensory, optional, and bounded.
player.say: "Give me one concrete detail your character notices: sound, smell, light, motion, temperature, or something about the trees."
player.ask: If a player freezes: "You can take one of mine: green light, wet bark smell, animal calls above you, roots like old hands, or a road too narrow for comfort."
player.deeper: This is a safe creativity prompt: small, sensory, optional, and bounded.

story.title: The forest is alive, not scenery
story.statement: The place reacts through sound, scale, and quiet.
story.body: Use per-character hooks to distribute attention without making every moment a roll.
story.say: "The forest is not a backdrop. It has weather, breath, animals, and old paths under the company road."
story.ask: If players ask what their PC senses: "Varian catches layered smells first; Barnacle notices what would make a good hiding place; Garrick reads the road like security exposure; Khari feels how small the carriage is under the trees; Marlowe notices wardcraft fading behind them."
story.deeper: Use per-character hooks to distribute attention without making every moment a roll.

mechanic.title: Sensory spotlight can become Instinct
mechanic.statement: Free description becomes an Instinct roll only when the player pushes for warning.
mechanic.body: On Fear, still give the warning but make it late, partial, or unnerving.
mechanic.say: "A sensory detail is free. If you are trying to read danger from it, roll Instinct."
mechanic.ask: If players ask for Difficulty: "Instinct 10 gives a broad warning that sound thins near the bend. Varian gets the clearest direction on success because scent and hearing are their lane."
mechanic.deeper: On Fear, still give the warning but make it late, partial, or unnerving.

player.title: The first obstacle is about to enter
player.statement: Players understand the quiet road is becoming active play.
player.body: This cue is the handoff, not the whole encounter. It should create forward pull.
player.say: "The carriage eases around the bend, and something is blocking the path."
player.ask: If players ask what they see: "Hold that for the next scene: shapes on the road, the carriage slowing, and enough time for one immediate reaction."
player.deeper: This cue is the handoff, not the whole encounter. It should create forward pull.

story.title: The route complication arrives
story.statement: The delivery is no longer only a contract; the road now pushes back.
story.body: Keep identity withheld until the Act One scene starts. Description first, proper nouns later.
story.say: "Whatever the company promised, the road has its own first answer."
story.ask: If players ask whether this is an ambush: "Your characters do not know yet. You know the path is blocked and the carriage is losing easy forward motion."
story.deeper: Keep identity withheld until the Act One scene starts. Description first, proper nouns later.

mechanic.title: Cut on pressure
mechanic.statement: The mechanic is pacing: end the Prologue on the first actionable pressure.
mechanic.body: This protects pacing and prevents the threshold from absorbing the Act One encounter.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The frame the entire adventure rides through: a colossal old-growth forest that Kazrak Industries claims to steward but never truly owned. It is the connective tissue between every other location — the carriage is always in the Preserve. Use it to set tone, plant unease, and answer "what's around us?" between scenes.
locationSlideModel.readAloud: This evening your party finally reaches the Sablewood Logistics Preserve — a sprawl of trees older than any signed deed, their trunks rising hundreds of feet until the canopy swallows the sky. The road beneath your carriage was a trade path long before Kazrak Industries stamped its name on it. From inside, you hear the forest breathing around you: the low call of lark-moths, the croak of a lemur-toad, the scatter of a fox-bat family through the underbrush. The light comes down green and filtered. Whatever this place agreed to, it did not agree to be owned.

sensoryStack.detail: Trees too large to be plausible; brass Kazrak compliance stamps nailed into bark and already being grown over; sunken trade paths worn into the roots; faint courier-route markers.
Lark-moth calls, lemur-toad croaks, fox-bat scittering, the creak of the carriage, wind moving through a canopy so high you never see it move.
Wet bark, crushed greenery, a sweetness like overripe fruit underneath. a faint resin tang near the compliance stamps.
Cool, damp, heavier than open road. Light arrives green.
Hybrid animals are the Preserve's signature — lark-moths, lemur-toads, fox-bats, and (later) strixwolves. NPCs are rare on the road itself; this is between-towns wilderness.

sensorySummary: Ancient trunks lean over the road until the sky becomes a thin green seam; old stones and moss shelves guide travel better than signs.
Leaf-drip, distant wingbeats, branches rubbing like low speech, and bird calls that restart behind the party but not ahead.
Cold rain on leaves, fungal sweetness, sap, wet bark, and the musk of unseen animals moving through root-shadow.
Bark leaves dark moisture and gold-brown pollen on fingers; the road shifts from springy moss to slick clay underfoot.
Owls, insects, and small ground creatures are around, but their silence moves like a ripple when danger or corporate residue passes.
visibleDetails: Great trunks lean over the road until the sky feels rationed.
Old stones, root shelves, and moss-dark bends shape travel more than signs do.
subtleDetails: Animals are present, but not where the signs say they should be.
Some roots curl around waymarker nails as if rejecting them slowly.
hazards: Lore sprawl. Keep as texture and move on.

slides.title: The Overturned Vendor Cart
slides.alt: The Overturned Vendor Cart scene art for The Logistics Incident.
slides.caption: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight.
slides.gmGoal: Block the road with a wrecked vendor cart, let the table read the scene, and plant that the obvious animal story does not add up.
slides.publicObjective: Figure out what happened here and clear the road.
slides.readAloud: Your steeds haul the carriage around a tight bend and stop hard. The path ahead is blocked: a vendor cart lies overturned, its fruit, vegetables, and spilled preserves scattered across the trail. Something has been feeding here. The air is wrong: sweet rot and something underneath it, coppery. From the far side of the cart, you hear wet, unhurried movement.
gmNotes: Use the wreck as an investigation scene first and a creature reveal second.
Player-safe language: body, feeding, blade wound. GM-only truth: staged murder and later Bramble connection.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The carriage stops hard. Ahead of you is a wreck, a body, and something feeding just out of sight. You can rush toward the sound, but you have time to look first. What do you check?" If someone checks the body, say: "The feeding is messy, but the killing wound is clean. This was not done by claws." If they need the roll, call Knowledge or Instinct, Difficulty 12.
gmReadAloud: The path ahead is blocked: a vendor cart lies overturned, its fruit, vegetables, and spilled preserves scattered across the trail.
Something has been feeding here. Sweet rot hangs over the copper smell of blood.
From the far side of the cart, you hear wet, unhurried movement.
gmChecklist: Offer investigation before the creature fully reveals.
Gate the slit-throat truth behind Garrick's passive read or a Knowledge/Instinct 12 check.
Seed the deliberate bramble in the wheel if Barnacle searches the cart.
Move to S01-03 when they approach the far side, try to clear the cart, or make enough noise to draw the creature out.
gmPrivate: The driver was murdered with a blade, then the scene was staged to read as a forest attack.
The creature is scavenging. It did not make the killing wound.
The bramble in the wheel foreshadows the later ambush. Seed it; do not explain it.
slides.playerTakeaway: Someone is dead, the road is blocked, and something alive is feeding on the other side of the cart.
slides.storyTakeaway: The wreck looks like a wild-animal attack, but the clean wound and staged cart point to a person behind the violence.

block2.day_to_day: Up before dawn, checking straps, route tags, and ward charms, then walking beside the cart until the wheels found a trustworthy groove.
block2.appearance: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair. Full-body reference: Full-body standing halfling courier in a practical traveling coat with satchel and route tags, weary kind posture, road-dust browns, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Debt-squeezed contractor; the care in her coat repairs shows she kept useful things alive long past their company warranty.
block2.animal_companion: No beast survived the wreck. Her closest road companion was the cart team and the route bell.
block2.physical: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.voice_style: She has no voice left. Let her speak through objects: the order of her route charms, the wear on a strap, a half-finished note. The table supplies her tone, and it should ache.
block2.body_language: The scene should read quiet and intimate, not grisly: a person interrupted mid-duty.
block2.quirks: Her route charms are arranged by people, not places.
block2.image_lore: The jaw scar came from an axle splinter on her first winter route. She kept the scarf because the person who bandaged her told her couriers should be seen before they are counted.
block2.npc_relationships: Other couriers would recognize her patched style, route knots, and careful manifest marks.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She cannot respond, so the scene asks the PCs to treat evidence as a person's last testimony.
block3.persuasion_levers: No persuasion. Instinct 12 or Knowledge 12 turns the wound, ward, and debt slip into the playable answer: this was made to look wild.

what_moves_them.result: The body and ground contradict a simple animal attack.
The debt slip points toward pressure bigger than one route.

block3.combat_lever: The playable lever is careful evidence handling and mercy toward what did not kill her.

Keystone Asset™: Inside the sealed crate, packed in wax-paper and reassurance, sits a heavy grey stone the size of a loaf, warm to the touch, faintly humming, with a light deep inside it that is slowly going out.

Incident Response Placard™: A flat brass disc on a post holds a watchful glyph and a single cheerful bell. When trouble happens nearby, the glyph lights, the bell rings once, brightly, and then nothing else happens at all.

Sableblade: Growing straight up out of dark forest soil, like a sapling that decided to be a sword, is a blade of living dark wood and pale metal. It has no maker's mark and hums when your hand nears the hilt.
Recall Stone: A smooth grey pebble feels warm and ordinary until it refuses to stay where you put it. Set it down, look away, and it waits back in your palm.
Goldwater Liability Token™: A heavy brass chit with a smiling coin-face drops into your palm like a tiny verdict. The fine print is too small to read without feeling blamed.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: Someone is dead, the road is blocked, and something alive is feeding on the other side of the cart.
player.say: "Three facts: someone is dead, the road is blocked, and something is eating on the other side of that cart. What do you do?"
player.ask: "You can search the cart, approach the body, listen to the thing feeding, hang back and watch, or ask another PC what they notice."
player.deeper: Give the table four concrete entry points: cart, body, sound, or position. This prevents the scene from becoming a single forced monster reveal.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The wreck looks like a wild-animal attack, but the clean wound and staged cart point to a person behind the violence.
story.say: "At first glance, this reads like the kind of forest attack the company warns about. The closer you look, the less clean that story gets."
story.ask: "The obvious answer is a creature attack. The discoverable answer is that the driver was killed with a blade first. Knowledge or Instinct 12 confirms it."
story.deeper: Do not name the later faction connection to players. Let the first fact stand: animal scavenging is true, but animal murder is false.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Investigation begins with what a PC examines; roll Knowledge or Instinct only when the answer is uncertain or gated.
mechanic.say: "Tell me what you examine. If the answer is obvious, I will give it to you. If the answer is uncertain or needs expertise, I will name the trait and the difficulty."
mechanic.ask: "Searching the cart gives basic facts automatically. Reading the cause of death is Knowledge or Instinct, Difficulty 12. Spotting deliberate staging in the wheel is Instinct, Difficulty 13."
mechanic.deeper: This is the first investigation procedure: question, object, answer. Dice appear only when the table needs uncertainty, expertise, or consequence.

likes_dislikes.likes: Warm bread wrapped for the road, clean tack, and couriers who remember names.

block2.dislikes: Company euphemisms for death, cracked cheap wards, and anyone pawing through her things without care.

block2.loved_ones: A family or household back along the courier road; name them only if the table searches or asks what the token means.
block2.day_to_day: Up before dawn, checking straps, route tags, and ward charms, then walking beside the cart until the wheels found a trustworthy groove.
block2.appearance: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair. Full-body reference: Full-body standing halfling courier in a practical traveling coat with satchel and route tags, weary kind posture, road-dust browns, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Debt-squeezed contractor; the care in her coat repairs shows she kept useful things alive long past their company warranty.
block2.animal_companion: No beast survived the wreck. Her closest road companion was the cart team and the route bell.
block2.physical: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.voice_style: She has no voice left. Let her speak through objects: the order of her route charms, the wear on a strap, a half-finished note. The table supplies her tone, and it should ache.
block2.body_language: The scene should read quiet and intimate, not grisly: a person interrupted mid-duty.
block2.quirks: Her route charms are arranged by people, not places.
block2.image_lore: The jaw scar came from an axle splinter on her first winter route. She kept the scarf because the person who bandaged her told her couriers should be seen before they are counted.
block2.npc_relationships: Other couriers would recognize her patched style, route knots, and careful manifest marks.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She cannot respond, so the scene asks the PCs to treat evidence as a person's last testimony.
block3.persuasion_levers: No persuasion. Instinct 12 or Knowledge 12 turns the wound, ward, and debt slip into the playable answer: this was made to look wild.

what_moves_them.result: The body and ground contradict a simple animal attack.
The debt slip points toward pressure bigger than one route.

block3.combat_lever: The playable lever is careful evidence handling and mercy toward what did not kill her.

player_safe: Her death is recent.

block2.appearance: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close. Full-body reference: Full-body owl-wolf hybrid mother, talon-tipped forepaws, barred grey-brown feathering, two downy pups at her flank, protective stance, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Wild creature under route pressure; no wealth, only territory and offspring.
block2.animal_companion: Her pups are present and should drive every reaction.
block2.physical: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.voice_style: No words. A rising chest-rumble, a wing mantled over the pups, eyes that track hands instead of faces. Her warnings escalate in clear, readable stages, and she would rather you leave than test the last one.
block2.body_language: Low, protective, ready to retreat if retreat becomes safer than warning.
block2.quirks: She watches boots more than eyes because boots decide distance.
block2.image_lore: The bright feathers around her throat are not ornamental; they flare when she is trying to look larger than her fear.
block2.npc_relationships: Her future relationship to the party is animal memory: mercy can become warning, distance, or aid later.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She expects armed two-legs to rush, shout, or claim the body without noticing the pups.

mapData.title: Overturned Vendor Cart Scene Board
mapData.caption: The blocked road, the dead driver, the strixwolf family, and the first clues that this was not a simple animal attack.
sensorySummary: A torn canvas cart, scattered cargo, wheel ruts, a body placed too neatly, and feathered movement low under the wreck.
A low wing-rustle under the cart, spooked horses breathing hard, small pups shifting in cover, and the forest holding back its usual calls.
Coppery blood, wet road grit, torn grain sacks, animal musk, and rain soaking into canvas.
Mud is churned and slick near the wheels; the cart boards are splintered; loose feathers cling to wet hands.
The strixwolf family is alive, frightened, and watching. The corpse and staging are evidence; the animal pressure is a mercy test.
interactables: The vendor cart: stripped of valuables before the creature arrived.
The dead driver: throat slit by a blade, then partially fed on.
The carriage wheel: thorny bramble deliberately wedged in it.
The spilled produce and preserves: harmless, but the sweet rot masks the blood smell.
The underbrush: movement, pups, and the creature's protected space.
hazards: Strixwolf protective pressure
spooked horses
hidden Bramble evidence

Instinct 13: bramble in the wheel and cart tipped deliberately.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The inciting scene and the table's first action roll (a Presence check to read the strixwolf). An overturned vendor cart blocks the road; a strixwolf and her pups are feeding on the dead driver. It teaches the Duality Dice through a tense-but-survivable animal encounter, and quietly plants the murder mystery (the driver's neck was slit — this was no accident).
locationSlideModel.readAloud: As your steeds haul the carriage around a tight corner, the path ahead is blocked. A vendor cart lies overturned, fruits and vegetables scattered across the trail. From behind it steps a strixwolf — a large creature with the body of a wolf, the face of an owl, broad wings folded along its back. It is finishing a meal: the hand of the dead driver. It stares at you, unhurried, deciding whether you are friend or food. Behind it, two pups stumble clumsily into view. Inside, you feel the carriage lurch to a halt. What do you do?

sensoryStack.detail: Overturned cart, scattered produce, the dead driver, the owl-faced wolf, two pups, broad feathered wings.
The strixwolf's wet chewing, a low warning hoot-howl, pups mewling, produce squelching underfoot.
blood and crushed fruit together — sweet and iron, deeply wrong.
Sudden stillness; the carriage stopped; everyone's breath held.
The strixwolf family is the focus. fox-bats watch from branches, drawn by the spilled food.

optionalRolls.Action: First action roll — read the strixwolf
optionalRolls.Notes: Canon (p.29). Success (10+): she's just protecting pups. With Hope → gain Hope. With Fear → gain Fear + a soft consequence (a second hoot-howl answers from the trees). Failure (≤9): she snarls; with Fear, PC marks Stress. Crit: she approaches tail-wagging, sits.
Canon scenario (p.30): stripped of valuables; driver's arm mangled by the family.
Canon (p.30): the driver's neck was slit. This is the murder seed — Bramble Union foreshadow.
Canon (p.30): on success, deal weapon damage; pups flee; mother flies to a branch and watches.

optionalRolls.Action: Look for signs of something strange
optionalRolls.Notes: Canon (p.30): thorny bramble tangled in the carriage wheel and strewn on the road — the ambush was staged.

optionalRolls.Action: Move the cart / get rolling again
optionalRolls.Notes: Canon: any attempt to clear the road or leave the trail jumps to the Ambush (location 03).

fearEvents: With Fear on the Presence roll: a hoot-howl answers from deeper in the trees — "you might not be alone for long."
Spend Fear: the pups bolt toward a PC, and the mother reads it as a threat — escalates without anyone choosing violence.
The strixwolf is not the real threat. If the table fixates on her, use her to point at the bramble in the wheel and the slit throat.
transitions: In: From the road (01), tight corner reveals the cart.
Out: Clearing the cart, leaving the trail, or getting the carriage moving → 03_The_Ambush_Site ("Ambushed!"). The whole cart was bait.
locationSlideModel.canonSource: Read-aloud, the Presence first-roll, the slit throat, the bramble-in-the-wheel, and the strixwolf stat line are all module-canon (pp.29–30).
hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: the slit throat and staged cart point toward a manufactured crisis, not a monster attack.
The useful question is who benefits from couriers dying on roads corporations claim to steward.
locationSlideModel.storyTakeaway: The vendor cart is a crime scene and mercy test, not a random animal fight.
locationSlideModel.mechanicTakeaway: Teach the first Presence roll through the strixwolf's protective posture, then point attention to the slit throat and bramble evidence.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Give basic search facts automatically, then use Knowledge, Instinct, or Finesse when players test the staging.
mechanic.say: "If your character just searches the cart, I will give the obvious facts. If you are reconstructing the scene or reading a body, that is where the dice come in."

mechanic.deeper: This board is the investigation procedure in one place: choose object, state method, answer obvious facts, roll gated facts.

perCharacterLayer.passive: The blood under the sweet-rot smell is older than the creature's feeding. Other PCs just smell that something is wrong.

discover.text: Places animal musk as recent, human blood as older, and a faint chemical-leather tang that belongs to neither.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can track which direction the creature came from versus which direction the killer left.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, your nose sorts this out faster than the others. The blood here is older than the animal. Want to follow what that tells you?

perCharacterLayer.passive: The throat wound is a clean blade cut, not claws or teeth. Someone killed this man.

discover.text: Confirms a deliberate, practiced cut: an execution staged as an animal attack.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can secure the scene and keep the party calm and methodical.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, you have stood over bodies before. This one's wrong. Want to say how?

perCharacterLayer.passive: The cart was tipped from the wrong side to be a simple accident.

discover.text: Finds thorny bramble wedged in the carriage wheel and valuables stripped before the creature arrived.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can rig the cart to clear the road quickly or quietly pocket something useful from the wreck.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, this does not read like an accident to you. What do you notice?

perCharacterLayer.passive: From her height she sees the drag marks, the feeding place, and the death place are not the same spot.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can clear the overturned cart single-handed when the party is ready to move.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, you can see the whole picture from up there. The man did not die where he is being eaten. Want to point that out?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Her attuned senses register no magic on the scene. Whatever happened here was mundane and deliberate.

discover.text: Confirms the absence of magic is notable; this killing was done the old-fashioned way by someone using the wild as cover.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can tell the party that the important package is not what caused this wreck to pulse with magic; there is no pulse here.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, you would feel it if magic did this. You do not. That is worth sitting with.

slides.title: The Creature and Her Young
slides.alt: The Strixwolf Mother scene art for The Logistics Incident.
slides.caption: The Strixwolf Mother is dangerous, frightened, and probably not guilty of the murder.
slides.gmGoal: Reveal the feeding creature by description first, then show that she is protecting pups and is not the simple monster story.
slides.publicObjective: Deal with the creature without anyone, including the pups, getting hurt, and clear the road.
slides.readAloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: the body of a wolf, the face of an owl, broad feathered wings folded along its back. It lifts its head from the meal and studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat. Then, behind it, two smaller shapes stumble into view: clumsy, big-eyed, and keeping close to its legs.
gmNotes: Player-safe: wary mother animal, two pups, road blocked by a decision.
GM-only: she did not kill the driver; she is not manufactured.
slides.gmScript: Say: "She has not attacked. She is watching you and keeping herself between you and the young. If you want the name, locals call this kind of creature a strixwolf. The important part right now is not the name. It is her posture. What signal do you give her?"
gmReadAloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: wolf body, owl face, and broad feathered wings folded along her back.
She studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat.
Two smaller shapes stumble into view behind her, clumsy and big-eyed, keeping close to her legs.
gmChecklist: Describe before naming.
Introduce the pups before anyone commits to violence.
Frame the creature as wary and protective, not aggressive.
Hand the resolution to S01-04: Presence 10 to read and influence her.
gmPrivate: She is a natural preserve hybrid and a scavenger here, not the killer.
If the party blames or kills her, the real killer's trail goes quieter and the corporate forest-danger story gets easier to believe.
slides.playerTakeaway: You face a wary mother animal and two pups; your posture decides whether this turns violent.
slides.storyTakeaway: The apparent monster is a parent protecting young, and the encounter is about restraint before violence.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: The next roll reads intent and influences reaction: Presence against Difficulty 10, with mercy and aggression branching the scene.

block1.critical_info: She is scavenging and protecting pups; she is probably not the killer.
block1.disposition_default: Protective, frightened, and willing to leave if given space.
block1.the_lever: Distance and calm hands. Food helps if the party does not crowd the pups.

block2.wants_now: Keep the pups fed and far from armed strangers.
block2.larger_motivation: Survive the roads that keep cutting through hunting ground.
block2.wants: Keep the pups fed and far from armed strangers.
block2.motivation: Survive the roads that keep cutting through hunting ground.
block2.personality: Not cruel and not hungry for a fight, just a cornered parent doing math no one taught her, weighing every armed stranger against two small clicking shapes under her wing. She will let you walk away. She will not let you walk closer.
voice: She does not speak; she lowers her wings over the pups and tracks hands, not faces.
block2.secrets: There is no secret motive; the clue is that she is a mother, not a murderer.
block2.fears: A sudden rush toward the pups, fire, and cornered noise.

likes_dislikes.likes: Distance, lowered weapons, tossed food, and the party giving her a clear exit.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.

block2.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.
block2.favorite_thing: The pups' soft clicking calls, which she answers with a low chest rumble.
block2.loved_ones: The two pups under her wing; they are the reason every choice matters.
block2.day_to_day: Hunts along the route edges at dawn and dusk, using wreckage only when the forest has been pushed thin.
block2.appearance: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close. Full-body reference: Full-body owl-wolf hybrid mother, talon-tipped forepaws, barred grey-brown feathering, two downy pups at her flank, protective stance, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Wild creature under route pressure; no wealth, only territory and offspring.
block2.animal_companion: Her pups are present and should drive every reaction.
block2.physical: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.voice_style: No words. A rising chest-rumble, a wing mantled over the pups, eyes that track hands instead of faces. Her warnings escalate in clear, readable stages, and she would rather you leave than test the last one.
block2.body_language: Low, protective, ready to retreat if retreat becomes safer than warning.
block2.quirks: She watches boots more than eyes because boots decide distance.
block2.image_lore: The bright feathers around her throat are not ornamental; they flare when she is trying to look larger than her fear.
block2.npc_relationships: Her future relationship to the party is animal memory: mercy can become warning, distance, or aid later.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She expects armed two-legs to rush, shout, or claim the body without noticing the pups.
block3.persuasion_levers: Empathy and calm land. Intimidation turns the scene into a fight. Presence 12 or Instinct 11 with food opens safe access.

what_moves_them.result: She stops escalating and gives the party room to investigate.
Food and distance turn the scene from fight to wary truce.

block3.combat_lever: She breaks off as soon as the pups have room to flee or the PCs clearly choose distance over dominance.

ties_to_pcs: Varian can smell fear and carrion separation; Khari can protect space without escalating.

block5.person_under_the_fight: Not a person, a mother. The wreck is not her doing; the road cut her hunting ground down to a ribbon and the pups have not eaten since yesterday. player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You face a wary mother animal and two pups; your posture decides whether this turns violent.
player.say: "She has not attacked. She is watching. What you do next sets the tone."
player.ask: "You could try to calm her, back the carriage off, give the pups room, put yourself between panic and harm, or ready a weapon. Each sends a different signal."
player.deeper: Ask for posture, not tactics first. Hands open, lowered weapons, soft voices, slow retreat, or protective positioning all give the next roll a clear fictional basis.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The apparent monster is a parent protecting young, and the encounter is about restraint before violence.
story.say: "This is not a monster blocking your road. This is a mother that found an easy meal, and she has young."
story.ask: "A local or Varian can name her a strixwolf. If you ask whether she killed the driver, the body clue says no: the killing wound was a blade."
story.deeper: The players can learn the name through play, but the emotional truth lands first: mother, pups, fear, space.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: The next roll reads intent and influences reaction: Presence against Difficulty 10, with mercy and aggression branching the scene.
mechanic.say: "You are about to read her, not attack her. How you carry yourself decides what she does."
mechanic.ask: "If you try to calm or read her, this is Presence, Difficulty 10. If you attack, use the combat board; she defends the pups and tries to flee, not die."
mechanic.deeper: This scene teaches that mechanics follow approach. Mercy routes to a reaction roll; aggression routes to the combat map as a recoverable failure state.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Teach duality, outcome bands, and the slider together.
gm_runtime_payload: Roll both d12s. Add the numbers and report total plus which die came up higher.
The higher die gives the tone: Hope or Fear.
Now read the slider for this total: Botch, Miss, Hit, Clean, Soar, or Crit.
If the dice match, it is a Critical. Treat it as a success beat, award the bonus, and keep the scene moving.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: First real roll: teach official 2d12 Duality plus Kyle's slider overlay without a lecture.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Fear is escalation fuel, not punishment.
gm_runtime_payload: GM Fear starts at 1 per player and caps at 12.
Default play uses official 2d12 Duality.
Spend Fear to spotlight adversaries, make stronger moves, add adversary Experience, or trigger Fear features when the scene calls for pressure.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Keep Fear visible enough for pacing while preserving player-safe fiction.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Bank and spend Hope immediately in-context.
gm_runtime_payload: Hope starts at 2 and caps at 6.
Spend Hope on class features, Help an Ally, Experiences, and Tag Team later.
This is player currency: earning it means the table can push back.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Name Hope as immediate agency, not bookkeeping.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Teach the non-lethal path before the table misses it.
gm_runtime_payload: You do not have to end this with damage.
Approaching the strixwolf without spooking her is Presence 12.
Later, Bramble Union de-escalation is Presence 15.
On success, they pull back or listen; on Fear, the scene still asks for a cost.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Frame mercy as a viable tactic, not a hidden morality quiz.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Stress is pressure with a recovery edge.
gm_runtime_payload: Mark Stress when the consequence is strain, fear, pressure, or resource cost.
When a character marks their last Stress, they become Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 Stress.
If they must mark Stress while maxed, mark HP instead.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Make pressure visible without making it feel arbitrary.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Thresholds and severity land at the first hit.
gm_runtime_payload: Compare incoming damage to the target's thresholds.
Below Minor: mark 1 HP. At or above Major: mark 2 HP. At or above Severe: mark 3 HP.
One Armor Slot can reduce the severity by one threshold.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Teach damage once, out loud, so later hits move fast.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: One rule can unlock a better roll right now.
gm_runtime_payload: Traits use the spread +2, +1, +1, 0, 0, -1 across Agility, Strength, Finesse, Instinct, Knowledge, and Presence.
If an Experience clearly applies, spend 1 Hope for +2.
Ask the player what part of their background helps before the roll lands.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Teach character sheets through a real risky action.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Heightened senses catch predator panic first.
gm_runtime_payload: Varian, your Ranger focus spots the non-threat posture. Want to read the creature and shape the team's action?

slides.title: Creature Mercy / Defensive Escalation Battlefield
slides.alt: Strixwolf Mercy / Defensive Escalation battlefield map board.
slides.caption: Battlefield operating board for Strixwolf Mercy / Defensive Escalation.
slides.gmGoal: Use this only if the encounter turns physical. Make the combat board a recoverable failure state where restraint can still win.
slides.publicObjective: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
slides.readAloud: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
gmNotes: The creature defends and flees. She does not fight to the death unless the table hard-commits to killing a fleeing mother.
Winning does not mean killing her. Winning means road cleared and no one made the world worse.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is not a monster hunt. This is a defensive standoff. Every turn, you can escalate by threatening her or the young, or de-escalate by creating space, lowering weapons, opening the pups' escape route, or calming her."
gmReadAloud: The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open and claws in the mud.
The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
gmChecklist: Start with disposition at wary unless the party already attacked.
Offer a mercy route every round.
Use Fear to increase pressure, not to force a kill-box.
End the fight when she flees with the young or calms enough to leave.
gmPrivate: The right outcome is that nobody dies: no PC, no pup, not the mother.
Killing her quietly strengthens the false corporate story that the forest itself is the danger.
slides.playerTakeaway: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
slides.storyTakeaway: The fight is a consequence of fear; the clean win is still making space for the mother and young to leave.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Use normal action rolls, adversary attacks, Stress, and Fear, but keep a de-escalation route available every round.

gmNotes: The creature defends and flees. She does not fight to the death unless the table hard-commits to killing a fleeing mother.
Winning does not mean killing her. Winning means road cleared and no one made the world worse.
mapData.gmOrientation: The same blocked bend has become a tense defensive standoff. The mother is between the party and the cleared road; the pups shelter behind her. Every round of aggression escalates, and every round of restraint de-escalates.
mapData.combatBlock:
Treat this as a defensive standoff, not a monster hunt.
The mother pressures anyone who closes on the pups.
The party can win by creating space, calming her, or opening the pups' escape route.
If steel comes out first, use claws, wings, cart cover, ditch footing, and horse panic to make the cost immediate.

sensorySummary: The cart splits the road into threat lanes: pups under cover, the mother near the wreck, brush close enough for panic to become violence.
The mother growls through a birdlike rasp; pups chirr and whine under the cart; every weapon draw makes claws scrape wood.
Blood on wet dirt, frightened animal breath, torn canvas, old feed, and the sour edge of fear-sweat from the horses.
Wheel spokes snap under weight; the ditch is slick; loose harness straps can burn palms if grabbed hard.
This is a living family in a crime scene. Let the environment answer kindness, haste, and threat posture immediately.
hazards: Spilled produce creates difficult footing around the cart.
The pups are underfoot; reckless attacks risk harming them and should trigger a safety-aware check-in.
Horse panic can pull the carriage into the road if nobody steadies it.

checks.prompt: Presence vs Difficulty 10. Success de-escalates a step even after violence starts.
Agility or Strength 12. Once the young are safe, she de-escalates.
Normal action roll vs Difficulty 10. On a hit, she escalates to defensive and the pups try to flee.

fearSpends: She hoot-howls, implying another creature may be close without guaranteeing one appears.
A pup bolts under the cart, forcing a choice between pursuit and restraint.
A horse panics and shifts the carriage into a worse position.

optionalRolls.Action: Lower weapons and give the family space
optionalRolls.Notes: Signals mercy and can return the encounter to calm.
Creates a nonviolent win condition.
Use the cart, tarp, harness, or body position to block harm.

gmPrivate: The right outcome is that nobody dies: no PC, no pup, not the mother.
Killing her quietly strengthens the false corporate story that the forest itself is the danger.

gmDetails.title: Defensive escalation
gmDetails.body: Start wary, not hostile. Restraint moves her toward calm. Threatening her or the pups moves her toward defensive. She fights to create space, not to kill.

gmDetails.title: Creature operating stats
gmDetails.body: Tier 1 Standard creature. Difficulty 10. Attack +1. HP 3. Stress 3. Use the linked combat workspace for full encounter tools; on this slide, the important rule is protective flight at last HP or when the pups are threatened.

gmDetails.title: The pups' escape
gmDetails.body: The pups can flee through low branches and a brush gap. Opening that path de-escalates her one step.

gmDetails.title: Per-character hooks
gmDetails.body: Khari can be a living buffer. Varian can calm by scent and posture. Garrick can talk the party down. Barnacle can open an escape path. Marlowe can offer steady presence.

combatFraming: The creature starts wary, not hostile. Track disposition as calm, wary, defensive, fleeing.
Restraint de-escalates: any round where no PC threatens her or the pups moves her toward calm.
Aggression escalates: attacking, cornering, or threatening pups makes her defensive.
She flees, not dies: at last HP or when the pups are threatened, she gathers them and escapes to a branch, watching.
hiddenTruth: She did not make the kill. Killing her buries the real killer's trail and confirms the wrong story.
Let consequences land later through silence, distrust, or lost warning signs rather than a punishment speech.
transitions: Mercy or calm: she leaves with the young, the road clears, and Act 1's first beat resolves.
Combat: the encounter ends when she flees with the young, not when she dies.
After either route: return to the carriage and travel toward the next road pressure.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Recognizes a parent guarding young and instinctively wants to give the pups room.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Reads this as a tense standoff to defuse, not a fight to win.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Already sees the fastest way around her without making himself the center of attention.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can slip wide to open the pups' escape path or clear the road without a confrontation.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, you do not need to win this, just get past it. See a quiet way around?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Senses old preserve magic in the creature's blood, not corporate construction.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can reassure the table that this is a living forest creature, not a made weapon.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, she's the real thing, born of this forest. Not made. File that away.

slides.title: The First Action Roll - Reading the Creature
slides.alt: The First Roll scene art for The Logistics Incident.
slides.caption: The first meaningful roll teaches that this adventure is about judgment, not just success.
slides.gmGoal: Teach Duality Dice through the creature reaction roll and resolve the standoff caused by S01-03.
slides.publicObjective: Read the creature correctly and get everyone, including the young, out of this without bloodshed.
slides.readAloud: The creature is wary of every movement you make. Let's find out how she reacts. This is your first roll: grab your two d12s, add your Presence, and tell me the total, plus which die came up higher. If you have an Experience that fits, you can spend a Hope before you roll to add it.
gmNotes: Use the exact outcome language here so the first roll feels transparent.
After resolving the roll, return to the blocked road: the creature leaves, the road clears, or the encounter moves to the combat board.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is our first action roll. You are trying to read and influence a living creature, so this is Presence, Difficulty 10. Roll two d12s, add Presence, then tell me your total and whether Hope or Fear is higher. Before you roll, does an Experience fit strongly enough that you want to spend a Hope on it?"
gmReadAloud: This is your first roll: two d12s plus Presence against Difficulty 10.
Tell me the total and which die is higher: Hope or Fear.
If you have a fitting Experience, you can spend a Hope before the roll to add it.
gmChecklist: Name Presence and Difficulty 10 before dice hit the table.
Offer spend-Hope-for-Experience before the roll.
Resolve both axes: success/failure and Hope/Fear.
Route success or mercy toward a cleared road; route fear-heavy escalation to MAP-COMBAT-S01-03.
gmPrivate: This is not a floating tutorial. It is the resolution of S01-03.
Keep mercy as the clean path. Combat is a consequence of fear, threat posture, or failure, not the goal.
slides.playerTakeaway: You now know the action-roll engine: total against difficulty, then Hope or Fear colors the result.
slides.storyTakeaway: How you read and treat a frightened animal sets the moral tone for the rest of the route.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Roll Presence against Difficulty 10; 10+ succeeds, Hope/Fear changes who gains momentum, and doubles are a critical success.

rollCards.title: Make the first meaningful roll matter
rollCards.roll: Make the first meaningful roll matter
rollCards.why_this_trait: This is the teaching roll: ask what the PC does, choose the trait, then show Hope/Fear.
rollCards.stakes: The table learns that the roll changes the fiction, not just pass/fail.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: The table learns that the roll changes the fiction, not just pass/fail. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: None.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rollCards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rollCards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
relevant_conditions: Vulnerable
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Ask a player to narrate what Hope or Fear looks like on their face.
rollCards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the Difficulty, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You now know the action-roll engine: total against difficulty, then Hope or Fear colors the result.
player.say: "That is the engine: total beats the number or it does not; the higher die tells us who the moment favors."
player.ask: "For this roll, use Presence. If you have a fitting Experience, spend a Hope before rolling to add it. Then tell me total, Hope or Fear, and whether the dice match."
player.deeper: After this, future rolls can be faster: ask intent, name trait, name difficulty, roll, read Hope/Fear, narrate consequence.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: How you read and treat a frightened animal sets the moral tone for the rest of the route.
story.say: "This first roll is not about winning. It is about what kind of crew you are when fear gives you an easy violent answer."
story.ask: "If you calm her, she clears the way with the pups. If the scene turns hostile, she defends space and tries to flee; the road still clears, but the memory of how it happened follows you."
story.deeper: Use this result to set future texture: mercy can become warning, trust, or a feather token; cruelty can become silence, guilt, or later distrust.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Roll Presence against Difficulty 10; 10+ succeeds, Hope/Fear changes who gains momentum, and doubles are a critical success.
mechanic.say: "Ten or higher succeeds. Hope higher means you also gain Hope. Fear higher means I gain Fear and add pressure. Doubles mean a critical success: success, gain Hope, and clear a Stress."
mechanic.ask: "Success with Hope: she calms and creates space. Success with Fear: she calms, but hoot-howls as if calling another. Failure with Hope: she advances but you keep a softer opening. Failure with Fear: she advances and the roller marks Stress. Critical: she approaches head-down, tail wagging, and sits."
mechanic.deeper: This cue card is the exact table script for the first roll. Read it as needed, then narrate the specific posture and branch.

slides.title: Act Two: Cargo Reclaimers
slides.caption: The incident becomes a moral investigation instead of a simple ambush.
slides.gmGoal: Open Act 2 as the first moral fracture: the staged wreck points to people, not wilderness, and the coming ambush can become a fight, a parley, or a consequence the party has to live with.
slides.publicObjective: Get through the people blocking the road and keep the package moving toward the village.
slides.readAloud: The animal is behind you, one way or another. But the wreck did not arrange itself, and the more you look, the less this feels like bad luck. Someone wanted a wreck here. Someone wanted you here. The forest the company calls dangerous is starting to feel less like wilderness and more like a stage.
slides.playerTakeaway: You are being hunted by people, not predators, and how you treat them is a choice the game will remember.
slides.storyTakeaway: The danger in these woods has hands; Act 2 turns the dangerous-forest story into a human conflict.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Act 2 widens the toolkit: Instinct spot checks, Group Action investigation, combat pressure, and Presence de-escalation.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You are being hunted by people, not predators, and how you treat them is a choice the game will remember.
player.say: "Whoever is out there, you get to decide how this goes: blade first, words first, or eyes open before either."

player.deeper: The visible player choice is posture: alert investigation, defensive movement, direct challenge, or continued travel. Record later outcomes under bramble_outcome.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The danger in these woods has hands; Act 2 turns the dangerous-forest story into a human conflict.
story.say: "The road is telling you this was not a monster story. It is a people story wearing one."
story.ask: "You do not know who yet. You know they planned, they staged, and they are close enough for the staging to matter."
story.deeper: Keep the truth as a thread: people did this, they know the preserve, and the corporate forest story is now suspect.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Act 2 widens the toolkit: Instinct spot checks, Group Action investigation, combat pressure, and Presence de-escalation.
mechanic.say: "Watching, listening, and talking are real moves here. Swords are one option, not the whole tool kit."
mechanic.ask: "The next hard roll is likely Instinct 14 to spot the ambush before it springs. If the table investigates as a crew, use a Group Action Roll."
mechanic.deeper: Use Act 2 to demonstrate mechanical variety: team investigation, reaction/spot check, combat map pressure, mercy rewards, and consequence flags.

slides.title: The Fallout Investigation
slides.alt: The Fallout Investigation scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
slides.caption: The cart scene becomes evidence of a claim war, not a random wilderness hazard.
slides.gmGoal: Let the party confirm the wreck was staged, find the planted bramble, and realize the ambush is closing in.
slides.publicObjective: Work out what really happened here before you move on.
slides.readAloud: With the creature dealt with, the wreck is yours to read. Up close, the story stops adding up. The cart was stripped clean before anything wild got to it. The driver's wounds are not all bites. And worked into one carriage wheel, where it has no business being, is a snarl of black thorn that does not match this stretch of road.
gmNotes: Deepen Act 1's clue instead of replaying it: body, cart, wheel, tracks, then watchers.
Player-safe conclusion: people staged this and marked the carriage.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The animal part of this scene is over. Now the wreck gets stranger. The cart was stripped before anything fed here, the killing wound is too clean for teeth, and the thorn in your wheel means somebody got close to your carriage. What do you inspect first?" If they ask who did it, say: "You do not have a name. You have method: staged, local, and deliberate."
gmReadAloud: The cart was stripped clean before anything wild got to it.
The driver's wounds are not all bites.
A snarl of black thorn is worked into one carriage wheel, where it has no business being.
gmChecklist: If Act 1 already revealed the slit throat, frame this as confirmation of staging, not a repeat reveal.
Offer Group Action Roll: one leader, helpers feed evidence.
Start or tick the Closing In countdown if they linger loudly.
Do not name the faction yet.
gmPrivate: The staging points to organized people in the preserve. Do not decide the driver's killer; the README canon flag stays unresolved.
The planted bramble is the handoff into S02-02 and the ambush board.
slides.playerTakeaway: You now know three things: the wreck was staged, the stagers know this forest, and they have already touched your carriage.
slides.storyTakeaway: The party is the target, not a bystander; the road incident is becoming an ambush.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Investigation can be a Group Action Roll: one PC leads with Instinct or Knowledge while others help assemble the scene.

block2.wants_now: Keep the pups fed and far from armed strangers.
block2.larger_motivation: Survive the roads that keep cutting through hunting ground.
block2.wants: Keep the pups fed and far from armed strangers.
block2.motivation: Survive the roads that keep cutting through hunting ground.
block2.personality: Not cruel and not hungry for a fight, just a cornered parent doing math no one taught her, weighing every armed stranger against two small clicking shapes under her wing. She will let you walk away. She will not let you walk closer.
voice: She does not speak; she lowers her wings over the pups and tracks hands, not faces.
block2.secrets: There is no secret motive; the clue is that she is a mother, not a murderer.
block2.fears: A sudden rush toward the pups, fire, and cornered noise.

likes_dislikes.likes: Distance, lowered weapons, tossed food, and the party giving her a clear exit.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.

block2.likes: Distance, lowered weapons, tossed food, and the party giving her a clear exit.
block2.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.
block2.favorite_thing: The pups' soft clicking calls, which she answers with a low chest rumble.
block2.loved_ones: The two pups under her wing; they are the reason every choice matters.
block2.day_to_day: Hunts along the route edges at dawn and dusk, using wreckage only when the forest has been pushed thin.
block2.appearance: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close. Full-body reference: Full-body owl-wolf hybrid mother, talon-tipped forepaws, barred grey-brown feathering, two downy pups at her flank, protective stance, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Wild creature under route pressure; no wealth, only territory and offspring.
block2.animal_companion: Her pups are present and should drive every reaction.
block2.physical: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.voice_style: No words. A rising chest-rumble, a wing mantled over the pups, eyes that track hands instead of faces. Her warnings escalate in clear, readable stages, and she would rather you leave than test the last one.
block2.body_language: Low, protective, ready to retreat if retreat becomes safer than warning.
block2.quirks: She watches boots more than eyes because boots decide distance.
block2.image_lore: The bright feathers around her throat are not ornamental; they flare when she is trying to look larger than her fear.
block2.npc_relationships: Her future relationship to the party is animal memory: mercy can become warning, distance, or aid later.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She expects armed two-legs to rush, shout, or claim the body without noticing the pups.
block3.persuasion_levers: Empathy and calm land. Intimidation turns the scene into a fight. Presence 12 or Instinct 11 with food opens safe access.

what_moves_them.result: She stops escalating and gives the party room to investigate.
Food and distance turn the scene from fight to wary truce.

block3.combat_lever: She breaks off as soon as the pups have room to flee or the PCs clearly choose distance over dominance.

player_safe: The road is dangerous for animals too.
The body does not match a simple feeding kill.
gm_only: A mercy outcome can soften later wilderness pressure.

block4.disposition_to_corporations: No ideology; she embodies what routes and protection contracts do to living terrain.
block4.p2p_universe_tie: Shows how corporate routes turn living terrain into liability.
hidden_plot_hooks: Spared animal pressure can return as help, warning, or nonverbal witness.
ties_to_pcs: Varian can smell fear and carrion separation; Khari can protect space without escalating.
block4.npc_relationships: Her future relationship to the party is animal memory: mercy can become warning, distance, or aid later.

Every snap of her beak is the same question. Are you one more thing that takes, or the rare thing that finally just passes by.

npcProfile.imagine_it_like: Think a great horned owl crossed with a wolf, carrying the maternal fury of a mother bear. Picture the nature-documentary moment where the lens creeps too close to the den and the parent suddenly fills the whole frame.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The reclaimers target the cargo and manifest, not purses, and avoid killing when possible.
Their gear includes salvaged, repainted Grail/Kazrak kit: ex-workers, not feral bandits.
act_seeds.roll: Knowledge Medium 15 to name the issue

act_seeds.text: "That stone belongs in the ground." "You do not know what you are carrying."
