perCharacterLayer.passive: Recognizes the scene as staged immediately: looted, displayed, and too clean in the wrong places.

discover.text: The blade work was professional, not panicked; the death was made to look like wilderness violence.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can lead the Group Action Roll and turn separate observations into one clean read.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, this is staged and you know staged. Want to run the read while the others feed you details?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Clocks that the cart was professionally stripped; someone knew what was worth taking and moved fast.

discover.text: The thorn in the wheel was placed, and drag-trails lead toward the likely ambush position.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can back-trace the approach and give the party a better fictional position before S02-02.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, someone planted that thorn in your wheel on purpose. Want to follow how they got close?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Smells multiple people on the wreck, recently, with nervous sweat under the blood and mud.

discover.text: Counts roughly four or five distinct people and can tell they were frightened while they worked.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can separate animal scavenging, human staging, and the direction the watchers withdrew.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, your nose says four or five people did this, and they were scared the whole time. Want to read into that?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Finds no magic on the staging. The wrongness is mundane, ordinary, and therefore more unsettling.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can tell the party this scene was made by hands, not a spell around the package.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, again, no magic. People did this by hand. Sit with how ordinary that is.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Reads the road like a defender: where she would stand to box in a carriage, and where the party is vulnerable.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can reposition the carriage or stand as a defensive anchor before the spot check.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, if you were setting an ambush here, where would you stand? Want to guard against exactly that?

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You now know three things: the wreck was staged, the stagers know this forest, and they have already touched your carriage.
player.say: "Staged, local, and close. That thorn in your wheel means this was aimed at you."
player.ask: "You can inspect the body, cart, wheel, tracks, or treeline. The safest next action is to choose one thread and name who watches the carriage while you do it."
player.deeper: Keep the next action concrete: body, cart, wheel, tracks, treeline, or carriage guard. The evidence should feel playable, not abstract.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The party is the target, not a bystander; the road incident is becoming an ambush.
story.say: "This was not random damage on a road. This was a message and a setup."
story.ask: "The evidence says the people who did it understand the preserve, planned the stop, and got close to your carriage before you noticed."
story.deeper: Do not reveal the self-name or motive yet. The story truth for this scene is target, method, and proximity.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Investigation can be a Group Action Roll: one PC leads with Instinct or Knowledge while others help assemble the scene.
mechanic.say: "If you want to read this as a team, choose a lead. Everyone else says what they check and rolls to help that lead build the full picture."
mechanic.ask: "Use Instinct if you are reading tracks, smell, spacing, and threat posture. Use Knowledge if you are reconstructing wounds, staging, and procedure. Difficulty 12 for the body; 13 for the planted thorn trail."
mechanic.deeper: Group Action keeps this from becoming five separate rolls. It turns scattered observations into one shared conclusion before the ambush pressure arrives.

slides.gmGoal: Run the ambush spot check and fold in the strixwolf carryover before the road breaks open.
slides.publicObjective: Notice the threat before it reaches you.
slides.readAloud: The road feels watched. A branch snaps where no wind moved it. The hybrid animals have gone quiet: lark-moths, fox-bats, all of them holding their breath the way you are holding yours. Something is keeping pace with you in the brush, and it is not an animal.
gmNotes: This is dread into snap: quiet, tell, roll, ambush.
Mercy carryover is a mechanical reward, but the exact canon weight remains a Kyle confirmation flag.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The forest has gone quiet in a way your bodies understand before your minds do. Make an Instinct roll against Difficulty 14. Beat it and you see them before they move. Miss it and they get the jump." If the strixwolf was calmed or helped, add: "A distant hoot gives you one heartbeat of warning. Take an advantage die." If the strixwolf was killed or left blood-debt behind, add: "The forest gives no warning this time."
gmReadAloud: The road feels watched.
A branch snaps where no wind moved it.
Something is keeping pace with you in the brush, and it is not an animal.
gmChecklist: Read strixwolf_outcome, strixwolf_trust, and strixwolf_blood_debt.
Run Instinct 14.
Set ambushAwareness to see-them-coming or ambushed.
Move directly to MAP-S02-03 / S02-03 after the result.
gmPrivate: The watchers are nervous and organized, not monsters.
A high roll can reveal salvaged corporate gear without naming the deeper truth.
slides.playerTakeaway: Your attention right now decides whether the encounter starts on your terms or theirs.
slides.storyTakeaway: The hunters are close enough to act; the road has become a trap with a heartbeat of warning.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: This is an Instinct 14 reaction/spot check; strixwolf mercy can grant an advantage die or lower pressure.

The path forward is blocked by people, not beasts.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The module's first real combat and the Bramble Union reveal. The overturned cart was a staged distraction; Bramble Union reclaimers ambush the party to steal the carriage holding the delivery. Teaches: battle-map setup, the Ambush reaction, reference stat blocks, and the spotted-vs-ambushed branch (an Instinct 14 roll decides who acts first).
locationSlideModel.readAloud: In a whirlwind of cracking branches and unsheathed steel, four figures rise from the brush alongside the road. The overturned cart was an ambush all along. They stand before you, weapons drawn, blocking the way — and they move first.

sensoryStack.detail: Four Bramblefolk; armor made of polished river stones; daggers; thorny bramble worked into their gear; the staged cart behind them.
Branches snapping, steel leaving sheaths, a sharp whistle between the ambushers .
green sap, crushed thorn, sweat — people who live rough in the deep preserve.
Adrenaline; the road suddenly narrow; the carriage a prize behind the party.
The forest goes quiet (animals scatter from the violence).

optionalRolls.Notes: Canon (p.30). Success → "See Them Coming," PCs act first; with Fear, +1 Fear and mark Stress. Failure → "Ambushed!", Bramblefolk act first; with Fear, +1 Fear + Stress.

The thief's whole goal is the carriage; a PC can body-block the theft.

Setup (p.30): Lay the cut-out forest terrain across the table collaboratively; place the overturned vendor cart; players position their minis near the carriage; put Bramble Ambusher standees + the Bramble Thief in Close range.

slides.title: The Ambush
slides.alt: The Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
slides.caption: The road ambush should feel dangerous and understandable at the same time.
slides.gmGoal: Run the ambush as a dangerous moral choice: fight, defend, flee, surrender, or talk it down.
slides.publicObjective: Survive the ambush and protect the carriage and the package.
slides.readAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn. Their blades are mismatched, half of them salvaged. A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders. They do not whoop or charge. They block the road, weapons up, like people who hate that it has come to this. "The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."
gmNotes: The leader does not want a massacre.
Use Back Off to create space and panic, not to punish parley.
A downed ambusher can be spared without a roll; that lowers social difficulty.
slides.gmScript: Say: "They want the cargo, not your lives. You can fight, defend the carriage, run, surrender the package, or talk while weapons are up. If you talk, make the case in character and roll Presence against Difficulty 15." If they ask who they are and the conversation earns it, have the leader say: "We're the Bramble Union. We didn't used to be thieves."
gmReadAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn.
A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders.
"The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."
gmChecklist: Apply ambushAwareness from S02-02.
Explicitly offer parley as a live action.
Use Presence 15 for de-escalation; lower it for mercy, spared foes, or strong leverage.
Record bramble_outcome using existing enum: killed, captured, spared, negotiated, escaped.
Do not say Keystone Asset in player-facing text.
gmPrivate: The self-name is earned through dialogue. The public/corporate label remains Cargo Reclaimers until that moment.
Their salvaged gear points to former company people, but do not over-explain the hidden plot in combat.
If players choose slaughter, they win the fight and lose the easiest route to the truth.
slides.playerTakeaway: You can win this with steel, restraint, surrender, or words, and the choice defines who the party is.
slides.storyTakeaway: The attackers are desperate people who want the cargo more than blood; their humanity is visible before their story is clear.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: This combat tracks an outcome, not a body count: Presence de-escalation, non-lethal choices, and bramble_outcome all matter.

official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: A bad touch announces the party to every hidden bow. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: None.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rollCards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rollCards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
relevant_conditions: Hidden
Restrained
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Rogue PCs can turn the snare into cover.
rollCards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the Difficulty, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

lootClues: Use Bramble Union Ambushers and Claimrunner loot tables
Bramble Union Stoneweave: A garment of thousands of tiny polished stones moves like cloth and turns thorns like armor. Every fitted piece looks cut by hands that loved the work.
Vial of Briarpowder: A small stoppered vial holds fine grey-green thorn powder that seems to drink the light. A blade edge near it looks sharper and hungrier.
Bramble Ward-Scrap Charm Cluster: A knot of blue ward shards, twine, and tiny salvage tags clacks softly at a Bramblefolk belt. It looks illegal only because it looks useful.

Claimrunner Serrated Blade: A short serrated blade shows careful filing along the back edge and a handle wrapped in road cord. It is ugly in the practical way of a tool that has never had a decorative day.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You can win this with steel, restraint, surrender, or words, and the choice defines who the party is.
player.say: "Blade, bargain, shield, or surrender - all of those can end this. Pick the one your character can live with."
player.ask: "You can attack, protect the carriage, try Presence 15 to talk them down, spare a downed attacker, run, or hand over the package and deal with the fallout."
player.deeper: Make all exits real. The players should feel that victory is defined by consequences, not by eliminating every enemy.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The attackers are desperate people who want the cargo more than blood; their humanity is visible before their story is clear.
story.say: "They look scared and committed, not gleeful. That does not make them safe. It makes them people."
story.ask: "If the leader speaks honestly, she can give the self-name: Bramble Union. If nobody earns that moment, keep them as Cargo Reclaimers or ambushers in player-facing language."
story.deeper: This is the earned disclosure point. Use dialogue to reveal the name, never narration before the table creates the opening.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: This combat tracks an outcome, not a body count: Presence de-escalation, non-lethal choices, and bramble_outcome all matter.
mechanic.say: "Presence 15 can end this fight. Mercy shown earlier or now can lower the difficulty. Killing is not the only resolution the rules care about."
mechanic.ask: "Set bramble_outcome: killed, captured, spared, negotiated, or escaped. That flag changes S02-04 and whether the location maps open."
mechanic.deeper: Use HP and Stress for danger, but use bramble_outcome for meaning. The map, adversaries, Fear features, and social off-ramp all serve that outcome.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Ambush
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The road ambush should feel dangerous and understandable at the same time.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Survive the ambush and protect the carriage and the package.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn. Their blades are mismatched, half of them salvaged. A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders. They do not whoop or charge. They block the road, weapons up, like people who hate that it has come to this. "The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: Mercy opened a place, not just information.
player.say: "This is what not killing everyone made possible: a door, a fire, and people willing to decide whether you are safe."
player.ask: "You can listen, help, ask about the route maps, ask about the names, tend wounded people, or choose to leave without taking more from them."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The hidden villages make the attackers' motive human: these were people with homes, families, and losses.
story.say: "They were not born as a road problem. They became one when the road problem came for them."
story.ask: "The village shows families, injured workers, a memory wall, and repurposed company gear. The motive is survival, not cartoon banditry."
story.deeper: Do not excuse the ambush. Context and accountability should sit together.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Mercy creates access: Presence, Knowledge, and careful listening can turn a combat outcome into an ally route.
mechanic.say: "Presence 13 earns the story if mercy did not already. Knowledge 13 reads the route maps. Either can set bramble_truth_learned."
mechanic.ask: "If the players ask what this changes: it can open a safer route, a guide, a future ally, and stronger evidence before Hush."
mechanic.deeper: This map is a branch reward. It should not be reachable after a slaughter outcome unless Kyle chooses a later redemption path.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Recognizes the memory wall and route tags as company-discarded worker evidence.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, this looks less like a camp and more like people the company filed away. Want to read the wall?

perCharacterLayer.passive: The village's route maps make the package feel less like cargo and more like part of the same system.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, the route maps make your sealed delivery feel connected to their losses. Want to ask how?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Understands the logic of making ugly choices when all the clean doors close.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, you know the look of people surviving on bad options. Want to speak to them without judgment first?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Sees children, elders, and injured people before she sees defenses.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, the first tactical truth is that this place has vulnerable people. What do you do with that?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Reads the forest paths and can see the official danger map does not match the living terrain.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, the map they keep here does not match the company map. Want to compare what your senses know?

sensorySummary: A long briar mass shifts around paths, wagons, and hidden shelters. Leaves face the sound of blood before they face sunlight. The briar opens more easily for people who move like they belong.
Leaf-drip, insects, distant wingbeats, and animal calls that stop or resume according to pressure, not comfort.
Green sap, iron tang, crushed leaves, and damp earth under a bitter floral edge.
Thorns are smooth until they hook; vines are warm where the wall is awake.
The forest is populated even when no NPC is present; silence, birds, insects, and tracks are actionable signals.

gmDetails.body: Salvaged documents, incident maps, and timing notes point hard at manufactured danger without proving the whole campaign.

gmDetails.title: Council or leadership
gmDetails.body: The leadership can become future allies if the table earned trust and did not treat the place as loot.

transitions: From hidden villages or deep mercy after S02-04.

slides.title: After the Ambush
slides.alt: After the Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
slides.caption: After the fight, the module asks what victory cost and what the party learned.
slides.gmGoal: Turn the outcome of the ambush into consequence, truth, and the next route toward the village.
slides.publicObjective: Decide what to do with what just happened and get the package moving again.
slides.readAloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done. The horses breathe hard. The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly. Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks from the same kind of system that hired you.
gmNotes: Mercy route: leader or survivors talk.
Combat route: gear and effects talk.
Either route should leave the party asking who benefits from a dangerous forest.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The fight is over. The outcome matters now." If mercy or negotiation opened trust, say: "Up close, these people look less like bandits and more like former workers who have been sleeping rough and losing for a long time." If the party killed or routed them, say: "The gear tells the story the survivors cannot: company issue, filed off and reused." If players ask for the truth, use Presence or Knowledge 14, or mercy already earned, to reveal: "They were company or preserve workers who say the danger reports were manufactured to sell protection and discard the people who noticed."
gmReadAloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done.
Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks.
The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly.
gmChecklist: Read bramble_outcome before choosing variant tone.
Set bramble_truth_learned only if mercy/parley, survivor dialogue, or Presence/Knowledge 14 earns it.
Unlock location maps only for spared, negotiated, captured-with-care, or escaped-with-contact routes.
Give a thread, not the whole campaign explanation.
gmPrivate: The workers' claim is the first load-bearing truth thread, but the driver-killer canon flag remains unresolved.
Do not mention Keystone Asset in player-facing aftermath.
If players pursue the communities, use the two location maps as optional discovery, not mandatory plot.
slides.playerTakeaway: You do not have the whole picture, but you have seen enough to question who benefits from a dangerous forest.
slides.storyTakeaway: The attackers were tied to the same company world that hired the party; the forest's danger story no longer matches the evidence.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: The mechanic here is consequence: bramble_outcome and bramble_truth_learned decide what doors open next.

block2.day_to_day: Walks the perimeter, checks blade edges, settles arguments, and sleeps only after the youngest scouts do.

block2.animal_companion: No beast; the thistle charm is treated with the care another person might give a pet.
block2.physical: A horned Bramble field leader stands in moss-dark armor, jaw set, a blue ward pendant burning at the chest like a borrowed badge of command.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A horned Bramble field leader stands in moss-dark armor, jaw set, a blue ward pendant burning at the chest like a borrowed badge of command.

block2.body_language: Measures every person as either cover, witness, leverage, or threat.

block2.image_lore: The blue pendant is a dead waymarker lens. Kett wears it because people follow a person who looks like they know where the road used to be.
block2.npc_relationships: Protective of Vela, Rye, Brannic, and Nettle even when snapping at them.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: Kett expects outsiders to bargain like harm is already priced in.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You do not have the whole picture, but you have seen enough to question who benefits from a dangerous forest.
player.say: "You do not know the whole truth. You know enough to stop trusting the easy version."
player.ask: "You can question survivors, tend the wounded, search dropped gear, bury the dead, or get the package moving with new questions in your pocket."
player.deeper: Give players permission to move on without solving everything. The takeaway is suspicion with evidence, not a lore dump.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The attackers were tied to the same company world that hired the party; the forest's danger story no longer matches the evidence.
story.say: "These people were not outside the system. They were used by it, discarded by it, or armed from its leftovers."
story.ask: "Mercy or Presence/Knowledge 14 can reveal the worker-displacement thread: they say danger reports were manufactured to sell protection and silence people who noticed."
story.deeper: Keep the reveal as a thread. Do not settle the driver-killer canon flag or the whole ward economy yet.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: The mechanic here is consequence: bramble_outcome and bramble_truth_learned decide what doors open next.
mechanic.say: "How this ended changes what opens next. Mercy, blood, capture, escape, or negotiation all leave different doors behind."
mechanic.ask: "Set bramble_outcome from the fight. Set bramble_truth_learned only if they earn the thread. If mercy or trust exists, the optional location maps can open."
mechanic.deeper: This is the first clear branch payoff: violent resolution narrows truth access; mercy/parley opens communities, guides, and stronger future leverage.

slides.title: Act Three: Seeking a Custodian
slides.caption: Hush turns the package from cargo into a community question.
slides.gmGoal: Shift from road peril to a warm village sanctuary, then let the contrast carry unease. Establish the job plainly: reach Hush, find the person who keeps it safe, and deliver the package.
slides.publicObjective: Reach the village, find the person who can receive the package, and deliver it.
slides.readAloud: The road softens. The trees do not change, but the air does: warmer, kinder, like a held breath finally letting go. Ahead, lantern-light and music gather around ordinary people who feel safe. Somewhere in this village is the person you were sent to find. All you have to do now is hand off the package and collect your pay. Simple.
gmNotes: High mercy from earlier acts starts Hush warmer. Slaughter or extraction starts Hush polite but cooler.

slides.title: Arrival at Hush

slides.caption: Hush must land as a warm place with jokes inside it, not as the joke.
slides.gmGoal: Run the ward-boundary crossing, the first welcome, and the first read of how prior choices affect Hush trust.
slides.publicObjective: Enter the village, get your bearings, and find the person who keeps this place safe.
slides.readAloud: A tall stone pillar rises beside the road, carved top to bottom with old protective marks and newer brass stamps. As the carriage passes it, you feel a small sensation like a bubble popping. The forest hush gives way to friendly chatter, tavern music, and smiling faces turning to wave you in. The trees are still colossal, but here the air feels safe. What do you do?
gmNotes: Hush people are sincere. Company marks are the unease.

slides.gmScript: Say: "That bubble-pop is the ward. You just crossed into protected ground. If you arrived with mercy behind you, the welcome feels warmer. If the road behind you was bloodier, the welcome is polite but watchful."

sensorySummary: Low roofs, shoe lines, kitchen windows, repair benches, clover charms, and ward posts make the village feel guarded but lived in.
Mugs clink indoors, children whisper behind trusted adults, a distant work song falters when the ward hum misses a beat.
Bread, wet clover, hearth smoke, clean laundry, and a mineral edge from ward fixtures working too hard.
Packed earth is softened by moss; doorframes are polished by hands; the air warms near kitchens and cools near ward posts.
People notice everything without making a scene. Dogs, children, elders, and workers keep adjusting around the party's choices.

Children watch from behind people they trust; nobody runs, but nobody relaxes until the party proves how they arrived.

Corporate plaques use the trademarked name, while locals speak around it like an old irritation.
hazards: Contract-first posture cools trust.

Too much pressure about the ward makes locals go quiet.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The roleplay and breather hub. A warded village of warmth and music where the party must find the Whitefire Custodian by talking to locals. This is the social heart of the one-shot — three named NPCs, a vertical tavern, an optional festival, and the strongest "ask the players to build it with you" beat in the module.
locationSlideModel.readAloud: The path leads deeper until a tall stone pillar rises beside the road — carved top to bottom in old dwarven symbols, studded with small brass compliance stamps. It marks one corner of Hush Community Enclave. As your carriage passes the marker, you feel a small sensation, like a bubble popping, and the forest's hush gives way to the sound of people: friendly chatter, lively music drifting from a tavern at the center of town. The trees here are the same colossal preserve-trees, but the air feels safe, comforting. Smiling faces turn as you roll in, waving, calling warm greetings. Somewhere in this town is the Custodian you were sent to find. What do you do?

sensoryStack.detail: Carved dwarven ward-pillar with brass compliance stamps; lantern-strung branches; a tavern (the Clover Co-op) built up the trunk of an ancient tree; shoes hung on a line across the bar's ground floor.
Music, laughter, good-natured conversation, the creak of the tavern's wooden levels.
Ask the players (canon, p.32): "What smell permeates the air throughout this place?" Pre-loaded fallback : woodsmoke, fresh bread, spilled ale, moss.
The "bubble pop" of crossing the ward; warmth; safety after the road.
Children lighting lanterns in the branches; a clank playing an unknown card-and-acorn game; a bearded dwarf hauling an ale barrel on one shoulder.

gmDetails.title: Named NPCs (GM-only, canon p.32)
gmDetails.body:
Fidget — Wildborne Human, they/them. A young child who will not stop wiggling; scurries up trees lighting lanterns; knows the fastest routes through town; curious what life is like outside Hush.
Lausa Standworth — Wildborne Dwarf, she/her. Older woman, thick beard, hauls an ale barrel on her shoulder the entire conversation. Wants to know the name of every party member's weapon and the date it was forged.
Halython Fives — Loreborne Clank (humanoid robot), he/him. Soft-spoken, scratches on one metal shoulder where a friendly fox-bat perches. Plays an unknown card-and-acorn game. Asks about the Bramble Union.
Use one to make first contact, a second as the friend who knows where the Custodian lives.

gmDetails.title: OPTIONAL — The Firstmoss Launch Festival (canon, p.32)
gmDetails.body: If the party arrives early, Hush is mid-festival: the Sunless Farms crops have grown their first moss layer (ripening for the season). Arm-wrestling competition, a stone-painting class, a small marketplace of homemade trinkets. A full breather scene if the table wants downtime.

hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: Hush's dependence on corporate stewardship is partly engineered, even though the community's warmth is real.
Do not explain the scheme here; let the ward's comfort and fragility sit side by side.

sensorySummary: A polished official sign and neat route stones frame a village that keeps interrupting the label with charms, scuffed paths, and hand repairs.
The entry ward hums unevenly; someone inside laughs, then lowers their voice; a sign chain taps in the damp wind.
Damp paint, moss, warm bread from deeper in town, and the brass smell of a ward fixture under strain.
The sign is smooth and cold; the handmade charms are waxed, rough, and thumb-worn from being touched.
Locals move through the entrance by habit, using the paths they trust instead of the lines the sign wants them to use.
visibleDetails: A polished sign uses the trademarked name; someone has hung a hand-painted clover charm over one corner.
The route stones are neat near the entrance and messier where residents actually walk.
subtleDetails: Locals do not correct the name every time; they choose when the correction matters.
The cleanest sign is also the least touched object in view.
hazards: Using the official label casually chills local warmth.
Pushing records too hard makes watchers close the room.

player.say: "The sign is official and newer than the place. The locals mostly ignore it."
player.ask: "You can ask what locals call the village, study the marks, or move deeper toward the warm parts of town."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The sign frames the gap between a living place and a managed asset.
story.say: "The village feels older, warmer, and more stubborn than the label trying to sit on it."
story.ask: "Sharp read: the paperwork is not decoration. It records protection as infrastructure."
story.deeper: This is a seed for later reveals; it should create suspicion, not an answer key.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Instinct or Knowledge can turn signage into a clue.
mechanic.say: "Instinct 13 catches who watches you notice the sign. Knowledge 13 reads what the stamps legally describe."
mechanic.ask: "A success can set hush_clues=corporate_seam or ward_awareness=seed."

sensorySummary: Green lanterns, damp banners, mossfruit baskets, children's game stones, and adults keeping lanes clear without calling it guarding.
Work songs, clapping, small feet on mud, griddle hiss, and the sudden dip in music whenever the ward hum catches wrong.
Sweet mossfruit, hot griddle cakes, trampled clover, rain on lantern paper, and smoke from cookfires kept low.
Mud is springy under moss; ribbons brush faces; lantern paper goes soft at the edges in the wet air.
This is joy with watchfulness inside it. Let children, cooks, elders, and workers make the stakes visible before the crisis.

sensorySummary: Blue-green rows grow in shade beds under low roofs, with water paths, survey stakes, tool hooks, and crop markers only locals read quickly.
Irrigation trickles under boards, insects drone in the damp rows, and farmers pause whenever a weak ward post changes pitch.
Mushroom loam, damp leaves, cold channel water, cut stems, and the mineral bite of mosslit irrigation.
Soil is soft, dark, and springy; leaves feel waxy from low light; tool handles are polished by wet hands.
Field workers, insects, and crop behavior are the warning system. The farms should feel intelligent, not quaint.
visibleDetails: Blue-green rows grow in carefully shaded beds.
Farm tools hang under low roofs where rain and sap cannot ruin them.
subtleDetails: The healthiest crops cluster near older local water paths.
Corporate survey stakes stand where no farmer would plant.
hazards: Rushing damages irrigation.
Too many corporate questions make crews stop talking.
The route south is unclear without local guidance.

slides.gmGoal: Run the Co-op as a social hub: shoe custom, regulars, games, tavern prompts, and trust-building.
slides.publicObjective: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
slides.readAloud: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is the room where Hush decides whether the party belongs for tonight. Offer shoes, food, a game, and one regular by description before name."
gmReadAloud: Tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, and chipped mugs.
A room full of people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
gmChecklist: Offer the shoe line.
Use at least one regular.
Ask one tavern-building prompt.
Let the room react to bramble_outcome if it comes up.
gmPrivate: Halython's Bramble question is a clean carry-in read; use it only once the table is settled enough for it to matter.
slides.playerTakeaway: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
slides.storyTakeaway: The Co-op turns Hush from a destination into people with customs and boundaries.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Presence, Prepare/Hope, and table spotlight are enough to make this scene mechanically alive.

entities.name: Clover Co-op
entities.summary: Warm lamps, clover doors, shared bowls, and dry jokes make the Clover Co-op feel like Hush's stubborn heartbeat.
entities.role: Make hospitality practical, specific, and emotionally risky.
entities.personality: The social heart of Hush; shoes get polished and filled with trinkets.; introduce it with a sensory palette, who feels safe there, and what has been neglected.
entities.wants: Pull player attention toward the choices, clues, and relationships tied to Hush, Yera Mossglass, Firstmoss Launch Festival.
entities.sampleLine: The social heart of Hush; shoes get polished and filled with trinkets.

entities.name: Fidget
entities.summary: A restless child who knows fast routes through the village and asks blunt questions.
entities.role: Warm local guide and pace reset.
entities.playerDisplayCaption: a restless child guide who knows the fastest ways through the village
entities.personality: Restless, sharp, and starved to be useful before the grown-ups decide the useful part is over. Reads people fast and forgives slow. The bead strings are a walking map only Fidget can fully read: blue for water, brass for tolls, bone-white for the places adults say children should not go.

mapData.caption: Visual reference for Clover Co-op.
mapData.playerText: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
mapData.readAloud: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
mapData.gmGoal: Run the Co-op as a social hub: shoe custom, regulars, games, tavern prompts, and trust-building.
sensorySummary: Mismatched chairs face inward, shoe lines mark the threshold, and gift shelves hold jars, cloth, ribbons, and careful generosity.
Tea pours, mugs knock softly, someone clears their throat before hard news, and a ward chime outside lands a little flat.
Clover honey, tea steam, wet boot leather, old wood warmed by bodies, and food stretched with pride instead of abundance.
Counters are nicked smooth; mugs are chipped in familiar places; wool sleeves stay damp near the door.
The room tracks manners. People make space, stop talking, resume talking, and decide whether the party is safe to feed.
visibleDetails: Mismatched chairs face the room instead of the door.
Shoes, jars, folded cloth, and festival ribbons sit in tidy little systems that locals understand immediately.
subtleDetails: People notice who says thank you and who reaches before being offered.
The gift shelves are sparse but maintained with pride.
hazards: Taking hospitality as entitlement lowers trust.
Road news can turn warmth into grief.
Mocking customs closes doors.

checks.prompt: Presence 10 if uncertain; automatic if the player simply leans into it.
Instinct 12: who wants to talk, who protects someone, who is watching the package.
Finesse or Knowledge 12 if a player joins Halython's game.

fearSpends: A familiar item from the road is recognized.
A gift is offered with hands that shake.
The ward chime outside flattens while everyone pretends not to hear it.

sensoryStack.detail: Stacked levels, shoe lines, lanterns, gift shelves, and mismatched mugs.
Music, laughter, clacking game pieces, a fox-bat chirp.
Tea, wet boot leather, clover honey, old wood warmed by bodies.
Warm, public, generous, and carefully bounded.
People notice thank-yous, impatience, and who reaches before being offered.

mapData.gmOrientation: A vertical tree-tavern and public room. Ground floor shoe line, upper levels shaped by player answers, quiet games nook, bar, gift shelf, and the regulars.
mapData.gmScript: Say: "This is the room where Hush decides whether the party belongs for tonight. Offer shoes, food, a game, and one regular by description before name."
gmReadAloud: Tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, and chipped mugs.
A room full of people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
gmChecklist: Offer the shoe line.
Use at least one regular.
Ask one tavern-building prompt.
Let the room react to bramble_outcome if it comes up.
gmPrivate: Halython's Bramble question is a clean carry-in read; use it only once the table is settled enough for it to matter.

slides.title: Local Clues
slides.alt: Local Clues scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
slides.caption: Local clues make the infrastructure failure personal and specific.
slides.gmGoal: Run the objective spine: talk to locals, build trust, find the route to the person who keeps Hush safe, and seed the watched/corporate unease.
slides.publicObjective: Find someone who can point you toward the person who keeps the ward working.
slides.readAloud: The town is happy to talk. Everyone seems to know the person you are looking for, though they are protective of her. A friendly local can point the way, if the town decides you are safe enough to send toward someone it loves.
gmNotes: S03-02 must set custodian_route; this is the Act 3 to Act 4 hinge.
Bramble truth learned makes sharper questions land; if false, let contradictions still be visible.
slides.gmScript: Say: "They know who you mean, but they do not hand beloved people to strangers just because the strangers have a contract. Talk to them. Let them decide whether you are guests, customers, or trouble."
gmReadAloud: The town is happy to talk.
Everyone seems to know the person you are looking for, though they are protective of her.
A friendly local can point the way, if the town decides you are safe enough.
gmChecklist: Use description before NPC names: wiggling lantern-child, bearded ale-hauler, quiet clank with a fox-bat.
Set custodian_route by trust: safe, dangerous, or unknown.
Set hush_clues when the party earns a route, ward seed, corporate seam, farm seed, or market rumor.
If players push on the ward/company, offer one brave thread and one watched-room cost.
gmPrivate: Hush is watched. A brave local can hint at official paperwork, managed farms, or nervous ward maintenance, then shut down when a minder is near.
Do not name the full ward economy or the Keystone. The strongest player-safe phrase is: the ward keeps Hush safe, and people are worried about it.
slides.playerTakeaway: The way to the keeper runs through the town's trust, not through contract authority.
slides.storyTakeaway: Hush will help the party reach the person it protects, but only after the party treats Hush like people.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: This is social investigation: Presence earns directions, Instinct reads what gets dodged, and Knowledge reads ward or infrastructure clues.

entities.role: Warm local guide and pace reset.
entities.playerDisplayCaption: a restless child guide who knows the fastest ways through the village

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: The way to the keeper runs through the town's trust, not through contract authority.
player.say: "Be someone they would send to a beloved protector. That is the route."
player.ask: "A gentle question, a favor, honest road news, or joining a local custom can earn directions. A demand gets you only vague southward pointing."
player.deeper: Specific next actions: talk to the lantern-child, the ale-hauler, the quiet clank, a market seller, a farm worker, or whoever responded warmly to the party.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Hush will help the party reach the person it protects, but only after the party treats Hush like people.
story.say: "They are not hiding her to be difficult. They are protecting somebody who protects them."
story.ask: "Low trust means: south, past the farms. Neutral trust means a clear path. High trust means a guide and the safe irrigation route."
story.deeper: This is the act hinge. The story payoff is not just finding a location; it is whether the town vouches for the party before Act 4.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: This is social investigation: Presence earns directions, Instinct reads what gets dodged, and Knowledge reads ward or infrastructure clues.
mechanic.say: "Presence earns the route. Instinct catches the dodge. Knowledge reads the ward marks and logistics. Pick the tool that matches what you actually do."
mechanic.ask: "For directions, use Presence 12 if uncertain. For the watched/corporate seam, use Instinct or Knowledge 13. Success sets custodian_route or ward_awareness."
mechanic.deeper: Record the mechanical consequence immediately: custodian_route safe/dangerous/unknown, ward_awareness none/seed/aware, and hush_clues for what they learned.

slides.title: The Clover Co-op
slides.alt: The Clover Co-op scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
slides.caption: The Clover Co-op gives the party hospitality, texture, and reasons to care.
slides.gmGoal: Use the vertical tavern as Hush's social heart: shoe custom, named locals, player-authored details, and a chance to belong.
slides.publicObjective: Rest, connect, and become someone the town trusts.
slides.readAloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree, level stacked on level, crowded with music and good-natured noise. A friendly local stops you at the door: newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor. By the time you leave, locals promise, the shoes come back shined and filled with little trinkets. Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait. What do you do?
gmNotes: This scene is relationship, not objective extraction. Slow down and let players be people.
Do not turn hospitality into shopping inventory; use gifts as story boons.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is Hush's living room. Hang your shoes if you want to honor the custom. Pick a face, pick a table, or tell me one thing this tavern has that no tavern outside Hush would have."
gmReadAloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree.
Newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor.
Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait.
gmChecklist: Offer the shoe custom and reward it later with polished, trinket-filled shoes.
Describe Fidget, Lausa, and Halython before naming them.
Ask one player-authored tavern prompt.
Offer Prepare/Hope as a quiet breather.
Let Halython ask about the road outcome when the moment is warm.
gmPrivate: Halython's Bramble question lets bramble_outcome affect trust without lore-dumping.
Even the tavern has small protective wards; Marlowe can notice this.
slides.playerTakeaway: This is the warm center of the act: a place to be people before being couriers again.
slides.storyTakeaway: Belonging in Hush is offered through customs, food, games, and careful attention.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Downtime is mechanical here: Prepare/Hope, Presence, and respectful roleplay can raise hush_trust and unlock a guide.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: This is the warm center of the act: a place to be people before being couriers again.
player.say: "Put the job down for a minute. Be a person. Hush is watching kindly."
player.ask: "You can hang your shoes, share a drink, play the clank's card-and-acorn game, talk weapons with the ale-hauler, follow the lantern-child, or take a quiet Prepare beat."
player.deeper: Give players one named table action at a time: shoes, drink, game, conversation, quiet rest, or ask-the-players tavern detail.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Belonging in Hush is offered through customs, food, games, and careful attention.
story.say: "They are not testing you with a form. They are seeing whether you can be gentle with their home."
story.ask: "Halython may ask what happened with the road attackers. A mercy answer warms the room. A bloody answer makes people quieter."
story.deeper: Let the Bramble carry-in affect faces and tone, not a lecture. The town can be kind and still judge the party's choices.

slides.title: Firstmoss Launch Festival
slides.alt: Firstmoss Launch Festival scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
slides.caption: Firstmoss makes the stakes joyous before the module asks the party to defend them.
slides.gmGoal: Offer the optional reward arc: a joyful festival, low-stakes contests, a concrete boon, and one quiet seed about the farms.
slides.publicObjective: Join the celebration if you want, earn goodwill, and gather what helps for the road ahead.
slides.readAloud: You have arrived during the Firstmoss Launch Festival. The town celebrates the season's first moss rising on the Sunless Farms crops, the promise of fresh fruit and full tables ahead. There is a good-natured arm-wrestling competition, a stone-painting class, and a small market of homemade trinkets. The whole village feels lighter for a moment. What do you do?
gmNotes: The festival is the act's exhale before the Act 4 turn.
Boon examples: charm, favor token, useful market find, or goodwill that opens a door later.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This festival is optional, but it is real. If you join in, Hush remembers. Arm-wrestle, paint a stone, browse the market, dance badly, ask about the farms, or skip it and keep moving."
gmReadAloud: You have arrived during the Firstmoss Launch Festival.
There is arm-wrestling, stone-painting, and a small market of homemade trinkets.
The whole village feels lighter for a moment.
gmChecklist: Frame festival participation as optional.
Grant a concrete festival_boon for sincere participation or a contest win.
Let Khari/Varian/Barnacle/Marlowe hooks surface if those PCs are in play.
Only seed the farm/corporate thread if a player probes it.
Route back toward S03-02/MAP-LOC-hush-farms when ready.
gmPrivate: The Sunless Farms are managed infrastructure. Seed through crops, schedules, and volunteer precision; do not explain the ward economy.
Skipping the festival is an opportunity cost, not a punishment.
slides.playerTakeaway: You get one genuinely good day; taking part can give the party goodwill and a small boon.
slides.storyTakeaway: Hush's abundance is real and joyful, even if a curious player may notice how carefully it is managed.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Low-stakes mechanics still matter: Strength, Finesse, Presence, market choices, and Prepare/Hope can all produce a festival_boon.

likes_dislikes.likes: Warm bread wrapped for the road, clean tack, and couriers who remember names.

block2.likes: Warm bread wrapped for the road, clean tack, and couriers who remember names.
block2.dislikes: Company euphemisms for death, cracked cheap wards, and anyone pawing through her things without care.
block2.favorite_thing: The little home-token at her neck, thumb-polished from nervous road miles.
block2.loved_ones: A family or household back along the courier road; name them only if the table searches or asks what the token means.
block2.day_to_day: Up before dawn, checking straps, route tags, and ward charms, then walking beside the cart until the wheels found a trustworthy groove.
block2.appearance: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair. Full-body reference: Full-body standing halfling courier in a practical traveling coat with satchel and route tags, weary kind posture, road-dust browns, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Debt-squeezed contractor; the care in her coat repairs shows she kept useful things alive long past their company warranty.
block2.animal_companion: No beast survived the wreck. Her closest road companion was the cart team and the route bell.
block2.physical: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A tired courier with a blue scarf, patched leather, route charms, and a pale scar near the jaw looks like someone who kept walking long after the road stopped being fair.
block2.voice_style: She has no voice left. Let her speak through objects: the order of her route charms, the wear on a strap, a half-finished note. The table supplies her tone, and it should ache.
block2.body_language: The scene should read quiet and intimate, not grisly: a person interrupted mid-duty.
block2.quirks: Her route charms are arranged by people, not places.
block2.image_lore: The jaw scar came from an axle splinter on her first winter route. She kept the scarf because the person who bandaged her told her couriers should be seen before they are counted.
block2.npc_relationships: Other couriers would recognize her patched style, route knots, and careful manifest marks.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She cannot respond, so the scene asks the PCs to treat evidence as a person's last testimony.
block3.persuasion_levers: No persuasion. Instinct 12 or Knowledge 12 turns the wound, ward, and debt slip into the playable answer: this was made to look wild.

what_moves_them.result: The body and ground contradict a simple animal attack.
The debt slip points toward pressure bigger than one route.

block3.combat_lever: The playable lever is careful evidence handling and mercy toward what did not kill her.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

A ledger shows protection costs and hazard sightings climbing together.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You get one genuinely good day; taking part can give the party goodwill and a small boon.
player.say: "You have earned one good day. Spend a little of it here, and Hush may send something useful with you."
player.ask: "You can arm-wrestle, paint a stone, browse the market, ask about Firstmoss, or skip the festival and keep moving toward the keeper."
player.deeper: The player-facing choice is participation vs. momentum. Both are valid; only participation grants the boon.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Hush's abundance is real and joyful, even if a curious player may notice how carefully it is managed.
story.say: "The joy is real. The food is real. A curious mind may still wonder who runs the farms that make it possible."
story.ask: "Player-safe answer: Firstmoss is the first ripening layer on the Sunless Farms crops. Sharp read: the farms run with unusual precision."
story.deeper: Seed managed abundance through detail only: schedules, crops, volunteers, branded stall, and people going quiet near official questions.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Low-stakes mechanics still matter: Strength, Finesse, Presence, market choices, and Prepare/Hope can all produce a festival_boon.
mechanic.say: "Arm-wrestling is Strength 12. Stone-painting or graceful mingling can be Finesse or Presence 12. A probing farm read is Instinct or Knowledge 13."
mechanic.ask: "A win or sincere contribution earns a boon: charm, favor, market find, or goodwill. Set festival_boon when it happens."
mechanic.deeper: Use this beat to show that mechanics can reward joy, not only danger. The delayed payoff is a spendable social or practical edge.

block1.name: Whitefire Custodian
block1.one_line: an old faerie-like ward keeper whose exhaustion glows around the edges
block1.game_role: Trust gate, ritual guide, and person the party can protect without owning.
block1.critical_info: The Custodian must carry the reveal; Marlowe can only add recognition, not replace her.
block1.disposition_default: Dry, tired, luminous, and warmer when treated as a person.
block1.the_lever: Respect her name, her consent, and the cost she has already paid.

block2.wants_now: Renew the ward without being treated as a device.
block2.larger_motivation: Keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember safety can be care instead of product.
block2.wants: Renew the ward without being treated as a device.
block2.motivation: Keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember safety can be care instead of product.
block2.personality: Ancient kindness running on fumes, glowing a little brighter whenever someone tells the truth nearby. Wants to keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember that safety can be care instead of a product, and is quietly breaking under the cost of it.
voice: Please do not call me the ward interface.
A contract can move a package. It cannot decide what a life is worth.
If you are here to help, stand where help costs you something.
block2.secrets: The ward's cost is personal, and the deepest economy behind that cost is worse than she will say unless trust and understanding are earned.
block2.fears: The stone waking hungry, the Relay failing, and being remembered as infrastructure instead of a person.

likes_dislikes.likes: Names spoken carefully, consent, patience, and brave people who admit fear.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Being called an interface, rushed rituals, and corporate ownership language.

block2.likes: Names spoken carefully, consent, patience, and brave people who admit fear.
block2.dislikes: Being called an interface, rushed rituals, and corporate ownership language.
block2.favorite_thing: A tiny bell charm she rings once when a ward line steadies.
block2.loved_ones: Other keepers, mostly gone or distant; the Relay Keeper matters as a person, not a destination.
block2.day_to_day: Tends failing ward threads, trims light from old knots, speaks to quiet bells, and sleeps only when the ward hum changes.
block2.appearance: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest. Full-body reference: Full-body tall luminous faerie custodian, wings folded, warm gold-green glow under translucent skin, gentle commanding presence, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Ancient and materially spare; the beauty around her is duty, not luxury.
block2.animal_companion: No animal; moths and fireflies gather around her light like worried attendants.
block2.physical: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest.
block2.voice_style: Luminous and weary; speaks in slow, true sentences and flinches at being called equipment.
block2.body_language: Ancient gentleness held upright by duty.
block2.quirks: Answers transactional questions with questions about fear, memory, or cost.
block2.image_lore: The branch-crown grew after the Custodian chose to stay with the ward instead of leaving with the old keepers. It blooms brighter when someone tells the truth without advantage.
block2.npc_relationships: She can care for every PC; Marlowe only gets a recognition beat, never ownership of the reveal.

slides.title: Act Four: The Hanging Office
slides.caption: The Custodian and the Hanging Office turn the delivery into a choice.
slides.gmGoal: Turn the courier job into a calling. The party reaches the person who can receive the package, learns what it really is, and chooses whether to carry the danger forward.
slides.publicObjective: Find the Custodian, deliver the package, and learn what comes next.
slides.readAloud: The town thins behind you, fields giving way to forest again. The trees here wear faces, hundreds of them carved into the bark, eyes turned every direction. Somewhere past them lives the person you were sent to find. After everything the road asked of you, the last stretch is the strangest. Whatever is in that crate, you are about to learn why it mattered enough to send a crew to die for it.
gmNotes: High mercy, high Hush trust, and a safe route make the Custodian warmer and more candid.
Low trust, dangerous route, or blood-debt makes the carved faces feel watchful and the Custodian more guarded.
slides.playerTakeaway: The simple job is over; what you do next is the actual story.
slides.storyTakeaway: This is where a delivery becomes a reason: the party learns what they carried and why it matters.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Act 4 runs on social trust, arcane discovery, and a preparation decision that sets the Act 5 ritual pressure.

slides.title: Through the Farms
slides.alt: Through the Farms scene art for The Hanging Office.
slides.caption: The road through the farms shifts the story from delivery job to stewardship problem.
slides.gmGoal: Cross from Hush farmland into the carved-face preserve edge and pay off the route the party earned.
slides.publicObjective: Reach the Custodian's home.
slides.readAloud: Past the last homes of the village, the crops change: fruits and vegetables wear a thin layer of glowing blue moss that pulses softly with warmth as you pass. Then the cultivated land ends, and the preserve returns. The great trees here have faces, hundreds of them, carved into every side. Ahead, something hangs in the canopy: a cabin, swaying gently, suspended over a counterweight stone the size of a cabin itself.
gmNotes: This is the Act 3 to Act 4 consequence handoff: route quality changes approach pressure.
The alternate hazard is minor and non-combat. Save lethal danger for Act 5.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is where the route you earned pays off. If Hush trusted you, the way is calm. If the route is dangerous or unknown, the preserve asks for one last bit of attention before the treehouse."
gmReadAloud: The crops wear a thin layer of glowing blue moss.
The cultivated land ends, and the preserve returns.
The great trees here have faces carved into every side.
gmChecklist: Read custodian_route before framing the path.
Safe route: guided calm, no roll.
Dangerous/unknown route: Instinct 13 or one minor Stress-level preserve hazard.
If strixwolf_blood_debt is true, make the carved faces feel hostile.
If package_status=lost, the approach can continue but the normal reveal is blocked.
gmPrivate: The carved faces are ward anchors. Seed them as texture now; let the Custodian explain later.
The moss shares the ward's magic. Do not explain the cost here.
slides.playerTakeaway: You are leaving safe ground and approaching something old and watchful.
slides.storyTakeaway: The Custodian's home sits at the strange heart of the preserve, where the ward's protection becomes visible.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: custodian_route gates the approach: safe route skips the obstacle, dangerous or unknown route asks for Instinct 13 or costs 1 Stress.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

sensorySummary: Hanging cabin, giant rope braid, carved counterweight boulder, yellow-green window light, trees covered in hundreds of carved watching faces, blue glowing moss starting on the nearby crops.
The slow creak of the swaying cabin; the Custodian's clear, expressive voice once she emerges; a low hum from the carved faces when the wind moves.
potions, dried herbs, beeswax, old wood — a cluttered-but-precise workshop.
Uncanny watchfulness (the faces); the cabin's gentle motion; the sense that nothing here is accidental.
Small creatures of all kinds inside the cabin; potion bottles, spellbooks, runes, plants — crowded but immaculately ordered.
visibleDetails: Ropes, ladders, stamped forms, hanging planters, and a rune-marked counterweight keep the office suspended.
Paperwork is everywhere, but so are tea cups, patched gloves, and practical repairs.
subtleDetails: The safest path is the one worn by locals, not the one marked for visitors.
The counterweight has more inspection tags than maintenance marks.
hazards: Cutting the rope costs 1 Stress.
Stealing or mocking her home lowers custodian_trust.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The reveal scene. The party meets the Whitefire Custodian — a seven-foot humanoid-firefly faerie — delivers the sealed crate, and learns the truth: it holds the Keystone Asset, the ward-stone for the entire capital city. Her home is a puzzle-toy that folds open like a flower. This is the emotional and expository pivot from "courier job" to "save the ward."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: Making your way past the village homes and through the farmland, you find the Custodian's home — though "home" undersells it. A cabin hangs from a braid of rope as thick around as a giant's forearm, tied to a massive branch and counterweighted by a cabin-sized boulder resting at the tree's base. The whole thing sways gently, like overripe fruit ready to drop. The boulder is carved with symbols; the cabin windows flicker with a soft yellow-green light. And the preserve-trees here are different — hundreds of faces carved into their trunks on every side, eyes peering in every direction. What do you do?

gmDetails.title: The Whitefire Custodian (GM-only, canon p.33)
gmDetails.body:
Form: Seven-foot mix of humanoid and firefly; moves in slow-then-suddenly-jerky faerie motions. Face hard to read, but her voice carries all her emotion. Old but spry, mischievous.
Voice sample (canon): "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my, you're rather late, aren't you. Come in, come in."
Manner: Curious about their journey, who directed them to her, and — pointedly — how each of them imagines they might die one day. She notices if a single item in her home is moved an inch.

gmDetails.title: The Package reveal (CANON — read aloud, p.33)
gmDetails.body:
Inside Emeris Crown Holdings' package lies a massive stone with a lion's face carved into it. Marlowe — you recognize this as the Keystone Asset from the capital city's main archway.
The Custodian: "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery secret. If anyone knew your city was no longer warded, you would be conquered before sunrise." Then: "We must travel to the Open Vale Ritual Site to revitalize the ward. Such an effort of magic will attract dangerous creatures from the darkest reaches of the preserve. I'll need your help."

hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: the Custodian may be a true believer being used, a partial witness, or both.
Her fear of the Forgotten Gods should not erase the corporate-sounding texture around the Keystone and ward economy.

slides.title: The Hanging Office Exterior
slides.alt: The Hanging Office Exterior scene art for The Hanging Office.
slides.caption: The Hanging Office is absurd because the system is absurd; the people inside are not.
slides.gmGoal: Run the hanging-home puzzle as a gentle test of patience, courtesy, and cleverness.
slides.publicObjective: Get the Custodian's attention or reach her home.
slides.readAloud: Up close, cabin undersells it. A home hangs from a braid of rope as thick as a giant's forearm, tied to a massive branch and counterweighted by a boulder the size of the cabin itself. The whole thing sways like overripe fruit ready to drop. The boulder is carved with symbols; the windows flash a soft yellow-green light. There is no obvious door at ground level. What do you do?
gmNotes: The goal is not to stump the table. Let the puzzle reveal what kind of guests they are.
Destructive force lowers trust; gentle strength or patient honesty raises it.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is not a lock to force. It is a person to convince. Call up, climb, study the counterweight, or wait and announce yourselves honestly."
gmReadAloud: A home hangs from a braid of rope as thick as a giant's forearm.
A boulder the size of the cabin counterweights it at the tree's base.
The windows flash with soft yellow-green light.
gmChecklist: Offer all three module options: call, cut the rope, climb.
Cutting the rope blasts them back and costs 1 Stress.
Climbing is Agility 13; failure means a limb gently sets them down.
Clever/courteous solutions nudge custodian_trust up.
festival_boon can help charm or signal her.
gmPrivate: She emerges on something worthy: patience, courtesy, cleverness, restraint, or genuine vulnerability.
Keep consequences whimsical and non-lethal.
slides.playerTakeaway: The way in is to be the kind of people worth opening the door for.
slides.storyTakeaway: The Custodian tests character before access; her home answers courtesy faster than force.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: This is a forgiving puzzle with real cost: call, climb, study, or force it; force costs Stress while cleverness raises custodian_trust.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."

The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

story.statement: The Custodian tests character before access.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: Up close, cabin undersells it. A home hangs from a braid of rope as thick as a giant's forearm, tied to a massive branch and counterweighted by a boulder the size of the cabin itself. slides.title: The Whitefire Custodian
slides.alt: The Whitefire Custodian scene art for The Hanging Office.
slides.caption: The Whitefire Custodian is a person, not the adventure's magical help desk.
slides.gmGoal: Deliver the Custodian as the RP heart of Act 4 and let the party earn her trust before the reveal.
slides.publicObjective: Win the Custodian's confidence and hand over the package.
slides.readAloud: The home lowers, and from it steps a being seven feet tall: part humanoid, part firefly, moving in slow drifts broken by sudden jerky motions. Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly. She eyes your group with open mischief. "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my. You are rather late, are you not? Come in, come in." Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should, packed with potion bottles, spellbooks, runes, plants, and small creatures. None of it is messy. You get the sense that if you moved a single item an inch, she would know.
gmNotes: This scene is pure RP with stakes. Dice are optional; trust is not optional.
Per-character hooks belong in perCharacterLayer, not in these notes.
slides.gmScript: Say: "She is warm, weird, ancient, and deciding right now who you are. She rewards honesty and curiosity. Meet her strangeness with warmth and she will meet yours."
gmReadAloud: A seven-foot being steps from the hanging home: part humanoid, part firefly.
Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly.
Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should.
gmChecklist: Describe before naming: seven-foot firefly-faerie first, Whitefire Custodian after she names herself.
Ask about the journey, who sent them, and how they imagine they might die.
Read hush_trust, bramble_truth_learned, strixwolf_blood_debt, and custodian_route.
Set custodian_trust from warmth, honesty, restraint, and answers.
Do not reveal the package truth until S04-04.
gmPrivate: Her knowledge stance is a Kyle canon flag. Play her as warm and guarded; do not resolve whether she fully knows the ward cost.
If strixwolf_blood_debt is true, she can gently name that the forest has been watching the party with teeth.
slides.playerTakeaway: Be genuine with her and she becomes your greatest ally; be cold and she gives only what she must.
slides.storyTakeaway: The person the job served is strange, ancient, warm, and bound to the safety everyone has been circling.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: custodian_trust is the mechanic: warmth, honest answers, restraint, and curiosity decide how much candor and help she gives.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The home lowers, and from it steps a being seven feet tall: part humanoid, part firefly, moving in slow drifts broken by sudden jerky motions. Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly. She eyes your group with open mischief. "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my. You are rather late, are you not? Come in, come in." Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should, packed with potion bottles, spellbooks, runes, plants, and small creatures. None of it is messy. You get the sense that if you moved a single item an inch, she would know.

slides.title: The Keystone Reveal
slides.alt: The Keystone Reveal scene art for The Hanging Office.
slides.caption: The Keystone Asset stops being cargo and becomes a communal protection problem.
slides.gmGoal: Route the package reveal through the Custodian, not Marlowe, and set keystone_understanding.
slides.publicObjective: Learn what the package is and what must be done.
slides.readAloud: The Custodian unfolds her home like a blossoming flower and draws the crate inside, sealing it open again as a workshop. She breaks the seal. Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face. She goes still, then nods, slow and grave. "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery quiet," she says. "This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward. If the route knew what you carried, every hungry thing in the preserve would follow the scent of it." The light in her home dims as she speaks. "We must take it to the Open Vale and revitalize the ward before Hush has to trust paper promises instead of protection. That much magic will draw dangerous things from the deep preserve. I will need your help."
gmNotes: This is the controlled spoiler release. Earlier player text must not have named the Keystone Asset.
Players can react before choosing prep. Do not rush the table out of shock.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The Custodian carries this reveal. Marlowe can recognize a personal detail if she is present, but the truth does not depend on any one PC."
gmReadAloud: She breaks the seal.
Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face.
"This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward."
gmChecklist: Check package_status before starting; if lost, do not run this reveal as written.
Name Keystone Asset here for the first time in player text.
Route recognition through the Custodian.
Marlowe gets only an optional bonus recognition beat.
Set keystone_understanding surface/deep.
Seed, but do not explain, the deeper consume/soul-economy truth.
gmPrivate: If package_status=lost, stop the normal reveal and use only the Kyle-confirmed recovery branch when it exists.
The deepest truth is that the ward protects by consuming. In Act 4 this remains a seed, never a full explanation.
Calibrate her candor to custodian_trust and ward_awareness.
slides.playerTakeaway: The job was never small, and now you know why: you are being asked to finish it at real risk.
slides.storyTakeaway: The package was the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward, and renewing it will draw danger from the deep preserve.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: The reveal writes keystone_understanding: surface from hearing her, deep from Knowledge 14 or hard questions with high trust.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.

The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Keystone Reveal
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Keystone Reveal scene art for The Hanging Office.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The Keystone Asset stops being cargo and becomes a communal protection problem.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Learn what the package is and what must be done.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian unfolds her home like a blossoming flower and draws the crate inside, sealing it open again as a workshop. She breaks the seal. Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face. She goes still, then nods, slow and grave. "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery quiet," she says. "This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward. If the route knew what you carried, every hungry thing in the preserve would follow the scent of it." The light in her home dims as she speaks. "We must take it to the Open Vale and revitalize the ward before Hush has to trust paper promises instead of protection. That much magic will draw dangerous things from the deep preserve. I will need your help."
