slides.title: Toward Open Vale
slides.alt: Toward Open Vale scene art for The Hanging Office.
slides.caption: The final approach turns understanding into preparation.
slides.gmGoal: Convert the reveal into commitment, offer real preparation, and bridge to Act 5.
slides.publicObjective: Commit to the ritual and set out for the Open Vale.
slides.readAloud: The Custodian gathers what she needs with the brisk energy of someone much younger than she looks. "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged," she says. "It is where it must be renewed." She looks at each of you in turn. "I cannot do this alone, and what comes for us when the magic rises will not be gentle. But I think you already knew the job was bigger than a crate." When you are ready, the treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.
gmNotes: This is the bridge scene. The important output is state, not more lore.
A reluctant yes still counts if the party chooses the hard road with eyes open.
slides.gmScript: Say: "Before we go: you can rest, prepare, ask her what to expect, or spend any favor you earned. It all matters when the ritual starts."
gmReadAloud: "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged."
"I cannot do this alone."
The treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.
gmChecklist: Do not railroad the yes; let the stakes and trust carry it.
Offer prep: rest, learn the ritual, spend festival_boon or Hush favor, plan positions.
Set ritual_prep ready/unready.
Set final custodian_trust.
Set ward_stability fragile/stable for Act 5.
Use MAP-LOC-open-vale-ward-lines as the forward edge.
gmPrivate: Convergence math: high trust + deep understanding + ready prep = ward_stability stable. Otherwise fragile.
If package_status=lost, commitment can exist emotionally but Act 5 cannot proceed normally until the recovery branch is confirmed.
slides.playerTakeaway: You are choosing the hard road on purpose, and what you do before you walk it will keep you alive.
slides.storyTakeaway: The party chooses to finish what the job started, not just because of pay but because the stakes are now real.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Preparation is the mechanic: rest, learn, spend boons, and plan; ritual_prep and ward_stability set the Act 5 countdown pressure.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

playerSafeProjection.alt: Toward Open Vale scene art for The Hanging Office.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The final approach turns understanding into preparation.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Commit to the ritual and set out for the Open Vale.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian gathers what she needs with the brisk energy of someone much younger than she looks. "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged," she says. "It is where it must be renewed." She looks at each of you in turn. "I cannot do this alone, and what comes for us when the magic rises will not be gentle. But I think you already knew the job was bigger than a crate." When you are ready, the treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.

slides.title: Act Five: The Ward Renewal
slides.caption: The finale turns five acts of trust, mercy, preparation, and truth into one visible ritual outcome.
slides.gmGoal: Converge every prior choice into the ward renewal: protect the Custodian, make the countdown legible, resolve the ritual, and choose what truth leaves with the party.
slides.publicObjective: Protect the Custodian through the ritual, renew the ward, and finish what the job started.
slides.readAloud: The carriage pulls into a perfect circle of clearing, the only place in the preserve where the trees pull back and let you see the open sky. This is where it ends. The Custodian says the ward was first forged here, and here it must be renewed. She tells you it nearly killed her the first time. Then she smiles, old and unafraid, and asks you to stand with her while she does the most dangerous thing she knows how to do.
gmNotes: Act 5 is not a kill-all combat. It is protection under pressure until the countdown reaches 0.
Let prior mercy or trust become visible help: warning, charm, positioning, steadier Custodian, or a better aftermath.
If the fight drags, Market Correction can spawn easy skeletons so progress can resume without punishing beginners.
slides.playerTakeaway: You signed on for the hard road; this is the hard road. Stand with her and finish it.
slides.storyTakeaway: This is the resolution of everything: the ward, the city, the Custodian, and the choices that brought the party here.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Act 5 is a defense encounter on a countdown, then a report-choice epilogue gate.

gmBeats.label: Countdown
gmBeats.title: The visible clock
gmBeats.gmScript: Say: "Set the ritual countdown to 8. Each meaningful adversary defeat or pressure neutralized ticks it down by 1. Each Custodian hit or unprotected exposure ticks it up by 1. Clamp it between 0 and 10; at 0 the ward locks and the table moves to S05-07."
gmReadAloud: When the ritual begins, the countdown starts at 8. Defeat threats to move it down. Let the Custodian be hit, and it moves up.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You signed on for the hard road; this is the hard road. Stand with her and finish it.
player.say: "No more setup. This is the fight that ends the story. Protect her, hold the line, and see it through."
player.ask: "Take your last rest, ready your gear, and pick who you stand beside when it gets bad."
player.deeper: This is the player-facing finale thesis: shared courage, not lone-hero destiny.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: This is the resolution of everything: the ward, the city, the Custodian, and the choices that brought the party here.
story.say: "Every road you took leads to this clearing. What happens here is the ending you have been writing all along."
story.ask: "At stake: Hush, the Custodian, the ward, and what kind of truth survives the paperwork after you win."
story.deeper: Make carry-in flags visible through help, pressure, and aftermath, not as a list of variables read aloud.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Act 5 is a defense encounter on a countdown, then a report-choice epilogue gate.
mechanic.say: "A timed fight. She rituals, you hold the line. A countdown die runs the clock: defeat enemies to speed it, but every hit she takes slows it down."
mechanic.ask: "d8 starts at 8. Down 1 on adversary defeat or equivalent pressure neutralized. Up 1 when the Custodian is hit or exposed. At 0, the ritual completes."
mechanic.deeper: ward_stability and ritual_prep tune how forgiving the opening is; report_choice gates the Epilogue.

slides.title: The Open Vale Site
slides.alt: Old ritual clearing under open sky.
slides.caption: The quiet before the finale turns care, rest, and preparation into real protection.
slides.gmGoal: Arrive at the old ritual clearing, run the last Short Rest, and turn preparation into finale resources.
slides.publicObjective: Reach the ritual site, learn what is coming, and prepare.
slides.readAloud: The clearing is a perfect circle, the only break in the endless canopy: open sky above for the first time in days. The Custodian speaks softly as you arrive. This is where she first forged the ward pillars that keep Hush safe. She almost died doing it. Then her antennae perk in a disconcerting way. "This is good. Stop, here. Now come help me. I'm old." She begins to glow. "I'll need an hour. Enjoy the night air while you can. We'll be very busy soon."
gmNotes: This is the pressure valve before the finale. Give every player one prep spotlight before moving on.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is your last calm moment. Short Rest now: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, or Prepare for Hope. Pick two. If you Prepare together, you each get two Hope. I take 1d4 Fear during the rest."
gmReadAloud: The clearing is a perfect circle, the only break in the endless canopy.
The Custodian says this is where she first forged the ward pillars that keep Hush safe.
"I'll need an hour. Enjoy the night air while you can. We'll be very busy soon."
gmChecklist: Deliver the clearing and Custodian history beat.
Run Short Rest: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, Prepare.
Take 1d4 Fear during the rest.
If ritual_prep=ready, let a prepared PC preview the countdown before S05-02.
If package_status=lost, state that the ritual cannot proceed as written until a recovery/improvisation decision is made.
gmPrivate: The Forgotten Gods deflection is canon-facing; do not explain the deeper cost.
The player-facing site is warm Open Vale. Open Vale(TM) registration stays GM-only.
slides.playerTakeaway: This is the quiet before the worst of it; use it well.
slides.storyTakeaway: This clearing is where the ward was born and where it must be renewed, and the Custodian is risking herself again.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Short Rest is the final resource conversion: HP, Stress, Armor, Hope, ritual_prep, and GM Fear all change the fight.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The climax. A perfect circular clearing — the only break in the canopy — where the Custodian first forged Hush's ward pillars. The party takes a Short Rest, then defends her through the ward-renewal ritual against waves of skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths while a countdown die ticks. Win condition: survive until the ritual completes, not "kill everything."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: On the Custodian's direction, your carriage rolls into a clearing — a perfect circle, the only patch of the preserve where no trees block the open sky. Stars wheel overhead. This is the Open Vale Site. The Custodian's voice softens as she tells you she forged Hush's ward pillars here, on all four corners of the village — and that she nearly died doing it. She won't say more; something about angering the Forgotten Gods. Then her antennae perk in a way that unsettles you. "This is good. Stop, stop. Yes, here. Now come help me, I'm old." Her body begins to glow, flickering against the dark.

sensoryStack.detail: A flawless circular clearing, open sky (rare here), the Custodian glowing brighter and lifting the carriage a foot off the ground, eyes rolling back; later, skeletons clawing up from the earth and wraiths drifting in from the treeline.
The Custodian humming, then a shriek when the Keystone responds; unearthly screeches from the woods; rusted swords scraping free of the soil.
ozone, turned earth, cold air with no forest-damp — the clearing feels outside the preserve.
Charged, electric; the hair-raising sense of big magic; the open sky disorienting after days under canopy.
The Forgotten-Gods unease; the woods themselves seem to react to the arcane energy.

locationSlideModel.combatBlock:
The ritual countdown (p.35): Set a d8 to 8. Ticks down 1 each time an adversary is defeated; ticks up 1 each time the Custodian is hit. At 0, the ritual completes → Epilogue.
Setup (p.35): Custodian standee center; PCs around her; 4 Legacy Skeletons in Close range of her; 2 Soul-Audit Wraiths in Far range.
Legacy Skeleton — Tier 1 Standard (×4)
Rusted Sword: Melee, 1d6+1 phy · ATK +0 · Difficulty 12 · HP 2 · Stress 1 · Thresholds 7/none
Battle guide: roll d20 (no ATK mod) vs Evasion; hit → 1d6+1. Take 6 or less damage → mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated.
Group Attack (Feature): spend a Fear, move several skeletons into Melee, one shared attack roll at +0; on success deal 4 phy per skeleton, combined into one hit.
Soul-Audit Wraith — Tier 1 Bruiser (×2)
Lifedrain: Far, 2d6+8 mag · ATK +3 · Difficulty 13 · HP 6 · Stress 3 · Major 7 / Severe 14
Spectral Body (Passive): resistance to physical damage (incoming physical halved, round up).
Memory Delve (Action): attack a Close target; on hit, the wraith places a hand on their cheek — ask the player to describe a terrifying childhood moment — then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through (Action): spend a Fear, attack a Melee target; on success the PC is Untethered (can't act until the countdown ticks down). Whole party Untethered at once → all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition cleared.
Open Vale Site — Environment, Tier 1 Exploration
Feature Market Correction (Action): spend a Fear to summon 2 Legacy Skeletons within Very Close of a PC.
GM guidance (p.35): if the countdown stalls, use Market Correction to spawn easy skeletons. If no PC is in range, adversaries target the Custodian (Difficulty 11, narrative damage only). Death move (Quickstart): a PC at last HP falls unconscious until healed or the danger passes — not dead.
transitions: In: From the Treehouse (05), Act Five.
Out: Countdown hits 0 → ritual completes → the Keystone Asset epilogue (see 07 for the sequel hook).
locationSlideModel.canonSource: Countdown rules, all three stat blocks, the environment feature, Short Rest options, and GM guidance are module-canon (pp.34–35).
hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: Soul-Audit Wraiths and Legacy Skeletons read as corporate instruments, not natural spirits.
Run Memory Delve as extraction and the skeletons as repossessed/decommissioned labor logic, while keeping the reveal subtextual.

locationSlideModel.mechanicTakeaway: The win condition is the ritual countdown reaching 0, not clearing every adversary.

fearEvents: Environment Feature — Market Correction (canon): spend a Fear to summon two additional Legacy Skeletons from the ground within Very Close range of a PC. Use it to keep the countdown moving (skeletons die easily → countdown ticks down on each defeat).
The Wraiths' Memory Delve and Pass-Through are your big Fear spends — use Pass-Through sparingly (it can lock a PC out; if the whole party goes Untethered they all mark 2 HP and snap back).
Spend Fear: the open sky flickers — for one beat the stars rearrange wrongly (Forgotten Gods watching). Narrative dread, no mechanics.
mapData.combatBlock:
The ritual countdown (p.35): Set a d8 to 8. Ticks down 1 each time an adversary is defeated; ticks up 1 each time the Custodian is hit. At 0, the ritual completes → Epilogue.
Setup (p.35): Custodian standee center; PCs around her; 4 Legacy Skeletons in Close range of her; 2 Soul-Audit Wraiths in Far range.
Legacy Skeleton — Tier 1 Standard (×4)
Rusted Sword: Melee, 1d6+1 phy · ATK +0 · Difficulty 12 · HP 2 · Stress 1 · Thresholds 7/none
Battle guide: roll d20 (no ATK mod) vs Evasion; hit → 1d6+1. Take 6 or less damage → mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated.
Group Attack (Feature): spend a Fear, move several skeletons into Melee, one shared attack roll at +0; on success deal 4 phy per skeleton, combined into one hit.
Soul-Audit Wraith — Tier 1 Bruiser (×2)
Lifedrain: Far, 2d6+8 mag · ATK +3 · Difficulty 13 · HP 6 · Stress 3 · Major 7 / Severe 14
Spectral Body (Passive): resistance to physical damage (incoming physical halved, round up).
Memory Delve (Action): attack a Close target; on hit, the wraith places a hand on their cheek — ask the player to describe a terrifying childhood moment — then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through (Action): spend a Fear, attack a Melee target; on success the PC is Untethered (can't act until the countdown ticks down). Whole party Untethered at once → all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition cleared.
Open Vale Site — Environment, Tier 1 Exploration
Feature Market Correction (Action): spend a Fear to summon 2 Legacy Skeletons within Very Close of a PC.
GM guidance (p.35): if the countdown stalls, use Market Correction to spawn easy skeletons. If no PC is in range, adversaries target the Custodian (Difficulty 11, narrative damage only). Death move (Quickstart): a PC at last HP falls unconscious until healed or the danger passes — not dead.
transitions: Skeleton pressure escalates -> MAP-COMBAT-S05-05 / S05-05.
ritual_countdown=0 -> S05-06, then S05-07.

slides.gmGoal: The climax. A perfect circular clearing — the only break in the canopy — where the Custodian first forged Hush's ward pillars. sensorySummary: Standing stones ring wet grass and ward grooves; old runes and newer markers disagree about what the clearing is for.
The wind falls away near the center, ward-light ticks in stone seams, and every voice comes back slightly lower.
Cold mineral air, wet grass, stone dust, whitefire ozone, and the faint sweetness of crushed clover under lightning.

Animals avoid the center but circle the edge. The clearing is not dead; it is bracing for work.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The climax. A perfect circular clearing — the only break in the canopy — where the Custodian first forged Hush's ward pillars. The party takes a Short Rest, then defends her through the ward-renewal ritual against waves of skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths while a countdown die ticks. Win condition: survive until the ritual completes, not "kill everything."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: On the Custodian's direction, your carriage rolls into a clearing — a perfect circle, the only patch of the preserve where no trees block the open sky. Stars wheel overhead. This is the Open Vale Site. The Custodian's voice softens as she tells you she forged Hush's ward pillars here, on all four corners of the village — and that she nearly died doing it. She won't say more; something about angering the Forgotten Gods. Then her antennae perk in a way that unsettles you. "This is good. Stop, stop. Yes, here. Now come help me, I'm old." Her body begins to glow, flickering against the dark.

sensoryStack.detail: A flawless circular clearing, open sky (rare here), the Custodian glowing brighter and lifting the carriage a foot off the ground, eyes rolling back; later, skeletons clawing up from the earth and wraiths drifting in from the treeline.
The Custodian humming, then a shriek when the Keystone responds; unearthly screeches from the woods; rusted swords scraping free of the soil.
ozone, turned earth, cold air with no forest-damp — the clearing feels outside the preserve.
Charged, electric; the hair-raising sense of big magic; the open sky disorienting after days under canopy.
The Forgotten-Gods unease; the woods themselves seem to react to the arcane energy.

locationSlideModel.combatBlock:
The ritual countdown (p.35): Set a d8 to 8. Ticks down 1 each time an adversary is defeated; ticks up 1 each time the Custodian is hit. At 0, the ritual completes → Epilogue.
Setup (p.35): Custodian standee center; PCs around her; 4 Legacy Skeletons in Close range of her; 2 Soul-Audit Wraiths in Far range.
Legacy Skeleton — Tier 1 Standard (×4)
Rusted Sword: Melee, 1d6+1 phy · ATK +0 · Difficulty 12 · HP 2 · Stress 1 · Thresholds 7/none
Battle guide: roll d20 (no ATK mod) vs Evasion; hit → 1d6+1. Take 6 or less damage → mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated.
Group Attack (Feature): spend a Fear, move several skeletons into Melee, one shared attack roll at +0; on success deal 4 phy per skeleton, combined into one hit.
Soul-Audit Wraith — Tier 1 Bruiser (×2)
Lifedrain: Far, 2d6+8 mag · ATK +3 · Difficulty 13 · HP 6 · Stress 3 · Major 7 / Severe 14
Spectral Body (Passive): resistance to physical damage (incoming physical halved, round up).
Memory Delve (Action): attack a Close target; on hit, the wraith places a hand on their cheek — ask the player to describe a terrifying childhood moment — then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through (Action): spend a Fear, attack a Melee target; on success the PC is Untethered (can't act until the countdown ticks down). Whole party Untethered at once → all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition cleared.
Open Vale Site — Environment, Tier 1 Exploration
Feature Market Correction (Action): spend a Fear to summon 2 Legacy Skeletons within Very Close of a PC.
GM guidance (p.35): if the countdown stalls, use Market Correction to spawn easy skeletons. If no PC is in range, adversaries target the Custodian (Difficulty 11, narrative damage only). Death move (Quickstart): a PC at last HP falls unconscious until healed or the danger passes — not dead.
transitions: In: From the Treehouse (05), Act Five.
Out: Countdown hits 0 → ritual completes → the Keystone Asset epilogue (see 07 for the sequel hook).

slides.title: The Ritual Begins
slides.alt: Short Rest Before the Storm scene art for The Ward Renewal.
slides.caption: The ritual becomes visible pressure: protect the Custodian and drive the countdown to zero.
slides.gmGoal: Start the ritual, show the first threats, and put the countdown die on the table.
slides.publicObjective: Begin the defense and understand the countdown.
slides.readAloud: The Custodian lets out a shrill cry. "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway! Hurry!" Her glow swells, her eyes roll back, and the carriage lifts a foot off the ground. From the woods comes a chorus of unearthly screeches. The ground rumbles. Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up. In the distance, two shapes drift toward you, screeching, wrong. Hold the line until she's done.
gmNotes: Market Correction is available as a GM pressure valve, not player-facing terminology.
slides.gmScript: Say: "d8, starting at 8. Defeat an enemy or remove a real pressure, it ticks down one. She gets hit or exposed, it ticks up one. At zero, the ritual is done and you win. The math is simple; staying alive is not."
gmReadAloud: "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway!"
The carriage lifts a foot off the ground.
Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up.
Two shapes drift in the distance, screeching, wrong.
gmChecklist: Place Custodian center, PCs around her, 4 rusted-sword skeletons Close, and 2 screeching wraiths Far.
Set ritual_countdown=8.
If ward_stability=stable, soften the first exposure or give a prepared defense a free success beat; if fragile or missing, full canon pressure.
If ritual_prep=ready, let the prepared PC explain the countdown in character.
Initialize protected_whom as unresolved and start watching who covers whom.
gmPrivate: Use description before names: rusted-sword dead, floating screeching wraiths. Names and deeper meaning can come after the table understands what they see.
slides.playerTakeaway: This is the fight that ends the story: keep her safe and run the clock down.
slides.storyTakeaway: The ritual is live and irreversible now; the only way out is through.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: The countdown die is the win condition: d8 starts at 8, down on enemy defeat or pressure removed, up when the Custodian is hit.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: The rest becomes bookkeeping instead of care before danger. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Soul-Quiet Charm, Firstmoss Poultice.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rollCards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rollCards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Ask who helps someone else without making a big deal of it.
rollCards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the Difficulty, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

block1.game_role: Trust gate, ritual guide, and person the party can protect without owning.
block1.critical_info: The Custodian must carry the reveal; Marlowe can only add recognition, not replace her.
block1.disposition_default: Dry, tired, luminous, and warmer when treated as a person.
block1.the_lever: Respect her name, her consent, and the cost she has already paid.

block2.wants_now: Renew the ward without being treated as a device.
block2.larger_motivation: Keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember safety can be care instead of product.
block2.wants: Renew the ward without being treated as a device.
block2.motivation: Keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember safety can be care instead of product.
block2.personality: Ancient kindness running on fumes, glowing a little brighter whenever someone tells the truth nearby. Wants to keep one place honestly safe long enough for people to remember that safety can be care instead of a product, and is quietly breaking under the cost of it.
voice: Please do not call me the ward interface.
A contract can move a package. It cannot decide what a life is worth.
If you are here to help, stand where help costs you something.
block2.secrets: The ward's cost is personal, and the deepest economy behind that cost is worse than she will say unless trust and understanding are earned.
block2.fears: The stone waking hungry, the Relay failing, and being remembered as infrastructure instead of a person.

likes_dislikes.likes: Names spoken carefully, consent, patience, and brave people who admit fear.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Being called an interface, rushed rituals, and corporate ownership language.

block2.likes: Names spoken carefully, consent, patience, and brave people who admit fear.
block2.dislikes: Being called an interface, rushed rituals, and corporate ownership language.
block2.favorite_thing: A tiny bell charm she rings once when a ward line steadies.
block2.loved_ones: Other keepers, mostly gone or distant; the Relay Keeper matters as a person, not a destination.
block2.day_to_day: Tends failing ward threads, trims light from old knots, speaks to quiet bells, and sleeps only when the ward hum changes.
block2.appearance: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest. Full-body reference: Full-body tall luminous faerie custodian, wings folded, warm gold-green glow under translucent skin, gentle commanding presence, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Ancient and materially spare; the beauty around her is duty, not luxury.
block2.animal_companion: No animal; moths and fireflies gather around her light like worried attendants.
block2.physical: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A tall luminous faerie custodian stands like living bark and white fire, branchlike crown, translucent wings, and warm gold light gathered in the chest.
block2.voice_style: Luminous and weary; speaks in slow, true sentences and flinches at being called equipment.
block2.body_language: Ancient gentleness held upright by duty.
block2.quirks: Answers transactional questions with questions about fear, memory, or cost.
block2.image_lore: The branch-crown grew after the Custodian chose to stay with the ward instead of leaving with the old keepers. It blooms brighter when someone tells the truth without advantage.
block2.npc_relationships: She can care for every PC; Marlowe only gets a recognition beat, never ownership of the reveal.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She expects contractors to ask what the ward does before asking what it costs her.

story.statement: The ritual is live and irreversible now; the only way out is through.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: The countdown die is the win condition: d8 starts at 8, down on enemy defeat or pressure removed, up when the Custodian is hit.

mechanic.ask: "ward_stability stable means a kinder opening; fragile or missing means full pressure. ritual_prep ready means someone can explain this before the first hit."
mechanic.deeper: Keep updates visual and verbal every tick.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Ritual Begins
playerSafeProjection.alt: Short Rest Before the Storm scene art for The Ward Renewal.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The ritual becomes visible pressure: protect the Custodian and drive the countdown to zero.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Begin the defense and understand the countdown.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian lets out a shrill cry. "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway! Hurry!" Her glow swells, her eyes roll back, and the carriage lifts a foot off the ground. From the woods comes a chorus of unearthly screeches. The ground rumbles. Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up. In the distance, two shapes drift toward you, screeching, wrong. Hold the line until she's done.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: The finale clock is teachable math.
gm_runtime_payload: Start the countdown at 8.
Defeat an adversary or neutralize meaningful pressure: -1.
Custodian hit or exposed: +1.
When it reaches 0, the ritual completes.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Make the finale win condition visible to the table.

slides.title: Holding the Line
slides.alt: The Ritual Begins scene art for The Ward Renewal.
slides.caption: Holding the line teaches that defeating pressure and protecting the center are the same victory.
slides.gmGoal: Run the rusted-sword skeleton wave as clear protection pressure and countdown progress.
slides.publicObjective: Defeat the rusted dead and keep the Custodian safe.
slides.readAloud: The skeletons come in a clatter of rust and bone: not clever, but endless, and all of them reaching for the glowing figure at the center. For every one you put down, the ritual's clock ticks a notch closer to done. But they keep clawing up out of the dirt, and the Custodian cannot defend herself. The line is yours to hold.
gmNotes: Skeletons are pressure and countdown fuel, not a slog. Keep them moving toward the Custodian.
slides.gmScript: Say: "They are not strong. They are persistent, and they want her, not you. Stand in the way. Every one you drop moves the countdown down by one."
gmReadAloud: The skeletons come in a clatter of rust and bone.
All of them reach for the glowing figure at the center.
The line is yours to hold.
gmChecklist: Use Legacy Skeleton stats: Difficulty 12, HP 2, Stress 1, ATK +0, Rusted Sword 1d6+1 physical.
Damage 6 or less marks 1 HP; above that defeats the skeleton.
Each defeat ticks ritual_countdown -1.
Spend Fear for Group Attack when skeletons cluster: one shared +0 roll, 4 physical per skeleton combined.
Track who body-blocks the Custodian as protected_whom seed.
gmPrivate: Name them Legacy Skeletons only after the table has the image. Corporate-asset undertone stays GM-side.
slides.playerTakeaway: Hold the perimeter; every skeleton you drop is a step toward the end.
slides.storyTakeaway: The first wave is beatable, but it never stops reaching for her.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Skeleton defeats tick the countdown down, but Group Attack spikes damage if the party lets them cluster.

block5.person_under_the_fight: Once a debt collector who took the job to save their own family from the ledger, and then could not stop collecting. The medallion was an employee badge; the name is scraped away so thoroughly that only the balance is still legible. Protection freely given, or a memory offered without a price, makes the shape flicker like it half-remembers being owed to someone too.

Peat, cold water, mushroom rot, and fog heavy enough to taste.
Roots are slick and soft at the edges; mud pulls at boots like a hand.
The forest is populated even when no NPC is present; silence, birds, insects, and tracks are actionable signals.

slides.title: The Soul-Audit Wraiths
slides.alt: Legacy Security Skeletons scene art for The Ward Renewal.
slides.caption: The wraiths make care and grounding as important as attacks.
slides.gmGoal: Escalate into wraith pressure where memory, vulnerability, and rescue become the emotional core.
slides.publicObjective: Survive the wraiths, protect each other, and keep the ritual on track.
slides.readAloud: The drifting things reach you, and they do not swing for your body. One presses a cold hand to a face and reaches inside, dredging up something buried. The other simply passes through a body like a door, and for a horrible moment a soul stands outside itself, unable to move, unable to act, while the fight roars on without them. These are worse than the dead. These ask questions you do not want to answer.
gmNotes: Use Pass-Through sparingly. Rescue and grounding should return players to action quickly.
slides.gmScript: Say: "These do not want your blood. They want your worst memory and your soul out of your body. If someone gets knocked loose, protecting and calling them back is the scene."
gmReadAloud: The drifting things reach you.
They do not swing for your body.
A cold hand reaches inside memory.
A soul can stand outside itself for one horrible moment.
gmChecklist: Use Soul-Audit Wraith stats: Difficulty 13, HP 6, Stress 3, ATK +3, Lifedrain Far 2d6+8 magic.
Physical resistance halves incoming physical damage, round up.
Memory Delve: Close attack; ask for a terrifying childhood moment, then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through: spend Fear, Melee attack; on hit target is Untethered until countdown ticks down.
Whole party Untethered at once: all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition clears.
Track protected_whom as the primary emotional write.
gmPrivate: Memory Delve hooks live in perCharacterLayer. Use the active PC's hook if helpful, but accept any player-safe version.
Soul-economy stays a seed. The word itself is GM-only.
slides.playerTakeaway: You cannot out-muscle these; protect each other, cover the Untethered, and endure.
slides.storyTakeaway: The wraiths attack who you are, not just what you can take.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Memory Delve, Vulnerable, Pass-Through, Untethered, and grounding an ally make care a live combat mechanic.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You cannot out-muscle these; protect each other, cover the Untethered, and endure.
player.say: "Shield each other. If someone gets knocked loose, hold the line around them until the clock frees them. Nobody fights these alone."

player.deeper: This scene should make protection emotional, not just spatial.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The wraiths attack who you are, not just what you can take.
story.say: "These do not want your blood. They want your worst memory and your soul out of your body."
story.ask: "If players ask what they are, describe floating soul-reaching wraiths first. Soul-Audit Wraith is the GM name after the image lands."
story.deeper: The audit meaning is GM-only; let behavior imply the deeper system.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Memory Delve, Vulnerable, Pass-Through, Untethered, and grounding an ally make care a live combat mechanic.
mechanic.say: "Far-range, hard hits, physical resistance. Memory Delve makes you Vulnerable. Pass-Through can make you Untethered until the countdown ticks down."
mechanic.ask: "Stats: Difficulty 13, HP 6, Stress 3, ATK +3, Lifedrain Far 2d6+8 magic, physical resistance. Whole party Untethered: all mark 2 HP and souls return."
mechanic.deeper: Do not bench players. Use Untethered to invite rescue and return them fast.

playerSafeProjection.alt: Legacy Security Skeletons scene art for The Ward Renewal.

playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Survive the wraiths, protect each other, and keep the ritual on track.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The drifting things reach you, and they do not swing for your body. One presses a cold hand to a face and reaches inside, dredging up something buried. The other simply passes through a body like a door, and for a horrible moment a soul stands outside itself, unable to move, unable to act, while the fight roars on without them. These are worse than the dead. These ask questions you do not want to answer.

slides.title: The Peak
slides.alt: Soul-Audit Wraiths scene art for The Ward Renewal.
slides.caption: The peak asks what the party saves when it cannot save everything cleanly.
slides.gmGoal: Run the peak HOLD/BREAK choice and let resource spends, protection, and sacrifice decide the outcome track.
slides.publicObjective: Survive the peak and drive the countdown home.
slides.readAloud: It all comes at once: the dead clawing up faster, the wraiths pressing in, the Custodian's glow guttering like a candle in wind. The clock is close, but so is disaster. Every choice now costs something: guard her and leave a friend exposed, or save the friend and let her take the hit that sets you all back. There is no clean way through. There is only what you are willing to give.
gmNotes: No PC is required to land the final blow. Let any meaningful action create the final tick if fiction supports it.
slides.gmScript: Say: "All-in time. Spend Hope, boons, big abilities, tag-team moments, and last good ideas. You cannot cover it all, so what you choose to save becomes the ending."
gmReadAloud: It all comes at once.
The Custodian's glow gutters like a candle in wind.
The clock is close, but so is disaster.
gmChecklist: Threaten the Custodian honestly.
Offer Death Move choices heroically if a PC marks their last HP: Blaze of Glory, Avoid Death, or Risk It All.
Use HOLD if she is protected and the party drives the countdown home cleanly.
Use BREAK if someone falls, she is hit badly, or the win is bought with a severe cost.
Seed ritual_outcome as clean, costly, or pyrrhic; finalize protected_whom.
gmPrivate: Custodian death remains a Kyle canon flag. Use dying only as a marked unresolved possibility unless ruled live.
slides.playerTakeaway: This is the moment you will remember: give everything, choose who you save, and finish it.
slides.storyTakeaway: You cannot save everything, so what you choose to save becomes the ending.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Peak play spends Hope, boons, tag-team actions, Death Moves, and final countdown ticks to write ritual_outcome and protected_whom.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: Soul-Audit Wraiths bear audit glyphs and say, "Unlicensed soul-resonance detected. Submit for audit."
A defeated wraith leaves a Soulspire compliance tag or coil-credit token instead of natural remains.
Wraiths ignore forest creatures and home only on ritual soul-magic.
A player can read the markings and name Soulspire without the GM naming it first.
Optional flag: Legacy Skeletons carry scraps of old corporate credentials.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Natural body for the protect-choice: Custodian, ally, or center at her own cost.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can step into the hardest pressure without becoming mandatory.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, this is the moment a guardian lives for. Who do you put yourself between?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Can spend Hope, Tag Team, or a big Warrior push to drop the threat menacing the Custodian.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can bring the clock home through decisive action.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, go all-in on the thing about to hit her. Want to end this?

perCharacterLayer.passive: A last big spell can clear field pressure or shield the Custodian.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Her choice mirrors duty versus people without gating victory.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, one big push left. Protect her, or protect the party? Your call says who you've become.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Can yank an Untethered or falling ally out of danger.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can make the save nobody sees coming.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, someone's about to fall. Want to be the reason they don't?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Can land a final ranged burst to defeat the last threat and tick the clock to 0.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can end pressure from the edge.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, one clean shot could end it. Want to take it?

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: This is the moment you will remember: give everything, choose who you save, and finish it.
player.say: "Whatever you have been saving, now. Decide who you stand in front of and bring the clock home."
player.ask: "Throw your best at the biggest threat, body-block the Custodian, spend a boon, or save the teammate about to fall. No wrong answer, only yours."
player.deeper: Make this a choice scene, not a math exercise.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: You cannot save everything, so what you choose to save becomes the ending.
story.say: "You cannot cover it all. What you sacrifice here is the story you will tell about tonight."
story.ask: "There is no hidden trick. The clock can be won; the question is at what cost."
story.deeper: HOLD/BREAK should be visible and emotionally fair.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Peak play spends Hope, boons, tag-team actions, Death Moves, and final countdown ticks to write ritual_outcome and protected_whom.
mechanic.say: "All-in time: spend Hope, festival boon, tag-team, class features. If someone hits last HP, Death Move is live and heroic."
mechanic.ask: "Every Custodian hit is +1; every defeat or true pressure removal is -1. Near the end, one choice can change clean to costly or costly to pyrrhic."
mechanic.deeper: No single PC owns the final tick. Any meaningful action can close the ritual if earned.

mapData.gmOrientation: Peak combat map for the hardest skeleton and protect-choice pressure. The Custodian is exposed, the countdown is close, and choices become ritual_outcome.
mapData.combatBlock: Legacy Skeleton x4 — Tier 1 Standard. Difficulty 12. Thresholds 7/none. HP 2. Stress 1. ATK +0. Rusted Sword Melee 1d6+1 physical. Defeat rule: take 6 or less damage -> mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated. Group Attack: spend Fear, move several skeletons into Melee of one target, one shared +0 roll vs Evasion, 4 physical per skeleton combined. Each skeleton defeated ticks ritual_countdown -1; each Custodian hit/exposure ticks +1.

slides.title: The Ward Renewed
slides.alt: Ward renewal light over the ritual clearing.
slides.caption: The ward renews, the field goes quiet, and the cost finally becomes visible.
slides.gmGoal: Resolve countdown zero, clear the field, and set ritual_outcome and custodian_fate.
slides.publicObjective: Finish the ritual; the ward is renewed.
slides.readAloud: As you land the blow that drops the last threat, the ritual ends. The carriage crashes back to earth and the Keystone blazes with arcane light. Then a soundless explosion erupts from the Custodian, washing outward, dissolving any enemy still standing. The screeching stops. The clawing stops. The clearing is quiet again, the open sky calm above you. It is done. The ward is renewed. You held the line, and a city you may never see will wake tomorrow still safe.
gmNotes: If custodian_fate=dying, mark it as a canon-sensitive result until Kyle rules whether she can die.
slides.gmScript: Say: "Clock at zero. Fight over. The blast clears whatever remains. You do not have to mop up. Breathe, then we count what it cost."
gmReadAloud: The carriage crashes back to earth.
The Keystone blazes with arcane light.
A soundless explosion washes outward.
The clearing is quiet again.
gmChecklist: End combat immediately when ritual_countdown reaches 0.
Clear remaining enemies with the ritual release.
Set ritual_outcome=clean, costly, or pyrrhic from S05-05.
Set custodian_fate=well, drained, or dying if Kyle/table canon allows.
Give a quiet breath before S05-07.
gmPrivate: The win is real. The cost is felt. Soul-economy stays dread, not exposition.
slides.playerTakeaway: You held long enough. It is over, and the ward is renewed.
slides.storyTakeaway: The city is safe tomorrow because the party held the line tonight.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: At countdown zero, combat ends immediately; ritual_outcome and custodian_fate carry the cost into the denouement.

voice: Please do not call me the ward interface.
A contract can move a package. It cannot decide what a life is worth.
If you are here to help, stand where help costs you something.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Ward Renewed
playerSafeProjection.alt: Ward renewal light over the ritual clearing.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The ward renews, the field goes quiet, and the cost finally becomes visible.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Finish the ritual; the ward is renewed.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: As you land the blow that drops the last threat, the ritual ends. The carriage crashes back to earth and the Keystone blazes with arcane light. Then a soundless explosion erupts from the Custodian, washing outward, dissolving any enemy still standing. The screeching stops. The clawing stops. The clearing is quiet again, the open sky calm above you. It is done. The ward is renewed. You held the line, and a city you may never see will wake tomorrow still safe.

mapData.combatBlock: Soul-Audit Wraith x2 — Tier 1 Bruiser. Difficulty 13. Thresholds 7/14. HP 6. Stress 3. ATK +3. Lifedrain Far 2d6+8 magic. Spectral Body: resistance to physical damage, half incoming physical rounded up. Memory Delve: Close attack; on hit, player describes a terrifying childhood memory -> 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest. Pass-Through: spend Fear, Melee attack; on hit the PC is Untethered and cannot act until countdown ticks down. Whole party Untethered: all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition clears. Death Move is live at last HP.

slides.title: Beyond the Contract
slides.alt: The Ward Locks Into Place scene art for The Ward Renewal.
slides.caption: The adventure ends with what truth the party chooses to carry forward.
slides.gmGoal: Honor the finale, run the report choice, and bridge to the Epilogue through report_choice.
slides.publicObjective: Wrap your story, decide how you report what happened, and learn what comes next.
slides.readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended over a rumbling hearth-fire. The Custodian, older now, exhaustion plain in her voice, folds herself into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." She lets you sit with it, the warmth and the weight both. And then, because there is always one more thing: she has a question about what you will tell the people who sent you, and a map to somewhere the light is going wrong.
gmNotes: The report choice is the satirical gut-punch: real heroism meets paperwork and future liability.
slides.gmScript: Say: "The fight is won. Now the real question: what do you put in the report? File honest, spin corporate, refuse to report, or withhold the truth. That choice decides the Epilogue tone."
gmReadAloud: The Keystone hangs over a rumbling hearth-fire.
The Custodian looks older now.
"You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone."
She asks what you will tell the people who sent you.
gmChecklist: Name protected_whom and honor the PC or group that covered the worst moment.
Name ritual_outcome and custodian_fate in the denouement tone.
Gate deeper truth: only keystone_understanding=deep + custodian_trust=high gets the strongest dread hint.
Offer report_choice: file-honest, spin-corporate, refuse, withhold-the-truth.
Set relay_hook_accepted if the party takes the Goldspire Relay hook.
Bridge S05-07 -> S06-* by report_choice.
gmPrivate: Truth-hint ladder low: the form has boxes for cost, blame, and recoverable asset, but no box for who was protected.
Truth-hint ladder medium: the Custodian flinches when lives, memories, or warmth are described as resources.

Truth-hint ladder high: only if keystone_understanding=deep and custodian_trust=high, say the frightening part is not that wards need power, but that someone learned how to profit from what protection consumes.
Do not fully explain soul-economy. Let players reach for the conclusion.
slides.playerTakeaway: You saved a city. Now decide what story you tell about it, and whether you answer the next call.
slides.storyTakeaway: The adventure ends not with the fight, but with who gets to own the truth of what happened.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: report_choice gates the Epilogue, while ritual_outcome, protected_whom, custodian_fate, and relay_hook_accepted carry the finale forward.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You saved a city. Now decide what story you tell about it, and whether you answer the next call.
player.say: "Heroes do not get a clean ending here; they get a form to fill out. What do you write? And do you take the next job?"
player.ask: "Say goodbye to the Custodian, ask what you have been holding, choose the report, and decide whether the Relay hook stays open."
player.deeper: Let players talk. This is the final agency beat.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The adventure ends not with the fight, but with who gets to own the truth of what happened.
story.say: "The fight is won. Now the real question is what story leaves this clearing, and who that story protects."
story.ask: "If they understand the cost, the report is moral pressure. If they do not, it is still how they frame a job well done."
story.deeper: Report choice is the story thesis; do not reduce it to bookkeeping.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: report_choice gates the Epilogue, while ritual_outcome, protected_whom, custodian_fate, and relay_hook_accepted carry the finale forward.
mechanic.say: "Set report_choice now: file-honest, spin-corporate, refuse, or withhold-the-truth. Then set whether they accept the Relay hook."
mechanic.ask: "file-honest risks retaliation, spin-corporate buys safety with complicity, refuse breaks the frame, withhold-the-truth has the largest future fallout."
mechanic.deeper: Exact long-tail branch consequences remain Kyle-adjudicated; the options are implemented as GM-selectable state now.

playerSafeProjection.title: Beyond the Contract
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Ward Locks Into Place scene art for The Ward Renewal.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The adventure ends with what truth the party chooses to carry forward.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Wrap your story, decide how you report what happened, and learn what comes next.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended over a rumbling hearth-fire. The Custodian, older now, exhaustion plain in her voice, folds herself into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." She lets you sit with it, the warmth and the weight both. And then, because there is always one more thing: she has a question about what you will tell the people who sent you, and a map to somewhere the light is going wrong.

slides.title: Epilogue: Beyond the Contract
slides.caption: The screeching is gone. The clearing is quiet, the open sky calm. Somewhere west, a city you may never see is waking up safe because of what you did tonight.
slides.gmGoal: Land the plane: reward the heroes, let the table breathe, then leave one official door and one optional hidden door open.
slides.publicObjective: Rest, reckon with what you did, and decide what you carry forward.
slides.readAloud: The screeching is gone. The clearing is quiet, the open sky calm. Somewhere west, a city you may never see is waking up safe because of what you did tonight. The Custodian is already shuffling you back toward warmth and food and a fire that does not want anything from you. For the first time since the road, there is nothing chasing you. You won. Sit with that a while.

slides.title: Back in the Hanging Office
slides.alt: Back in the Hanging Office scene art for Beyond the Contract.
slides.caption: Back at the Hanging Office, the party can see how the contract changed them.
slides.gmGoal: The Keystone rests above the hearth while the Custodian thanks the party.
slides.publicObjective: Rest, receive your due, and reckon with the choice you made.
slides.readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire, glowing soft and settled. The Custodian, older now, the night's work plain in her voice, folds into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." There is hot food, a warm bath waiting, and for the first time in days, nowhere you need to be. She looks at each of you like she is memorizing you. "Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."
gmNotes: Use triumphant, bittersweet, pyrrhic, or tragic tone from ritual_outcome and custodian_fate.
If package_status=lost somehow reached here, frame this as an alternate close and flag the normal reward text as changed.
slides.gmScript: Say: "This is the good part. The fire, the food, the old faerie who is alive because of you. Level up, collect what you earned, and let the report choice sit in the room."
gmReadAloud: The Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire.
The Custodian looks older, exhausted, and deeply grateful.
"Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."
gmChecklist: Grant level-up.
Distribute pay, goodwill, and the Custodian's parting gift.
Name protected_whom and ritual_outcome in plain emotional language.
Deliver report_choice payoff: honest, spin, refuse, or withhold.
Set rewards_granted and epilogue_tone.
Drop only one hidden seed if the table asks the right question.
gmPrivate: Reward first. The hidden thesis has not earned space until the players feel the win.
If custodian_trust is high, the Custodian can almost say: the ward does not make safety from nothing. Stop there.
Do not explain the soul-cost. Let it remain a seed.
slides.playerTakeaway: You are heroes tonight: take the reward, take the level, and take the moment with the person you saved.
slides.storyTakeaway: You saved something real, and the person you saved wants to thank you.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: Level-up, rewards_granted, epilogue_tone, and report_choice payoff resolve the one-shot's consequences.

playerSafeProjection.alt: Back in the Hanging Office scene art for Beyond the Contract.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire, glowing soft and settled. The Custodian, older now, the night's work plain in her voice, folds into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." There is hot food, a warm bath waiting, and for the first time in days, nowhere you need to be. She looks at each of you like she is memorizing you. "Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."

slides.title: The Relay Spire Hook
slides.alt: The Relay Spire Hook scene art for Beyond the Contract.
slides.caption: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending.
slides.gmGoal: The Custodian reveals another relay spire may be failing.
slides.publicObjective: Learn what is stirring west, and decide whether you leave that door open.
slides.readAloud: The Custodian leads you out of the treehouse, out of the forest itself, to look down on the green expanse from above. Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering in its tower like a beacon. "There's a relay out west," she says, "maybe a few hours. You might have felt it on the way in: its light was weaker than it should be. I think something's wrong with its Keeper, and I fear what happens if that fire goes out." She studies the horizon. "When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map, so you can make it there safe. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."
gmNotes: The Relay is seen and described, not entered.
If epilogue_tone is pyrrhic or tragic, the hook feels like unfinished business rather than excitement.
slides.gmScript: Say: "One more thing on the horizon. Not tonight unless you want it tonight: a fire going dim, a Keeper in trouble, and a map waiting if you ever come back."
gmReadAloud: Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering like a beacon.
"There's a relay out west," she says. "Its light was weaker than it should be."
"When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map."
gmChecklist: Deliver official Relay hook player-facing.
Offer the map as a future door, not a forced next scene.
Drop 0-4 hidden hints only if earned and the players bite.
Let players say the conclusion; do not lecture.
Set relay_hook_accepted, hidden_hook_discovered, and sequel_direction.
End open-ended. No combat, no countdown, no next act transition.
gmPrivate: Hidden thesis: the corporation manufactures the peril it profits from protecting against.
The official hook and hidden hook point to the same future destination, but the table only gets the hidden conclusion if they articulate it.

Hint ladder: convenient Relay failure; the Custodian almost saying safety is not made from nothing; Bramble truth if learned; staged attack/defensive monster/trademarked havens/assets pattern if they connect it.
Hold the soul-economy as a seed. Do not explain the mechanism.
slides.playerTakeaway: You can rest easy tonight, and if you want, a door west is open.
slides.storyTakeaway: The night's won, but a distant light is failing and the party may be the kind of people who answer.
slides.mechanicTakeaway: relay_hook_accepted, hidden_hook_discovered, and sequel_direction record which ending door the table leaves open.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You can rest easy tonight, and if you want, a door west is open.
player.say: "You are done for tonight, heroes. The door west is open whenever you want it."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The night's won, but a distant light is failing and the party may be the kind of people who answer.
story.say: "One more thing on the horizon: a fire going dim, a Keeper in trouble. Not tonight, but it is there."
story.ask: "The Relay is a beacon-spire west. Its light is failing, and the Keeper may be in danger."
story.deeper: The official hook is player-safe and clear. The hidden hook is only a clue chain unless players connect it.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway

mechanic.ask: "Set relay_hook_accepted if they take the map. Set hidden_hook_discovered only if they name the pattern. Set sequel_direction from the door they choose."
mechanic.deeper: No combat or countdown. The last mechanic is choice.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Relay Spire Hook
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Relay Spire Hook scene art for Beyond the Contract.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Learn what is stirring west, and decide whether you leave that door open.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian leads you out of the treehouse, out of the forest itself, to look down on the green expanse from above. Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering in its tower like a beacon. "There's a relay out west," she says, "maybe a few hours. You might have felt it on the way in: its light was weaker than it should be. I think something's wrong with its Keeper, and I fear what happens if that fire goes out." She studies the horizon. "When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map, so you can make it there safe. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The closer. After the ritual, back in the treehouse, the Custodian thanks the party and plants the next adventure: a Goldspire Relay spire to the west whose beacon-flame is weakening, with something wrong about its Relay Keeper. This is denouement + sequel bait, not a playable location yet. Keep it evocative and unresolved.
locationSlideModel.readAloud: We pull out of the Custodian's home, out of the forest itself, to see the verdant expanse from above — and there, breaking through the treeline, twisting stone spires, each with a flame flickering inside it like a beacon. The Custodian's voice follows you up: "There's a Goldspire Relay, just west of here. You may have felt it on the way to the ritual — its power was strange. The light felt weaker than it should be. I think something might be terribly wrong with the Relay Keeper, and I fear what will happen if its fire is extinguished altogether. When you're ready, come back, and I'll give you my map so you can make it there safely. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

entities.name: The Titan's Steps
entities.summary: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
entities.role: Make vertical logistics feel lived in, not decorative.
entities.personality: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.; introduce it with a sensory palette, who feels safe there, and what has been neglected.
entities.wants: Pull player attention toward the choices, clues, and relationships tied to The Sable Sinecure, Helena Corain, Mountain Crabs.
entities.sampleLine: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.

entities.name: Mountain Crabs
entities.summary: Granite-shelled cliff crabs with moss and alpine flowers growing on their backs, stone-heavy claws, many gripping legs, and wary eyes made for vertical roads.
entities.role: Crab-shell resource and climbing-route pressure
entities.personality: Grumpy granite tenants of the cliff with gardens growing on their own backs. Not malicious, just enormous and territorial on a road where one bad step is the last. They were here long before the climbing route and resent the traffic.
entities.wants: To be left to the cliff and the moss on their shells, and to keep the warm crevices they have always nested in.
entities.sampleLine: A deep grinding click you feel in the stone before you hear it.

entities.name: Fire-Falcons
entities.summary: Sleek ember-orange falcons with coal-black wing tips and feather edges like banked fire, beautiful enough for prestige and sharp enough to make a cache feel watched.
entities.role: Violent light-bearing Sable Sinecure companion birds
entities.personality: Beauty bred into a weapon. Banked-fire feathers the wealthy buy for spectacle and the Sinecure trains for harm. Loyal to whoever feeds them, sharp to everyone else, and aware, somewhere, that they are admired far more than they are loved.
entities.wants: To hunt, to be fed by a steady hand, and to keep the high perch they have claimed.
entities.sampleLine: A bright scaling shriek that turns every head across a market.

slides.title: GM Rules Reference
slides.caption: Full in-session rules reference. Mechanic names link to their wiki entry; hover for a quick card.
slides.gmGoal: Find any rule fast without leaving Run Mode.
gmNotes: Roll in 10 Seconds: Use this when a player asks what to roll.
• Pick the trait that matches the approach.
• Set the Difficulty before the roll matters.
• State the stakes.
• Roll Hope d12 + Fear d12.
• Add trait, Experience, and bonuses.
• Compare total to Difficulty.
Action Roll Results: Read total first, then Hope/Fear spin.
• Critical Success: best outcome, gain Hope, clear 1 Stress.
• Success with Hope: they get it and gain Hope.
• Success with Fear: they get it, but cost or pressure enters.
• Failure with Hope: they miss, but gain Hope and a useful thread.
• Failure with Fear: they miss and the GM makes a stronger move.
Difficulty Ladder: Beginner hinges often sit around 10-14.
• Very Easy 5.
• Easy 10.
• Average 15.
• Hard 20.
• Very Hard 25.
• Nearly Impossible 30.
Six Traits: Translate the fictional approach, not the D&D skill name.
• Agility: sprint, leap, maneuver.
• Strength: lift, smash, grapple.
• Finesse: control, hide, tinker.
• Instinct: perceive, sense, navigate.
• Presence: charm, perform, deceive.
• Knowledge: recall, analyze, comprehend.
D&D to Daggerheart: Convert the instinct quickly, then move on.
• Perception -> Instinct.
• Saving throw/save -> Reaction Roll.
• AC -> Evasion.
• Initiative -> Spotlight flow.
• Skill check -> Action Roll.
Hope Spend Menu: Give players fast ways to help themselves and each other.
• Help an Ally.
• Use an Experience.
• Tag Team Roll.
• Use a Hope Feature.
Fear Spend Menu: Spend Fear to escalate what the fiction already set up.
• Make or interrupt with a GM move.
• Make an extra move when pressure justifies it.
• Spotlight an additional adversary.
• Use an adversary or environment Fear feature.
• Add an adversary Experience when the stat block supports it.
Combat / Spotlight Loop: No initiative list; pass spotlight through the fiction.
• Spotlight follows immediate fictional pressure.
• PC action roll targets adversary Difficulty.
• Adversary attack: d20 + ATK vs PC Evasion.
• GM acts on failures, rolls with Fear, and Fear spends.
Damage / Armor / Stress: Compare damage to thresholds; do not improvise a condition.
• Compare damage to the target's thresholds.
• Mark HP by damage severity.
• Mark an Armor Slot to reduce severity by one threshold.
• If Stress maxes, the PC becomes Vulnerable until at least 1 Stress clears.
• Last HP points to the Death Move / quickstart handling.
Official Conditions: Only these global conditions belong in the Atlas.
• Hidden.
• Restrained.
• Vulnerable.
Short Rest: Use before Open Vale pressure spikes.
• Tend to Wounds.
• Clear Stress.
• Repair Armor.
• Prepare.

rules.title: Action Roll
rules.summary: Roll when a PC does something uncertain and consequences matter.
rules.when: Use for proactive PC action under pressure.
rules.not_when: Do not roll when success is obvious or failure would not change anything.
rules.question: What do I roll?
rules.answer: Tell me what you do, then we choose the trait that fits.
rules.example: Searching Tamsin's cart is an Action Roll because the result changes what the party learns.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

mechanic_profile.what_it_is: Roll when a PC does something uncertain and consequences matter.
mechanic_profile.why_it_matters: Tell me what you do, then we choose the trait that fits.
mechanic_profile.how_it_functions: Use for proactive PC action under pressure.
mechanic_profile.template: When a PC tries something uncertain and meaningful, choose a trait, set Difficulty, roll Hope d12 + Fear d12, add bonuses, compare total, then read Hope/Fear spin.
step_by_step: Player states the action in the fiction.
GM names the trait that best matches the method and the Difficulty.
Player rolls Hope d12 + Fear d12 and adds trait, Experience, or advantage/disadvantage.
Compare total to Difficulty, then resolve the Hope/Fear or critical result.

rules.title: Reaction Roll
rules.summary: A roll to react to danger or pressure rather than initiate action.
rules.when: Use when the GM calls for a response to sudden danger.
rules.not_when: Do not use as a default defense roll against every attack.
rules.question: Is this a saving throw?
rules.answer: Usually yes: if you mean a D&D save, look for a Reaction Roll.
rules.example: Dodging a sudden falling branch can be a Reaction Roll.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Duality Dice
rules.summary: Roll a Hope d12 and Fear d12 together, add modifiers, compare to Difficulty.
rules.when: Use for Action Rolls and most player-facing uncertain rolls.
rules.not_when: Do not replace this with a custom dice mode in official beginner play.
rules.question: Why are there two d12s?
rules.answer: One sets the total with the other; the higher die colors the result with Hope or Fear.
rules.example: A 10 Fear die plus 5 Hope die with +2 Instinct is 17 with Fear.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

mechanic_profile.why_it_matters: One sets the total with the other; the higher die colors the result with Hope or Fear.
mechanic_profile.how_it_functions: The two d12s are rolled together. Their sum plus bonuses determines success against Difficulty. The higher die says whether the result is with Hope or with Fear. Matching dice are a Critical Success.
mechanic_profile.p2p_note: This module uses only the official two-d12 Hope/Fear roll.

rules.title: Five Roll Outcomes
rules.summary: Every action roll resolves into one of five table results: critical success, success with Hope, success with Fear, failure with Hope, or failure with Fear.
rules.when: Use after every Action Roll or Reaction Roll where the Hope/Fear spin matters.
rules.not_when: Do not flatten rolls into pass/fail when the spin should change cost, benefit, or GM pressure.
rules.question: What does my result mean?
rules.answer: First compare the total to Difficulty. Then read Hope, Fear, or matching dice to choose the exact result.
rules.example: A Presence 12 strixwolf approach that succeeds with Fear calms the mother but lets the GM add pressure from the pack or the woods.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

mechanic_profile.template: Critical Success; Success with Hope; Success with Fear; Failure with Hope; Failure with Fear.
step_by_step: Check doubles first for Critical Success.
If not a critical, compare total to Difficulty.
At or above Difficulty succeeds; below Difficulty fails.
Hope spin gives Hope and a cleaner/kinder edge; Fear spin gives the GM Fear and a cost or complication.

rules.title: Connection Questions
rules.summary: Daggerheart-style prompts that let players define safe, playable relationships before the first scene.
rules.when: Use during Session Zero, character introductions, and optional party-bond refresh beats.
rules.not_when: Do not force a player to accept another player's premise; the answer can accept, alter, soften, or pass.
rules.question: What does a connection answer look like?
rules.answer: Offer one relationship prompt, then let the other player answer in their own words and keep only the part both players like.
rules.example: Varian asks, 'You saw me freeze once. What did you do?' The other player answers with a small memory the table can use later.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Ancestry
rules.summary: A character's people/species choice and its official feature package.
rules.when: Use at character creation and when ancestry fiction clearly explains how a PC perceives or approaches a moment.
rules.not_when: Do not invent a mechanical bonus because a species detail sounds useful; use advantage or a lower Difficulty only when Kyle chooses that adaptation.
rules.question: Does ancestry change rolls?
rules.answer: Use the printed ancestry feature. For scene flavor, give a distinct clue angle without changing math unless the table grants advantage or adjusts Difficulty.
rules.example: A Katari ranger may smell mineral wrongness in a package clue, but the roll is still Instinct unless a feature says otherwise.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Community
rules.summary: A character's social origin and the official feature tied to that origin.
rules.when: Use at character creation and when a PC's upbringing explains what they know, fear, or notice.
rules.not_when: Do not make community the only path to a clue; it should add texture or a cleaner route.
rules.question: What does community do?
rules.answer: Use the printed community feature and let the background shape how the same clue is discovered.
rules.example: A Highborne PC may recognize legal polish in a contract faster; an Underborne PC may notice who is absent from the paperwork.

rules.title: Damage Rolls
rules.summary: After a successful attack, roll the listed weapon, spell, or adversary damage dice and compare the total to thresholds when needed.
rules.when: Use after a hit or when a feature calls for damage.
rules.not_when: Do not roll damage before confirming the attack hit or before checking whether a non-damage outcome ended the danger.
rules.question: When do I roll damage?
rules.answer: After the attack succeeds. Roll the listed damage, then compare it to the target's thresholds or stat block instructions.
rules.example: If a skeleton hits, roll its listed damage; if a PC hits, use the weapon or spell on their sheet.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Long Rest
rules.summary: A deeper downtime recovery and reset structure used when the story has enough time.
rules.when: Use between adventures or when a sequel session gives the party real downtime.
rules.not_when: Do not use during the one-shot climax unless the fiction actually grants extended safety.
rules.question: Do we long rest?
rules.answer: Not during immediate danger. Use short rest inside the one-shot; save long rest for between-session recovery or continuation play.
rules.example: After the epilogue, a future campaign could begin after a long rest and level-up decisions.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Disposition / Resolution Track
rules.summary: A module-facing tracker for how a creature, NPC group, or faction leaves a scene: helped, calmed, fought, captured, spared, or harmed.
rules.when: Use for Strixwolf and Bramble-style outcomes that should ripple later.
rules.not_when: Do not turn it into a mandatory plot lock; it records consequence, not a required solution.
rules.question: What are we tracking?
rules.answer: Track what the table actually did and how the affected side now feels about them.
rules.example: The Strixwolf instance records whether the party calmed, fed, fought, or frightened the mother; the Bramble instance records parley, mercy, violence, or capture.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: NPC / Community Trust Track
rules.summary: A module-facing tracker for rapport with a person or settlement.
rules.when: Use when repeated choices change how warm, candid, generous, or guarded an NPC/community becomes.
rules.not_when: Do not make trust the only route to required information; low trust changes tone, cost, and available help.
rules.question: How does trust change play?
rules.answer: High trust makes help warmer and clearer. Low trust still lets play continue, but with distance, fewer gifts, or harder social positioning.
rules.example: Hush Trust changes how locals offer food, directions, and emotional buy-in. Custodian Trust changes how candid and tender the reveal feels.
rules.source: Official SRD / local quickstart reference. Use private full-rulebook material only at the table.

rules.title: Roll Slider
rules.summary: Kyle's optional degree-of-success overlay: the total says how far above or below Difficulty the result lands while Hope/Fear sets the spin.
rules.when: Use when a clue, negotiation, or set piece benefits from richer tiers than pass/fail.
rules.not_when: Do not replace official Daggerheart outcomes; keep 2d12 Hope/Fear as the baseline.
rules.question: What extra thing does the slider add?
rules.answer: It tells you how much they get: botch, miss, hit, clean, soar, or crit, while Hope/Fear still colors the result.
rules.example: At S01-03, Presence 12 with a high total may calm the strixwolf and reveal the corpse; the Fear spin can still call distant pack pressure.
